### Answering both questions directly

**Does the floor still plausibly drop?** Yes, but less confidently than my first pass — the
two-stage range now nearly overlaps the one-stage range at the top end (41.0 vs 45) where it
previously sat clearly below (36.4 vs 45). The direction is unchanged; the margin of expected
savings has narrowed, because stage 1 no longer gets a discount it was never entitled to.

**Does the failure-branch exposure shrink given the stage-1 checkpoint?** Yes, for the cost that
actually matters — **not the single-attempt hard ceiling** (384 core-h cumulative wall-clock per
endpoint is unchanged, a scheduler cap doesn't move), **but the expected cost of reaching a
converged answer across resubmissions**. A stage-2 `budget_exhausted` kill can now resume from
stage 1's saved geometry rather than restarting the whole endpoint from the guess: a retry re-pays
only stage 2 (4.9–30.4 core-h), not the full two-stage cost (7.5–41.0). This is the more
decision-relevant number for B0-F's actual expected spend, even though it does not change the
per-attempt worst-case figure already in §R38/§R38.10's flush block.

**Closed.** Nothing else in §R38's flush block moves: no convergence-rate prior, 302.4 as floor,
`[FIXTURE]`/`[UNVERIFIED PROVENANCE]`, unit-in-cell, production tier planned against the
with-nosymm branch — all unchanged, per the lead's explicit instruction.

# §R39 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: pricing U56-2 (§39.39(g)) and MTD (§39.40(g))

> **Abbreviations, first use in this section.** `U-56` = the open unknown *"transition state (TS)
> search success rate is unmeasured"*; split by §39.39 into `U-56a` (binary feasibility, the gate)
> and `U-56b` (per-attempt success fraction, a sizing input). `U56-1 / U56-2 / U56-3` = the three
> candidate gate instruments of §39.39(d). `B0` = the gate batch; `B0-D` = its solvation-cost arm;
> `B0-F` = its TS-method bake-off arm. `S3` = the pipeline stage that computes pathway + barrier
> per reaction. `R-A / R-B / R-C` = the three bake-off reactions of §39.26(d) (11 / 11 / 21 atoms).
> `MTD` = metadynamics. `GFN2-xTB` = Grimme's semiempirical tight-binding method (the vendored
> `xtb` binary, 6.7.1). `MD` = molecular dynamics. `IRC` = intrinsic reaction coordinate.
> `QST2` = Gaussian's synchronous-transit-guided quasi-Newton double-ended saddle search.
> `CalcFC` = compute the force constants (Hessian) at the first optimisation step.
> `PCM` = polarisable continuum model. `KNL` = Knights Landing, the cluster's compute-node
> architecture. `PBS` = the site's batch scheduler. `ADR-NNN` = decision record in
> `01_DECISION_LOG.md`. `[MEASURED] / [ESTIMATE] / [LITERATURE] / [FIXTURE]` = the four provenance
> tokens (§R38 flush block).

> **Every bare `core-h` below is RAW-KNL core-h**: cores-requested × wall-elapsed on the real
> cluster, 64-core convention (`select=1:ncpus=64`), **no κ applied**. This is §R38.4's convention
> and §39.39(g)'s explicit instruction. Reference core-h appears **only** in §R39.7, is labelled
> `ref core-h` in the same cell as the number, and always means raw-KNL ÷ κ. 🔴 The κ used there is
> **κ_physical = 2.4 [ESTIMATE]**, the standing operative planning value — **not** κ_thread = 1.218,
> which is a thread-scaling ratio and is not a KNL↔reference hardware ratio. Mixing the two is the

Wall: minutes. Run it **on 1 core**, not 64 — at 64 cores the `min_wall_h = 0.5` floor alone books
32 core-h of ceiling for a 7 core-h job. 🟢 proposer7's "minutes on one core" holds exactly.

🟢 **DUAL USE, and it is free money: the (d) 21-atom scan IS the T21-se attempt's relaxed scan.**
Same coordinate, same molecule, same engine. Running (d) first and keeping its trajectory removes
the scan stage from R-C's TS attempt at zero marginal cost, and removes a 203–5,346 core-h DFT scan
if the alternative was to scan at DFT. **Run (d) unconditionally and before everything else** —
it is 7 core-h, it can kill the entire MTD arm (F11), and it pre-pays a stage of the most expensive
item in R39.4.

🔴 **Two corrections to §39.40(g), both in the unfavourable direction.**

**1. Quench is NOT free, and it is NOT only a task-count problem.** §39.40(g) says *"cheap and
embarrassingly parallel; it is a task-count problem (ADR-107), not a core-h problem."* At 400
frames × 12 runs it is **960 core-h at base — 89% of the biased-MD arm and 47% of the whole
pilot.** It is both problems at once.
```
🟢 CHEAPER ALTERNATIVES, priced, pick one (this is a proposer7 science call, not mine):
  (i)  dump every 500 fs instead of 250 fs                       → quench 480 core-h, −50%
  (ii) quench-on-raw-graph-CHANGE, with a mandatory periodic     → quench 100-300 core-h, −70-90%
       quench every 5 ps as a backstop
       🔒 This does NOT violate §39.40(c)-3. That rule forbids CLASSIFYING on raw frames. Using a
       raw-frame graph change as a cheap TRIGGER for whether to quench is a different act: its only
       failure mode is a false negative (a reaction with no raw-graph change anywhere), and the
       5 ps backstop bounds that. Every classification still happens on a quenched structure.
  (iii) do nothing, pay 960 core-h. Also acceptable — it is 12% of U56-2's base total.
```

**2. The naive quench design is an ADR-107 landmine.** 4,800 one-frame tasks is an array of 4,800,
and `max_array_size` on this cluster is **null — never measured** (§R39.0). At the measured start
rate of 4.9 jobs/min that is **16.3 h of pure start latency** before any compute, and §R39.0's
queue-wait inversion means each of those single-node tasks also sits in the LONGEST wait class
(531 s vs 62 s for a 16-node job).
```
🟢 FIX, free: bundle 100 frames per PBS task ⟹ 48 tasks, not 4,800. Start latency 10 min, no
   dependence on an unmeasured max_array_size, and 48 is comfortably below the 200 the throughput
   probe DID accept. 🔒 Per-task write isolation still mandatory (Lustre arbitrates nothing).
```

## R39.6 Job structure — the design change that pays for itself

🔴 **Do not build a TS attempt as one PBS job.** R38.3 already found that P1.sh runs every stage
inside one walltime envelope; at 21 atoms that design fails on arithmetic alone:

```
T21-se as ONE job, base 5,074 core-h ⟹ wall 5,074/64 = 79.3 h > max_wall 48 h
                                     ⟹ links = ceil(5,074/3,072) = 2 ⟹ ceiling 6,144
🔒 And §R26.1's standing rule forbids chaining ARRAY tasks to escape this ("넘으면 링크를 늘리지
   말고 태스크를 쪼개라"). The stages are naturally sequential, so splitting is available for free.
```

🟢 **Recommended structure — 3 jobs per TS attempt** (a chain, like P1, not an array):
```
job 1  relaxed scan          GFN2, 1 core, minutes         — also serves §39.40(d)
job 2  ts_opt(CalcFC) + freq DFT, 64 cores, capped         — gated on job 1
job 3  irc_forward ∥ irc_reverse  DFT, 64 cores each, capped, SUBMITTED IN PARALLEL — gated on job 2
```
Three properties, all free:
1. **every job stays under the §R26.1 per-link ceiling (3,072)**, so links = 1 everywhere and the
   guard's `ceiling = Σ cores × clamp(b/cores, 2, 48) × links` arithmetic stays flat;
2. 🔴 **an attempt that fails at job 2 never pays for IRC.** IRC is 40% of an 11-atom attempt and
   49% of a 21-atom one. Given U-56 exists precisely because the TS-search success rate is
   unknown, this is the largest single expected-cost saving available and it costs nothing;
3. IRC forward and reverse are independent ⟹ parallel submission halves the attempt's worst-case
   wall-clock. (Same lever as R38.3's parallel endpoints; the calendar, not core-h, is what the
   5-month cap binds on.)

**Recommended wall caps (cumulative per job, across internal restarts — the R38.7 design condition,
which is what keeps the ceiling from tripling):**

| job | cores | wall cap | ceiling contribution (core-h) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GFN2 scan | 1 | 0.5 h (`min_wall_h` floor, §R27) | 0.5 |
| endpoint cert, 11 atoms | 64 | 6 h | 384 |
| **endpoint cert, 21 atoms** | 64 | **24 h** | **1,536** |
| `ts_opt`+`freq`, 11 atoms | 64 | 12 h | 768 |
| `ts_opt`+`freq`, 21 atoms | 64 | 24 h | 1,536 |
| IRC pair, 11 atoms (one job) | 64 | 12 h | 768 |
| IRC, 21 atoms (one job per direction) | 64 | 24 h each | 3,072 for the pair |
| QST2+freq+IRC, 11 atoms (R-A, as one chain like P1) | 64 | 24 h | 1,536 |

## §R39.13 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: MTD reprice after §39.40(d) returned. The run length is no longer an assumption I may make.

> **Abbreviations, first use in this subsection**: `MTD` = metadynamics; `(d)` / `(e)` = §39.40's
> free GFN2-xTB pre-check and its blind rediscovery pilot; `kpush` = xtb's `$metadyn` bias-strength
> parameter; `ν` = bias fill rate, i.e. how much bias potential (eV) the run deposits per ps;
> `B_req` = the bias a run must accumulate before the barrier is reachable; `kT` = thermal energy;
> `F11` = §39.40's falsifier "the pre-check finds no ring-opened GFN2 minimum".

### What arrived, and what it does to the price

```
[MEASURED, GFN2 pre-check §39.40(d), lead relay 2026-08-20]
  barrier/kT @ 400 K   14 (R-A, 11 atoms)  ⟹  0.483 eV
                       25 (R-C, 21 atoms)  ⟹  0.862 eV      (kT@400 K = 0.034475 eV)
  bias fill floor      B_req ≥ 0.5 eV (11 atoms) · ≥ 0.9 eV (21 atoms)
  F11                  DID NOT FIRE. The MTD arm survives. 🔒 F11 is now SPENT and may not be
                       re-used to justify the pilot (proposer7's own note).
[UNVERIFIED] 🔴 how xtb converts `kpush` into that accumulated fill. This is not a detail — it is
             the ONLY thing that sets the pilot's run length, and the run length is what the
             pilot's entire cost is linear in.
```

🟢 **First consequence, favourable and free: the matched-compute comparator ruling is now backed by
measurement, not only by pre-registration.** At 14–25 kT, 400 K plain MD cannot cross at any length
we would pay for, so the ADR-024 temperature ladder is the only admissible comparator. My §R39.5
"×2 for matched compute" assumption is unaffected in arithmetic and is now better grounded.

### 🔴 Second consequence, unfavourable: my 100 ps run length was an [ASSUMPTION] and it is now void as a point value

§R39.12 already flagged that 100 ps and 250 fs were §39.40(g)'s figures, that §39.40(e) fixes
neither, and that both costs are **linear** in them. The (d) result replaces the assumption with a
*requirement* — the run must last long enough to deposit B_req — and that requirement is a function
of the [UNVERIFIED] kpush→fill mapping. So the honest form of the estimate is a **cost function**,
not a number.

```
t_fill = B_req / ν                         ν = bias fill rate, eV/ps, [UNVERIFIED] for our binary
t_run  = f × t_fill,  f = 2 – 5            you must keep exploring AFTER the first crossing:
                                           §39.40(e)'s target list is T1–T4, not T1.
ν bracket used                             0.01 – 0.10 eV/ps  [ESTIMATE, LITERATURE-WEAK — inferred
                                           only from the published nanoreactor setting being
                                           designed to open rings on a 10–100 ps timescale. I have
                                           NOT read a primary that states ν, and this bracket is
                                           the widest single unknown now in either of my sections.]
⟹ t_fill (21 atoms, B_req 0.9 eV) = 9 – 90 ps
⟹ t_run                            = 18 – 450 ps        (vs the 100 ps I priced)
```

**Cost as a function of run length `t` (ps), 21 atoms, 3 seeds × 2 hyperparameter pairs = 6 runs,
matched comparator, quench every 250 fs. All raw-KNL core-h.**

```
total(t) =  9.96·t   (optimistic)   |   20.4·t  (base)   |   68.76·t  (pessimistic)
             ↑ MTD arm 5.16t + comparator (matched, = MTD arm) folded in + quench 4.8t
check: t = 100 reproduces §R39.5's 996 / 2,040 / 6,876 exactly.
```

| run length | optimistic | base | pessimistic |
|---|---|---|---|
| t = 18 ps (fast fill, f = 2) | **179** | 367 | 1,238 |
| t = 100 ps (§R39.5's figure, retained as base) | 996 | **2,040** | 6,876 |
| t = 450 ps (slow fill, f = 5) | 4,482 | 9,180 | **30,942** 🔴 |

🔴 **The joint pessimistic corner (slow bias fill × expensive MD) is 30,942 core-h — it breaches the
21,000/round guard on its own, before U56-2, P1b or P5 exist.** The spread is now 173×, far outside
the 3–5× band I am willing to call an estimate. **A run length is the wrong design parameter for
this pilot and I am withdrawing it as one.**

### 🟢 The fix — cap the pilot's COMPUTE, not its trajectory length

```
PRE-REGISTER   the pilot receives C raw-KNL core-h. The run length is WHATEVER C BUYS at the
               measured ν. "Matched compute" then becomes exact by construction rather than by
               a length coincidence, which is what §39.40(e) actually asked for.
RECOMMENDED    C = 2,000 – 3,000 raw-KNL core-h.
               C = 2,000 ⟹ t ≈ 98 ps at base · 201 ps optimistic · 29 ps pessimistic
               C = 3,000 ⟹ t ≈ 147 ps at base · 301 ps optimistic · 44 ps pessimistic
🔴 AND THE CLAUSE THAT PROTECTS THE PRE-REGISTRATION, which is the real point of this subsection:
   at the pessimistic corner the capped run may END BEFORE THE BIAS FILLS B_req. §39.40(e)'s
   REJECT criterion ("T1 not recovered in ≥2 of 3 seeds") would then fire on a run that never had
   a chance — recording a REJECTION of MTD when the finding is "we bought 29 ps and needed 90".
   ⟹ EVERY PILOT RUN MUST REPORT ITS ACCUMULATED BIAS AT END-OF-RUN, and:
        max accumulated bias < B_req   ⟹  verdict INDETERMINATE, never REJECT.
   🔒 Same shape as §39.40(e)'s existing INDETERMINATE clause for dissociation-dominated runs — a
   configuration fault, not a verdict on the method. Zero compute; a field and a comparison.
```

### 🟢 Cost-neutral improvement to the comparator, handed to proposer7 as a lever not a ruling

At 25 kT the temperature ladder's *lower* rungs are in the same position 400 K was: they will not
cross at any length C buys. Spreading matched compute across the whole ladder therefore spends part
of the comparator's budget on rungs whose result is knowable in advance. **Concentrating the
comparator's matched compute at the ladder's TOP rung costs exactly the same and produces a
strictly stronger comparator** — which is the direction §39.40(e) itself argues for ("a comparison
rigged in the new method's favour is worse than no comparison"). 🔒 Whether the ladder's top rung is
high enough at all is a chemistry question and proposer7's call; the cost of either choice is
identical, so this is free to adopt or refuse.

🔒 CORRECT VALUE: P5 ceiling = 3,128.   ❌ 4,238 is SUPERSEDED and must not be quoted again.

Two knock-on corrections I made while fixing it, because the same stale `min_wall_h` was in my

   MUST RUN ON A CHEAP ENGINE. A DFT 2-D scan at 21 atoms is not a thing this project can buy, in
   any round, under any cut. If the only admissible scan is a DFT scan, the single-ended method is

   run the 2-D GFN2 scan on R-C and check whether the minimum-energy path through the 2-D surface
   is SMOOTH once the translocation is given its own coordinate. If it is, the discontinuity was
   an artefact of projecting a 2-D reaction onto 1-D, and a guess taken from the 2-D path is not a
   guess taken at a discontinuity ⟹ dual use is restored for R-C in 2-D. If it is not smooth,
   proposer7's conclusion stands unweakened and the honest response is the one already on record

### 6. `p_min` — what I can derive, and the one input I do not own

proposer7 asked for `p_min` from the S3 sizing rule. **`p_min` is not a free-standing constant**:
it is `barriers_needed / attempts_affordable`, and I own only the denominator. What I can hand over
is the denominator, exactly, plus the map from any success-criterion to the `p` it implies.

```
DENOMINATOR I OWN   n = 2 (design B) or 3 (design A) production-class attempts per round.
                    n ≈ 13 for the 11-atom class (ceiling-limited, unchanged by this reprice).
🔴 PER SIZE CLASS, NEVER POOLED — proposer7 is right and the arithmetic is worse than stated: at
   3 production and ~13 small attempts a pooled p is 81% small-class BY BUDGET CONSTRUCTION. The
   weights would be set by the guard, not the chemistry. ADR-087's prohibition applies unchanged.
```

**`p_min` for the production class, by decision criterion** (exact binomial, computed here):

| criterion for S3 wave 1 | n = 3 (design A) | n = 2 (design B) |
|---|---|---|
| ≥1 barrier, more often than not (P ≥ 0.5) | **p ≥ 0.206** | p ≥ 0.293 |
| ≥1 barrier at 90% confidence | p ≥ 0.536 | p ≥ 0.684 |
| ≥2 barriers, more often than not | p ≥ 0.500 | — (impossible below p = 0.71) |

```
🟢 MY RECOMMENDED READING, offered as a default proposer7 may overrule: p_min = 0.206 for the
   production class under design A. It is the weakest criterion that still makes a wave MEAN
   something ("a wave of 3 yields at least one barrier more often than not"), and it is derived
   ENTIRELY from a guard ceiling I own plus one stated criterion — no chemistry assumption of mine
   is inside it.
🔴 AND THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER: §39.39(c)-2's own Clopper-Pearson argument
   applies to the futility rule too. At n = 3 the posterior on p is enormously wide — 0 of 3
   failures gives a 95% upper bound on p of 0.632. ⟹ **a wave-1 futility stop at n = 3 can only
   ever detect a catastrophically low p, never distinguish 0.2 from 0.5.** That is a property of
   the budget, not of the rule, and it should be pre-registered as one rather than discovered when
   the rule fails to fire. If the futility rule needs to separate 0.2 from 0.5, it needs n ≈ 15-20
   production attempts = 5-10 ROUNDS at design A, and that is a calendar decision for the lead and
   the user, not a rule I can tune.
```

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `stage 0` = §39.42's new first stage of the metadynamics (MTD)

> ensemble; `T1–T4` = §39.40(e)'s four sealed target reactions; `F13` = proposer7's pre-registered
> falsifier "matched-compute plain `engine-E3b` recovers the same targets ⟹ MTD buys nothing";
> `P-U2′` = my 3-in-1 calibration submission (§R39.13); `C` = the MTD pilot's pre-registered compute
> cap; `N_scan` = the number of points in a relaxed scan; `ν` = bias fill rate (eV/ps).
> Units: raw-KNL core-h throughout.

## 1. 🟢 Stage 0 priced — and my number and proposer7's agree by two independent routes

```
DERIVATION A (from my §R39.5 per-ps model)
  unbiased NVT per-ps, 21 atoms, KNL = 0.9 × the MTD per-ps figure (no bias-deposition overhead;
    the RMSD-vs-visited-structures term is what MTD adds and it grows with run length)
    = 0.39 / 0.81 / 3.72 core-h/ps
  3 seeds × 5 ps  ⟹  5.8 / 12.2 / 55.8      call it 6 / 12 / 56 raw-KNL core-h
DERIVATION B (from proposer7's own 1-seed run)
  ~2 core-h equivalent, dev box, 1 seed, 5 ps  × κ_xtb 2.4–12  × 3 seeds  ⟹  14 – 72 KNL core-h
🟢 The two bands overlap across most of their range and proposer7's own "~10 core-h [ESTIMATE]"
   sits inside both. CONFIRMED — stage 0 at 3 × 5 ps costs single-digit-to-low-tens core-h.
```

### 🔴 But 5 ps is the wrong length, and the reason is the mirror image of the clause I asked for

```
Stage 0's decision is ASYMMETRIC:
  comparator RECOVERS T1–T4   ⟹ the pilot is retired. A cheap, safe, correct outcome.
  comparator LEAVES TARGETS UNFOUND ⟹ 🔴 THE PILOT IS FUNDED — C core-h committed ON AN ABSENCE.
⟹ a too-short comparator returns "unfound" for a reason that has nothing to do with the engine,
  and spends C on it. That is EXACTLY the shape of the INDETERMINATE clause proposer7 accepted from
  me, running in the opposite direction: there, a too-short BIASED run risked a false REJECT of
  MTD; here, a too-short UNBIASED run risks a false FUND of it.
🔒 proposer7 already flagged the substance ("T2/T3/T4 were not seen in 5 ps and absence at n = 1 is
  not evidence of absence"). I am pricing the fix, because the fix is nearly free.
```

**T1 opened in under 1 ps. T3 and T4 are *secondary* steps** — they need the ring-opened
intermediate to survive and then react, so their first-passage times are not bounded by T1's.
A 5 ps window can only ever speak about T1.

| stage 0 design | cost (opt / base / pess) | what an "unfound" verdict is worth |
|---|---|---|
| 3 seeds × 5 ps (as proposed) | 6 / **12** / 56 | T1 only. "Unfound" for T2–T4 is uninformative |
| **3 seeds × 50 ps (recommended)** | 58 / **122** / 558 | T2–T4 get a real window. **6% of the C it gates** |
| 3 seeds × 100 ps | 117 / **243** / 1,116 | 12% of C; diminishing — 50 ps is the knee |

```
🟢 RECOMMEND 3 SEEDS × 50 ps ≈ 122 core-h base. It costs 6% of the budget whose commitment it
   decides, and it converts "absence" from an artefact of run length into an observation.
🔴 AND THE SYMMETRIC CLAUSE, which is proposer7's to write as the INDETERMINATE one was:
   PRE-REGISTER STAGE 0's LENGTH, and report per-target FIRST-PASSAGE TIME, not a boolean. The
   finding is "T2 unfound in 3 × 50 ps", never "T2 absent". A first-passage time also gives the
   pilot a MEASURED baseline recall to be scored against, which is what §39.42's own restructure
   says it wants.
```

N-scaling exponent as a by-product, at zero marginal cost** — two of P-U2′'s three deliverables.

pilot proceeds**.

```

   1. STAGE 0  (~122 core-h)  — can retire the whole arm; delivers κ_xtb + N-scaling free
   2. P-U2′, reduced to the ν measurement alone (~9 core-h), ONLY IF stage 0 funds the pilot
   3. the pilot itself, under cap C

   can kill the expensive thing goes first. It saves 9 core-h, which is nothing — but it also stops
   us measuring a bias-fill rate for a pilot that may never run, which is the point.

🟢 Trajectory question CLOSED by two independent confirmations (proposer7 + lead's source read).
   Per §R39.16 §2 that closes AVAILABILITY; R-C's admissibility remains refused on separate
   grounds and the live path is still the 21–35 core-h 2-D GFN2 probe.
```

# §R39.19 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: pricing §39.43 — the sorting rule, hysteresis as a budget gate, and what Δ_shell actually costs

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `Δ_shell` = the shell-conditioning correction, i.e. the barrier
> difference between a reaction computed on a small cluster and the same reaction at production
> solvation-shell size (§39.25, §39.26(d)); `MEP` = minimum-energy path; `hysteresis` (in a relaxed
> scan) = the sequential scan carrying the previous point's basin forward, so a coordinate needing
> a large discrete change moves late and abruptly; `rcfc`/`readfc` = read the Hessian from a
> checkpoint rather than recomputing it; `route smoke` = the cheap route-validation job that rides
> a submission; `T11-se` / `T21-se` / `T11-qst2` = the 11-atom single-ended, 21-atom single-ended
> and 11-atom double-ended TS attempts. Units: raw-KNL core-h throughout.

## 1. 🟢 The dev-box / cluster sorting rule — endorsed, with the one boundary that makes it safe

proposer7's rule: **a probe that measures CHEMISTRY does not need the cluster, because chemistry
does not know which machine it ran on; a probe that measures the MACHINE does.** They applied it to
run my 35 core-h 2-D probe on the dev box for free.

🟢 **Endorsed without reservation, and its value is on the axis that actually binds.** The saving is
not 35 core-h — it is a **~3.5-day submission round trip**, and every open condition on the
5-month schedule is wall-clock, not core-h (per the brief and §R38.3's own note). A rule that
converts a round trip into an afternoon is worth more than most core-h savings in this document.

```
🔴 THE ONE BOUNDARY, and it is the failure this project has already had twice this round:
   A CHEMISTRY PROBE WHOSE **COST** IS ALSO BEING READ MUST RUN ON THE CLUSTER — otherwise the
   answer is chemistry (portable) but the price tag is a dev-box number (not portable), and the
   two arrive in the same file looking equally trustworthy. That is exactly how the 0.247 core-h
   MTD anchor (12 threads, dev box) entered §R39.5 needing a κ_xtb of 2.4–12 to be usable at all.
🔒 OPERATIONAL FORM: a dev-box run may emit a CHEMICAL result with no provenance caveat. It may
   NOT emit a core-h figure without `[MEASURED, DEV BOX]` and the κ_xtb bracket attached in the
   same cell. Same discipline as §R38.4's unit-in-the-cell rule, applied to machines.
🟢 Under this rule P-U2′ correctly stays on the cluster (it measures κ_xtb, timing and N-scaling —
   pure machine), and stage 0 correctly stays on the cluster for the same reason even though its
   read-out is chemical. Nothing in §R39.18's ordering changes.
```

## 2. 🟢 Dual use for R-C — RESTORED in 2-D. Third state on one item, so here is the whole sequence.

The 2-D surface is smooth; no discontinuity in the grid; the MEP's `d(Li–O2)` runs 2.75 → 1.80
monotonically. The 1-D jump was a projection artefact.

```
STATE HISTORY OF ONE CLAIM — quote only the last row.
  §R39.5    dual use CLAIMED (the §39.40(d) scan IS T21-se's scan stage)         [my inference]
  §39.41(e) REFUSED for R-C — the 1-D maximum sits at a Li⁺ translocation        [proposer7, MEASURED]
  §R39.16   trajectory PRESERVED (lead) — closes availability, NOT admissibility [my flag]
  §39.43    🟢 RESTORED for R-C **in 2-D** — surface smooth, guess at
            d(O2–C3) ≈ 1.81 / d(Li–O2) ≈ 2.00, nothing discontinuous adjacent    [proposer7, MEASURED]
🔒 A reader who greps this document for "dual use" will hit four rows in four sections. The live
   one is the last. This is the second claim in two days to change state three times (the other is
   B0-D's unit), and both times the mid-states looked like conclusions.
```

**No reprice.** §R39.15 §5 already priced T21-se with a **GFN2** scan (12 / 35 / 120), and §R39.18
already offered the adaptive-grid variant at ~21. The 2-D requirement was inside the number before
this confirmation; what changed is that the number is now known to buy an admissible guess.

🟢 **And my item-2 verdict survives with its conclusion inverted in the good direction**, which
should be said plainly rather than quietly: *"at 21 atoms the scan runs on a cheap engine or
single-ended is eliminated by cost"* was the verdict; §39.43 confirms the cheap engine **works**,
so single-ended survives at production size. The verdict was a fork and the favourable branch is
the one that turned out to be real.

## 3. 🔴 The 0.10 eV hysteresis finding is a BUDGET GATE, and it is free

`1-D fine scan +0.955 eV` vs `2-D MEP +0.855 eV`. Li was free in both, so they should have agreed;
they differ because a sequential relaxed scan carries the previous basin forward, so the reported
maximum is **too high**. proposer7's rule: a discontinuity in a relaxed-scan profile is the
signature of a **missing coordinate** — never smooth it or re-grid it away.

**Its cost consequence, which is mine:**
```
A TS guess taken from a discontinuous 1-D scan is a guess at the wrong geometry. The TS
optimisation that follows is therefore drawn from a WORSE-than-baseline success distribution —
it is not a fair draw at q_capout = 0.25 (§R39.12's assumption, supported by n = 1).
⟹ 🔒 PRE-PAYMENT GATE, free, and it belongs in the payload not in a person's judgement:
   IF the relaxed-scan profile contains a discontinuity, DO NOT FUND `ts_opt+freq`+IRC on that
   guess. Re-scan in 2-D first (GFN2, ~21-35 core-h) or record the attempt as `indeterminate,
   missing coordinate` — which §39.39(f) already accepts as an outcome with a known cause.
COST AVOIDED PER FIRING   the whole downstream attempt, NOT a fraction of it:
   11 atoms  ~660 core-h        21 atoms  ~6,400 core-h (~4,700 with the rcfc saving)
COST TO IMPLEMENT         a monotonicity/jump check on a profile the scan already writes. Free.
```
🟢 **This is the cheapest gate identified in §R39** measured by cost-avoided per core-h-spent, and
unlike most gates it fires on data we generate anyway.

## 4. 🔴 Δ_shell — affordable. Its error bar is not. That distinction is the whole finding.

§39.43(e): S3 cannot buy production-size barriers per reaction, so buy the **shell-conditioning
correction once on a matched pair**. GFN2 gives R-A +0.486 vs R-C +0.855 ⟹ **Δ_shell ≈ 0.37 eV ≈
6.3 Boltzmann decades at 298 K.** Priced:

```
MARGINAL COST OF THE MATCHED PAIR
  R-A single-ended (T11-se)   already inside cut U56-2 — marginal cost 0
  R-C single-ended (T21-se)   6,371 base  (≈4,740 if the rcfc saving lands)
  ⟹ Δ_shell costs ONE T21-se. 🔴 WHICH IS THE ITEM THE CUT REMOVED.
🔒 ⟹ §39.43(e) RESURRECTS T21-se — at the same price, under a different and stronger
  justification. The cut was never a deletion of the computation; it was a deferral of it to the
  round where it buys a transferable correction instead of one orphan bake-off point. proposer7's
  stated reason for the cut and this consequence are the same fact seen twice, and the arithmetic
  I priced is unchanged.
⟹ AND IT IS ONE OF THE ≤3 PRODUCTION-CLASS ATTEMPTS PER ROUND (§R39.15 §5). A realistic S3 wave 1
  is: the Δ_shell R-C attempt + 2 others, and that round carries nothing else.
BREAK-EVEN vs per-reaction production-size barriers: 6,371N vs 6,371 ⟹ break-even at N = 1.1.
  For any S3 target set with ≥2 reactions the matched-pair design is cheaper. Not a close call.
```

### 🔴 What we cannot afford, stated because the plan will otherwise assume we can

```
Δ_shell measured on ONE pair has NO error bar. Its transferability across S3's target set is the
same class of question ADR-014 asks and it is UNMEASURED.
  2 pairs  ≈ 12,700 core-h   = most of a round, on top of wave 1's own attempts
  3 pairs  ≈ 19,100 core-h   = an entire round, buying n = 3 — still a useless variance estimate
⟹ 🔴 THE CORRECTION IS AFFORDABLE AT DFT; ITS UNCERTAINTY IS NOT. A 0.37 eV correction applied
  with an unmeasured spread is exactly the shape §39.32(h)'s 0.1 eV = ~50× warning is about, one
  level up — the correction is 6 decades and its own error could be a decade and we would not know.
🟢 THE ONLY AFFORDABLE VARIANCE INSTRUMENT, and it costs ~0 cluster core-h under §1's sorting rule:
  measure Δ_shell at GFN2 on 4-6 ADDITIONAL matched pairs ON THE DEV BOX. proposer7 already has
  the R-A/R-C pair at GFN2 (+0.486 / +0.855); extending it is the same job repeated.
  WHAT IT BUYS   the SHAPE of the spread — whether Δ_shell is a roughly constant offset across the
                 family or swings by ±0.2 eV with ligand identity. That is a decision-relevant
                 distinction and it is answerable for free.
  🔴 WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY   the MAGNITUDE at DFT. GFN2's own Δ_shell error is unmeasured, so the
                 GFN2 spread is a proxy for the DFT spread's shape and NOT for its size. I am
                 offering an instrument with a stated blind spot, not a substitute measurement.
⚠ proposer7's own protocol requirement is load-bearing on the cost too: MATCHED METHOD ON BOTH
  MEMBERS. With the 1-D value Δ_shell reads 0.47 instead of 0.37 — the correction's own error is
  the same order as the correction unless both sides are measured identically. ⟹ if the pair is
  ever split across rounds or methods, the money is spent and the number is void.
```

# §R39.20 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: 🔴🔴 REPRICE — the xtb anchor was 33× too high. My 3.24 exponent is RETRACTED, and the same defect may sit in the P3 anchor nobody has checked.

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `NVT` = constant particle-number/volume/temperature molecular
> dynamics; `stage 0` = §39.42's unbiased comparator run, which gates the metadynamics (MTD)
> pilot; `κ_xtb` = the KNL-vs-dev-box cost ratio **for xtb specifically** (a different number from
> G16's κ); `P3` = the round-1 plan item that produced this project's only cluster-side xtb cost
> figure; `1-thread-equivalent core-h` = cost at one thread, before any thread multiplier;
> `C` = the MTD pilot's pre-registered compute cap. Units: raw-KNL core-h unless stated.

## 1. My exponent inference is RETRACTED, and it failed for the reason proposer7 then found

```
§R39.18 §4, MINE:  ratio 2 / 0.247 = 8.10 over size ratio 1.909 ⟹ exponent 3.24, "above my
                   2-3 bracket, and the true value is probably higher still"
MEASURED, proposer7, same machine, same run type, SINGLE THREAD:
                   plain NVT 2 ps: 11 atoms 10.65 s · 21 atoms 39.00 s ⟹ EXPONENT = 2.01
🔴 RETRACTED IN FULL. 2.01 is inside my ORIGINAL 2-3 bracket, and I widened the bracket to 2-3.5
   on the strength of an inference whose denominator was a corrupted number.
```

🔒 **Why I was wrong is the useful part.** My denominator was `b0_conformers.json`'s anchor —
*5 ps, 11 atoms, 12 threads, 74 s wall = 0.247 core-h* — which is **wall × threads on a job that
cannot use more than ~2 threads**. The inflation lived entirely in the denominator, so the ratio
came out high and I read a real-looking exponent off it. I had the dev-box provenance flagged
(§R39.5, §R39.12) and the thread count printed in the anchor's own text, and I still divided by it.
**Flagging a number's provenance is not the same as checking its arithmetic.**

## 2. 🔴 The shipped anchor is 33× too high — and every xtb figure I wrote descends from it

```
MEASURED, proposer7, dev box, 1 thread, n = 1 per point:
  plain NVT, per ps:        11 atoms 0.00148 core-h/ps   ·   21 atoms 0.00542 core-h/ps
  MTD bias overhead/step:   11 atoms ×1.02               ·   21 atoms ×1.18   (2-18%, NOT a factor)
  thread scaling, 21 at:    1T 1.00 · 2T 1.40 · 4T 2.02 · 8T 2.01  ⟹ SATURATES AT 4, 8 BUYS NOTHING
b0_conformers.json's anchor  0.247 core-h for 5 ps @ 11 atoms
correct value                0.0074 core-h                ⟹ 🔴 33.4× TOO HIGH

🔒 **This is ADR-107's accounting lesson in a new place.** There, array tasks duplicated work and
the reported core-h was arithmetic about nothing. Here, threads were charged that were never used
and the reported core-h is arithmetic about nothing. **Same failure, different substrate**, and in
both cases the number looked entirely normal.

**Corrected planning rates, raw-KNL, 1-thread-equivalent** (κ_xtb 2.4 / 5 / 12 — still UNMEASURED,
still bracketed from §R21(e), and 🔴 still NOT κ_physical 2.4 or κ_thread 1.218, which are G16
numbers and are forbidden here by R35.2e):

|---|---|---|---|---|

| MTD, core-h/ps | 0.0153 | **0.0320** | 0.0767 | 0.43 / **0.90** / 4.13 ⟹ **28–54× too high** |

## 5. 🔒 Scheduling and accounting consequences — three, and all of them are guard-relevant

```
(a) AN xtb ITEM MUST DECLARE ITS CORES EXPLICITLY (1-4, knee at 2). A `cores_per_task = None`
    whole-node convention on an xtb item charges ~64 cores to buy ~2×, and §R26.3's ceiling
    formula makes it worse than the spend suggests: `64 × min_wall_h 0.5 = 32 core-h of CEILING
    per task` for a job that costs 0.03. ⟹ ~1,000× ceiling inflation, and the guard would refuse
    a package over threads nobody uses. 🔴 This is a guard-refusal risk, not a tidiness point.
(b) EVERY xtb DATUM RECORDS THREADS AND WALL SEPARATELY (proposer7's methodology ruling, adopted
    here as a costing rule). A single `core_hours` field cannot distinguish 74 s × 12 threads from
    74 s × 1 thread, and that indistinguishability IS the 33× error.
(c) 🔴 CPU TIME IS USELESS FOR xtb. proposer7 measured `/usr/bin/time` user time at ~3.8 × wall at
    4 threads — OpenMP busy-waits, so anyone computing parallel efficiency from CPU time concludes
    perfect scaling. ⟹ FREE SOURCE READ WORTH DOING: if `collect.py`'s core-h accounting uses CPU
    time anywhere rather than `cores × wall`, every xtb cost in the ledger is inflated ~3.8× on top
    of any thread error. I have not read it and I am not assuming which it is.
```

# §R39.21 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: pricing §39.45 — the reverse-scan gate is free, and Δ_shell(n) cannot be measured at DFT past n = 2

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `Δ_shell(n)` = the shell-conditioning correction as a *function* of
> the number of coordinating ligands `n` (§39.45), not the single number §39.43(e) treated it as;
> `T11-se` / `T21-se` / `T31-se` = single-ended transition-state (TS) attempts on the 11-, 21- and
> 31-atom members of the Li(EC)ₙ ladder; `SP` = single-point energy (one SCF, no gradient, no
> Hessian); `G-SCAN-1…5` = §39.45(a)'s reverse-scan gate conditions; `P-A`…`P-D` = proposer7's four
> proposed probes; `CN` = coordination number; `C-11` = the composite-level constraint (cheap
> geometry // expensive single point). Units: raw-KNL core-h unless stated.

## 1. 🟢 The reverse-scan gate — free, and its return on compute is the highest number in §R39

proposer7 could not reuse the refine trigger, for a reason I should have anticipated and did not:
**a jump on a coarse grid is expected** — it is a steep barrier sampled coarsely — so no `|ΔE|`
threshold at any value separates *steep* from *discontinuous*. Their instrument is structural
instead: run the scan in both directions, and **require the reverse scan to terminate at the
C-8-certified reactant**.

```
COST                one extra GFN2 relaxed scan per attempt.
  at the corrected xtb rates (§R39.20):   1-D, 21 atoms  ≈ 0.01 – 0.05 core-h
                                          2-D, 21 atoms  ≈ 0.05 – 0.30 core-h
COST AVOIDED PER FIRING   the whole downstream DFT attempt:
                          ~660 core-h (11 atoms)  ·  ~6,400 core-h (21 atoms)
RETURN              even at a 1% firing rate on 21-atom attempts the expected saving is ~64 core-h
                    against a cost of ~0.05. ⟹ ~1,000× on expectation, and the gate is CERTAIN
                    while the saving is probabilistic — which is the right way round.
```

🟢 **No reprice.** The scan is the free stage of a TS attempt, so doubling it moves T11-se and
T21-se by <0.1%. Both totals stand.
🟢 **And it is strictly better than the threshold gate I priced in §R39.19 §3**: a structural
identity check against a structure we already certify has no tuning parameter and transfers to
reactions nobody has looked at. My version needed a discontinuity detector and would have had to be
calibrated per reaction. **I priced a heuristic; proposer7 replaced it with an instrument at the
same cost.** The firing-count instrumentation (never fires ⟹ unreached; always fires ⟹ the scan
design is wrong) is the §R26.2 `cores_observed` pattern applied to a gate, and it is free.
⚠ The validation itself is the strongest single argument for the gate: forward max +0.856 vs
reverse +0.320, and the two scans do not end at the same structure (d(Li–O2) 2.73 vs 2.13 at the
same constrained coordinate). **A 0.536 eV apparent-barrier difference from path direction alone**
is not a subtle effect and nothing in a one-directional cost model would ever have shown it.

## 2. 🔴 Δ_shell(n) — the finding that reprices §R39.19 §4, and the answer is harder than "more pairs"

```
[MEASURED, GFN2, dev box — proposer7 §39.45]
  n = 1  barrier 0.489 eV   ΔE_rxn −0.317   ⟵ EXOTHERMIC
  n = 2  barrier 0.855      ΔE_rxn +0.090   ⟵ ENDOTHERMIC   🔴 the reaction changes SIGN
  n = 3  barrier 1.045      ΔE_rxn +0.202
  Δ_shell steps: +0.366 (1→2), +0.190 (2→3) — decelerating, roughly halving
```
⟹ §R39.19 §4 priced Δ_shell as **one number bought by one matched pair**. It is a **function**, and
one matched pair buys **one step of it**. That is a different purchase and it needs different
arithmetic.

### The hard limit, and it is a submission limit rather than a budget one

**Scale factor 11 → 31 atoms**: `(31/11)³ = 22.36` × cycle growth 1.0–2.8 (3N−6 goes 27 → 87)
⟹ **S₃₁ = 22.4 / 35.8 / 62.6** `[ESTIMATE, the same cube rule applied even further outside its
fitted range than §R39.3's — treat the optimistic column as the only one with any margin]`.

| T31-se stage (31 atoms, n = 3) | opt | base | pess |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts_opt`+`freq` | 3,293 | 11,993 | 35,243 |
| 2×IRC | 3,853 | 11,635 | 34,180 |
| GFN2 2-D scan | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 |
| **T31-se total** | **7,146** | **23,628** | **69,423** |

```
GUARD CHECK (§R26.1/§R26.3, ceiling basis, guard 21,000):
  at BASE   ts_opt+freq 11,993 ⟹ wall 187 h ⟹ links 4 ⟹ ceiling 12,288
            IRC as 2 jobs, 5,818 each ⟹ wall 91 h ⟹ links 2 ⟹ ceiling 6,144 each
            TOTAL CEILING 24,576  >  21,000   🔴 THE PACKAGE WOULD BE REFUSED AT SUBMIT.
  at OPTIMISTIC   ceiling ≈ 10,240 — it fits, but it fills half a round and carries no margin
                  against a scale factor extrapolated three ligands past its anchor.
🔴 VERDICT: A FULL DFT SINGLE-ENDED TS ATTEMPT AT n = 3 IS NOT SUBMITTABLE AT ANY CENTRAL ESTIMATE.
   ⟹ Δ_shell(n) IS MEASURABLE AT DFT FOR n = 1 AND n = 2 AND FOR NO LARGER n. THE DFT CORRECTION
     CAN ONLY EVER HAVE ONE STEP.
   ⟹ 🔴 THE "converges by n ≈ 4-5" EXTRAPOLATION CANNOT BE VALIDATED AT DFT WITHIN THIS PROJECT'S
     BUDGET, BY ANY DESIGN. It is a GFN2-only observation and must be reported as one.
```

🔒 **And this strengthens §39.43(e)'s design rather than weakening it, in a way worth stating
plainly**: §R39.19 §4 said the matched-pair design *beats* per-reaction production barriers at a
break-even of N = 1.1. It is stronger than that. **Per-reaction production-size barriers are not
expensive, they are IMPOSSIBLE** — the guard refuses them at n = 3 and above. The matched-pair
design is not the cheaper option; it is the only option that submits.

## 3. 🟢 The affordable instrument — a DFT single-point ladder on GFN2 geometries, anchored where we have both

The full attempt is unaffordable at n ≥ 3; the barrier *estimate* is not. Take the GFN2 2-D scan's
path — which is free and which §39.45's reverse gate now validates — and compute **DFT single-point
energies along it**. No saddle optimisation, no Hessian, no IRC.

```
DFT SP COST, level3 + UltraFine + open-shell doublet   [ESTIMATE, derived from li_ec_cation's
  11 atoms   ~0.16 – 0.56 core-h/point                  5.031 core-h opt+freq ÷ 20-40 cycles, then
  21 atoms   ~1.1  – 3.9                                × the route multiplier stack. NEVER measured
  31 atoms   ~3.6  – 12.6                               as a standalone SP on this project.]
  41 atoms   ~8.3  – 29

LADDER, 5 path points per n (reactant, 3 along the path, top):
  n = 3 (31 at)    18 –  63 core-h
  n = 4 (41 at)    42 – 145 core-h
  ⟹ Δ_shell(n) at DFT-SP level for n = 1, 2, 3, 4:  ≈ 100 – 250 core-h TOTAL
  ⟹ 0.4 – 1.1 % of ONE n = 3 full attempt, which cannot be submitted anyway.
```

```
🟢 AND IT IS CALIBRATABLE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A GUESS. We can afford FULL
   attempts at n = 1 and n = 2. Run the SP ladder at n = 1 and n = 2 as well and the SP method's
   OWN bias against a real TS attempt is MEASURED at two points, at ~5 core-h. A cheap estimator
   whose error is measured against the expensive one on the overlap is the standard hierarchical
   design, and here the overlap is free because we are buying n = 1 and n = 2 regardless.
🔴 WHAT IT IS NOT: an SP barrier on a GFN2 path is not a TS barrier. It is a barrier along a GFN2
   path, and the geometry error only partly cancels in a DIFFERENCE. That partial cancellation is
   C-11's own argument (cheap geometry // expensive single point) applied one level out, and
   C-11's transferability here is UNMEASURED — which is exactly what the n = 1/n = 2 calibration
   points measure. 🔒 I am proposing an estimator WITH its calibration attached, not instead of it.
⚠ TWO CONDITIONS, both free, both fatal if skipped:
   · the SP ladder must use the SAME level and route flags as the full attempts, or the calibration
     measures the route difference instead of the method difference (proposer7's matched-method
     requirement, one level down);
   · every rung uses a 2-D scan path that has PASSED the §39.45 reverse gate. An SP ladder on a
     hysteretic path inherits the 0.536 eV artefact and would report it as shell conditioning.
```

## 3b. 🔴 WHEN the ladder's two calibration points actually exist — a scheduling dependency, added after lead approval

The SP ladder's calibration rests on the full attempts at n = 1 and n = 2. **They are not in the
same round.**

```
n = 1 full attempt = T11-se (R-A)   🟢 INSIDE cut U56-2 — funded, this round
n = 2 full attempt = T21-se         🔴 CUT from U56-2 and deferred to S3 wave 1 (§R39.19 §4)
⟹ UNTIL WAVE 1 RUNS, THE LADDER HAS ONE CALIBRATION POINT, NOT TWO. One point measures an OFFSET;
  two measure whether the offset is CONSTANT ACROSS n — and constancy across n is the entire claim
  the ladder makes. A one-point calibration cannot support the 3-tier deliverable's SP rungs at
  n = 3 and n = 4; it can only support them provisionally, and the label must say so.
🟢 RECOMMENDATION, and it costs nothing to decide now: RUN THE LADDER IN THE U56-2 ROUND ANYWAY.
  ~100-250 core-h of ceiling is invisible against the 4,014 of headroom §R39.14 leaves, the n = 1
  calibration point lands immediately, and the n = 3/n = 4 rungs are then already computed and
  waiting when wave 1 supplies the second point. Deferring the ladder to wave 1 buys nothing and
  costs a round of latency on the tier the user's decision turns on.
🔒 So the honest form of the 3-tier deliverable, if it is reported before wave 1, is:
  DFT-resolved over ONE rung · SP-resolved over four, CALIBRATED AT ONE · GFN2-shaped beyond.
  It becomes the two-rung version quoted in §5 only after T21-se runs.
```

## 4. Ordering, and the two items that cost nothing

```
🟢 P-D FIRST — endorsed on cost grounds as well as proposer7's. It is dev-box GFN2, so ~0 cluster
   core-h, and it can invalidate everything downstream: a correction that does not transfer ACROSS
   REACTIONS is not a correction, and no amount of shell variation reveals that. This is the fourth
   time this round the cheapest item has been the one that can kill the expensive one (§39.40(d),
   stage 0, the reverse gate, now P-D). 🔒 It is no longer a coincidence; it is the shape of a
   correctly ordered plan, and it is worth naming as a standing heuristic rather than rediscovering.
🟢 P-A (n = 4) — dev-box GFN2, ~0 cluster core-h. Worth the slot: it decides whether the
   correction is over a SHORT LIST, and a short list is the difference between a declared axis with
   4 rungs and one with an open tail. But it runs AFTER P-D.
🟢 Δ_shell corrected 0.37 → 0.366 (matched 2-D on both members) — no arithmetic in §R39 moves.
   🔒 Recording proposer7's own note because it is the useful part: the number survived the
   matched-method check BY LUCK, and they published before running it. My warning that a
   split-method pair voids the money was right for the wrong pair — I aimed it at a future split
   and the violation was already in the published figure.
```

## 5. The shell-distribution axis — cost 0, but its RESOLUTION is what the ladder buys

proposer7 proposes treating the shell distribution as a declared uncertainty axis (the U-72 / F-1
pattern) rather than picking `n`, given U-65's finding that the experimental Li⁺(EC) CN does not
converge. **They are right that it costs 0 beyond what we already compute. What it costs is
RESOLUTION, and that is a number I owe the decision rather than an opinion:**

```
A shell-averaged rate's spread is only as resolved as the rungs behind it.
  DFT full attempts        n = 1, 2                    (2 rungs — the hard limit, §2)
  DFT-SP ladder            n = 1, 2, 3, 4              (4 rungs, ~100-250 core-h, calibrated at 2)
  GFN2                     n = 1 … 6                   (6+ rungs, ~0 cluster core-h, uncalibrated
                                                        against DFT beyond n = 2)
⟹ THE DELIVERABLE'S HONEST FORM IS: a shell-averaged rate whose spread is DFT-resolved over two
  rungs, SP-resolved over four, and GFN2-shaped beyond. Three tiers, three provenance labels, one
  number. 🔴 It must NOT be reported as a single spread with one label — that would hide exactly
  the tier boundary the user's decision turns on.
🔒 Whether that deliverable is acceptable is a USER decision, as proposer7 says. My contribution is
  the resolution figures above, so the user decides against numbers instead of against a shape.
```

| | work | charged, `cores = 12` | charged, whole-node default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 × 100 ps = 1,200 ps | 16 / **33** / 78 | 33 (η ≈ 1.00) | 173 (η = 0.19) |

```
🟢 CHEAPER THAN BOTH OF MY OPTIONS AND BETTER DESIGNED — 33 vs my 58 (3×500 ps) and 122 (3×50 ps).
   Guard ceiling = 12 cores × clamp(wall, 0.5, 48) ≈ 33. Invisible against 21,000.
⚠ ONE NUMBER NEEDS ITS BRACKET, under the rule we both adopted (§R39.19 §1): "~0.54 h per seed at
   1 thread" is a DEV-BOX wall. On KNL it is 0.54 × κ_xtb(2.4-12) = 1.3 – 6.5 h/seed. Same
   conclusion — nowhere near `max_wall_h` 48 — but the cell should carry the bracket, because a
   dev-box wall that travels without it is exactly how the 0.247 anchor got into my §R39.5.
🟢 THE STAGED READ-OUT AT 25/50/100 ps IS THE PART I COULD NOT HAVE PRICED: it turns "was the
   window sufficient?" from a design assumption into a measurement, at zero cost, and neither of my
   lengths could answer it at any price. Same with the precursor-survival field — a competing-risk
   outcome and a censored outcome sharing a bucket is the C-10.1 conflation in a new place.
```

## 3. 🟢 The SP ladder's calibration is itself extrapolated — accepted, and the noise term is buyable

proposer7's condition: the n = 1/2 calibration measures `bias(n)` **at n = 1 and 2**, and using it
at n = 3/4 assumes `bias` is n-independent — **the same transferability assumption Δ_shell is under
scrutiny for.** Correct, and it must be reported as *"one unquantified extrapolation converted into
a smaller, named one"* rather than as "a calibrated number."

Their free self-test — if `bias(n=1)` and `bias(n=2)` differ by more than their noise, flat-bias is
already refuted where we can look — needs a **noise** term, and we have no repeat measurements.
🟢 **It is buyable, and the reverse-scan gate already generates the second sample for free:**
```
Every gated reaction has TWO GFN2 paths (forward and reverse). Running the SP ladder on BOTH gives
a WITHIN-n path-sensitivity spread — which is the dominant noise term for an SP-on-a-path energy.
  cost of the second path:  n = 1  ~0.8 – 2.8 core-h   ·   n = 2  ~5 – 20 core-h
  ⟹ ~25 core-h TOTAL buys a within-n noise estimate at BOTH calibration points.
⟹ that is what decides whether bias(n=1) and bias(n=2) "differ by more than their noise". Without
  it the self-test has no denominator and cannot fire in either direction.
🔴 IT IS A PATH-SENSITIVITY SPREAD, NOT A FULL UNCERTAINTY. It does not cover basis, functional or
  the GFN2 geometry's own error. Named instrument, named blind spot — same footing as the ladder.
```

## 4. 🔒 The cheap-probe heuristic — its cost-side failure mode is LATENCY, and here is the number

proposer7 named the failure mode (an endless chain of cheap probes that never funds anything) and
the guard (each cheap item carries a pre-registered read-out that releases or kills). Both right.
**The cost side has a different failure mode and it is the one that would actually bite us:**

```
CUMULATIVE CORE-H OF EVERY CHEAP PROBE THIS ROUND — this is NOT the risk:
  §39.40(d) 7 · stage 0 33 · P-U2′ 0.7 · 2-D + reverse scans ~0.6 · SP ladder 100-250
  ≈ 140 – 290 core-h against the 3,514 (cut U56-2) they gate  ⟹ 4 – 8 %. A healthy ratio.
🔴 CUMULATIVE LATENCY — THIS IS THE RISK:
  four cluster-side probes SERIALISED at ~3.5 days per submission round trip = 2 WEEKS,
  against a 21.5-week cap whose every open condition is wall-clock (§R38.3, the brief).
  The same four BUNDLED INTO ONE SUBMISSION = one round trip.
🔒 ⟹ COST-SIDE GUARD, and it is free: BUNDLE CLUSTER-SIDE CHEAP PROBES INTO ONE SUBMISSION. Stage 0,
  P-U2′, the SP ladder's n = 1 rung and the U56-2 items can all ride the same round — none of them
  gates another (proposer7's ordering is stage 0 → P-U2′, but P-U2′ is 0.7 core-h, so running it
  unconditionally costs less than the round trip saved by not deferring it).
🟢 AND THE DEV-BOX SORTING RULE (§R39.19 §1) IS WHAT MAKES THE HEURISTIC SUSTAINABLE AT ALL — the
  probes with no latency cost are the ones that ran on the dev box. Four cheap probes would have
  been 2 weeks of calendar without it; with it, most cost an afternoon.
```

## 5. What moves

```
🟢 STAGE 0 REPRICED: 12 seeds × 100 ps = 16 / 33 / 78 core-h work, ceiling ~33 at `cores = 12`.
   Supersedes BOTH §R39.18's 3 × 50 ps (122) and §R39.20's 3 × 500 ps (58).
🟢 SP LADDER: +~25 core-h for the second-path noise estimate ⟹ ~125 – 275 core-h total.
🟢 DFT scan row, T11-se, T21-se, cut U56-2, Δ_shell economics, the n = 3 submission limit — all
   UNCHANGED.
🔴 NEW, PRICED-NOT-DECIDED: the ungated-DFT-scan case (no GFN2 path) — gating wins above a ~35%
   ungated-failure rate at 11 atoms, ~4% at 21. For when ADR-014's novel-element case arrives.
```

# §R39.24 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: `sp_ladder` — the plan.py Item spec for coder11

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `sp_ladder` = the DFT single-point ladder of §R39.21 §3 (single-point
> energies along a GFN2 path, no geometry optimisation / no Hessian / no intrinsic reaction
> coordinate); `rung` = one member of the Li(EC)ₙ series at ligand count `n`; `SP` = one single-point
> energy job; `P-A` = proposer7's n = 4 GFN2 probe (dev box, ~0 cluster cost); `gate` = §39.45's
> reverse-scan gate; `η` = packing efficiency (§R39.22); `links` / `min_wall_h` / `max_wall_h` /
> `CAP` = the §R26.3 ceiling machinery. Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` basis for every budget and
> ceiling field below (§R39.22 convention — a G16 job on `ncpus=64` actually uses its 64 cores, so
> work ≈ charged here by construction).

Lead approved the ladder into the U56-2 round and asked for exact core-h plus the `plan.py` Item
spec. This section is that hand-off and nothing else.

## 1. Scope, and why the point counts differ per rung

```
PER RUNG   SP energies along the rung's GATE-PASSED GFN2 2-D path.
  n = 1, 2   10 SP each = 5 path points × BOTH gate paths (forward + reverse)
             ⟹ the second path is the WITHIN-n NOISE term (§R39.23 §3). It is required ONLY at the
               calibration rungs, because that is where proposer7's flat-bias self-test lives:
               "do bias(n=1) and bias(n=2) differ by more than their noise" has no denominator
               without it and cannot fire in either direction.
  n = 3, 4    5 SP each = 5 path points × ONE path
             ⟹ the ladder's claim at n = 3/4 is carried by the calibration, not by a local spread.
5 points/path = the two endpoints + three along the path, including the maximum. NOT the profile —
  the profile is what the free GFN2 scan is for.
```

## 2. Costs — 🔴 SUPERSEDED BY §R39.26. The table below and §3's budget fields are the PRE-§39.48 version; the Item shape, `cores_per_task`, the ADR-110 note, the preconditions and the claim discipline all still stand.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| n = 2 | 21 | 10 | 1.1 – 3.9 | 11 – **39** |
| n = 3 | 31 | 5 | 3.6 – 12.6 | 18 – **63** |
| n = 4 | 41 | 5 | 8.3 – 29 | 42 – **145** |
| **total** | | **30** | | **73 – 253** |

🔴 `[ESTIMATE]`, and the weakest number here is the per-SP cost: it is the `li_ec_cation` opt+freq
anchor ÷ 20–40 optimisation cycles × the level3 route multiplier stack. **No standalone SP has ever
been measured on this project.** At 253 core-h against a 21,000 guard it would have to be wrong by
~80× to change any conclusion, which is why I am willing to ship it as a budget rather than pilot it
first — but the first rung to return is also this project's first SP measurement, and every later
rung should be re-derived from it rather than from my stack.

## 3. 🔴 The Item spec — and one task per rung, NOT one job for the ladder

A single 64-core job for the whole ladder has a lower ceiling (253 vs 279) and I am **not**
recommending it: one failure would lose all four rungs, and the rungs are independently useful.

```

                                 COMPLIANT — work ≈ charged by construction, η ≈ 1. The rule exists

    rung n=2   budget   39   wall 0.61 h                            → ceiling  39
    rung n=3   budget   63   wall 0.98 h                            → ceiling  63

## 4. 🔴 Four preconditions — none costs core-h, all of them void the rung if skipped

```
1  ROUTE FLAGS IDENTICAL TO THE FULL ATTEMPTS. level3 = wB97XD/def2-SVPD, `nosymm`,
   `Int(Grid=UltraFine)`, charge 0 / multiplicity 2, PCM ε 18.5. 🔴 If the SP route differs from the
   full attempt's in ANY flag, the calibration measures the ROUTE difference instead of the METHOD
   difference — proposer7's matched-method requirement one level down, and the money is spent
   either way. This is the same failure that made their own Δ_shell read 0.47 instead of 0.366.
2  EACH RUNG'S PATH MUST CARRY A §39.45 REVERSE-SCAN VERDICT. An SP ladder on a hysteretic path
   inherits the 0.536 eV artefact and reports it as shell conditioning. Cost of obtaining the
   verdict: ~0, dev box, GFN2. Cost of skipping it: the rung.
3  CONDITION 8 (§39.39(b)) APPLIES UNCHANGED — the deck must be verified as APPLIED, not echoed.
   🔴 `deck_verification.json` HAS NOT RETURNED. The ladder inherits this open condition exactly as
   the full attempts do; a silently-ignored `scrf=(pcm,read)` makes every rung a gas-phase number,
   and for a charge-localising ion pair that is a different quantity, not a biased one.
4  `cores` FIELD PRESENT, NOT DEFAULTED (§R39.22 §4). Under-reporting passes the guard and surfaces
   as an allocation surprise; over-reporting is at least refused loudly.
```

## 5. What the ladder can and cannot claim on the day it returns

```
🟢 CAN   an SP-level barrier at n = 1, 2, 3 (and 4) on gate-passed paths, with a within-n
         path-sensitivity spread at the two calibration rungs.
🔴 CANNOT   a calibrated bias, until the FULL attempt at n = 2 (T21-se) runs in S3 wave 1
         (§R39.21 §3b). Until then the ladder has ONE calibration point: it measures an OFFSET,
         not whether the offset is constant in n — and constancy in n is the ladder's whole claim.
🔒 ⟹ ON RETURN, THE HONEST LABEL IS: "DFT-resolved over ONE rung · SP-resolved over four,
     CALIBRATED AT ONE · GFN2-shaped beyond." It becomes the two-rung version only after wave 1.
     The three-tier deliverable must not be reported with one spread and one label at any stage.
```

## 6. ⚠ Stage 0 is NOT priced as final in this section

proposer7 flagged a message crossing: lead approved `3 × 500 ps` before reading their `12 × 100 ps`
ruling. The **total is ~1,200 ps either way (±20%), so my rate model is unaffected** — but the task
decomposition differs (12 small tasks vs 3 long ones) and that is precisely what §R39.22's η
arithmetic says matters:
```
12 seeds × 1 thread, cores declared 12   charged ≈ 33 core-h, ceiling ≈ 33     η ≈ 1.00
 3 seeds × 2 threads, cores declared 6   charged ≈ 58 core-h, ceiling ≈ 58     η ≈ 1.00
 either, whole-node default (64)         charged 173 – 619, ceiling likewise   η = 0.09 – 0.19
🔒 Both decompositions are fine IF cores are declared; NEITHER is fine under a whole-node default.
   And proposer7 is right that 12 tasks measure η better than 3 do — the same n-is-too-small
   argument they used for first-passage time and I used for p_min, now on a third quantity.
⟹ I will price stage 0 as final when the lead's confirmation lands. Nothing else waits on it.
```

# §R39.26 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: `sp_ladder` REPRICED after §39.48. Both ratifications buy more, and the budget triples.

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `G-SCAN-2` = the reverse-scan gate's endpoint-identity condition
> (§39.45(a), corrected in §39.48); `rung` = one member of the Li(EC)ₙ ladder; `SP` = one
> single-point energy job; `bracket` = the 5-point window centred on the GFN2 barrier maximum;
> `path-selection spread` = the within-rung scatter across independent kick-seed paths.
> Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` basis for budgets and ceilings (G16 at `ncpus=64` uses its 64
> cores ⟹ work ≈ charged, η ≈ 1).

🔴 **SUPERSEDES §R39.24 §2 and §3's cost table and budget fields.** Everything else in §R39.24 —
the Item shape, `cores_per_task = 64`, the ADR-110 misreading note, the four preconditions, the
claim discipline — stands unchanged.

## 1. What changed, and both changes buy more measurement

```
(a) PATH-SELECTION SPREAD AT EVERY RUNG, not just the calibration rungs.
    proposer7's reason, which I accept over my own: importing the spread from n = 1, 2 to n = 3, 4
    is ANOTHER FLAT-IN-n ASSUMPTION — the exact defect I flagged in the calibration itself. And the
    system demonstrably gets rougher with n (1 of 6 seeds landed 0.686 eV high at 21 atoms;
    hysteresis doubled from n = 2 to n = 3). 🔒 THE PRINCIPLE: buy what can be measured, assume
    only what cannot. The CALIBRATION at n = 3/4 is impossible (§R39.21 §2); the SPREAD is not.
    ⟹ 2 independent kick-seed paths at EVERY rung, not 2 at n = 1/2 and 1 at n = 3/4.
(b) 7 POINTS PER PATH, TRIGGERED TO ≤ 9 — not my 5.
    🔴 My 5 points evaluated DFT at the GFN2 maximum, and the DFT maximum need not sit there.
    Sampling a maximum on a coarse grid UNDER-ESTIMATES it — measured at 0.10 eV in this project —
    i.e. a barrier biased LOW ⟹ a rate biased HIGH ⟹ §0-h's optimistic direction, which is the
    one this project is not allowed to be wrong in silently. Spec: both endpoints + a 5-point
    bracket centred on the GFN2 maximum; if the DFT maximum lands at a bracket edge, extend by 2.
    🟢 AND IT MAKES THE LADDER SELF-CHECKING WHERE 5 COULD NOT, for free: comparing where the DFT
    maximum sits against where the GFN2 maximum sits measures how well a GFN2 path serves as a DFT
    path — the ladder's own foundational assumption, tested by the ladder itself.
```

## 2. Repriced — budget fields are the CAP (9 points × 2 paths = 18 SP/rung)

| n = 1 | 11 | 0.16 – 0.56 | 2.2 – 7.8 | **10** | 0.16 h → clamped 0.5 | **32** |
| n = 2 | 21 | 1.1 – 3.9 | 15 – 55 | **70** | 1.09 h | **70** |
| n = 3 | 31 | 3.6 – 12.6 | 50 – 176 | **227** | 3.55 h | **227** |
| n = 4 | 41 | 8.3 – 29 | 116 – 406 | **522** | 8.16 h | **522** |
| **3-rung (ship now)** | | | 67 – 239 | **307** | | **329** |
| **4-rung (with P-A)** | | | 183 – 645 | **829** | | **851** |

```
§R26.1 CHECK   every task budget ≤ CAP (64 × 48 = 3,072) ⟹ links == 1 everywhere. 🟢 PASSES.
vs §R39.24     3-rung budget 108 → 307 (2.8×) · ceiling 134 → 329 (2.5×). 4-rung ceiling 851.
```

**Bundled round, updated** (§R39.25 §3 arithmetic with the new ladder):
```
cut U56-2 6,530 + P1b 5,328 + P5 3,128 + sp_ladder 329 + stage 0 33 + P-U2′ 1
  = 15,349 / 21,000   ⟹ 🟢 FITS, margin 5,651 = 26.9%   (was 27.8%)

🔴 **And my disclosure needs restating at the new size, because its own margin shrank.** The per-SP
cost is still the `li_ec_cation` opt+freq anchor ÷ 20–40 cycles × the level3 multiplier stack, and
**no standalone SP has ever been measured on this project.** At 134 of ceiling it would have had to
be ~80× wrong to threaten the guard; at 851 (4-rung) it is **~25× wrong**. Still a wide margin, but
three times narrower than when I said "it cannot matter." 🔒 The mitigation is proposer7's rule and
it is already agreed: **the first rung to return is this project's first SP measurement, and every
later rung re-derives from it rather than from my stack** — the same discipline as "measure κ per
run, never store a correction factor."

## 3. Preconditions — two amendments, both free

```
PRECONDITION 2, AMENDED. The gate's primary test is no longer structural identity.
  🔴 n = 1 FALSIFIED G-SCAN-2 as written: the reverse endpoint sits 0.35 Å away but 0.000 eV away,
    with barriers agreeing to 0.013 eV — because `d(Li–O_break)` at n = 1 is a SOFT coordinate
    (1.95 → 3.40 Å spans 0.06 eV). A structural test cannot separate a soft-mode displacement from
    a reaction-relevant one, and the false positive blocks a GOOD path while looking like a
    pipeline failure. 🟢 CORRECTED TEST (proposer7): fire unless the reverse endpoint's ENERGY
    matches the certified reactant AND the two directions' BARRIERS agree, both within the scan's
    own measured resolution — self-referential, no imported constant, and it separates n = 1 (PASS)
    from n = 2 and n = 3 (FIRE). Structural identity is demoted to a reported covariate.
  ⟹ COST UNCHANGED (~0, dev box). Verdicts for n = 1, 2, 3 now EXIST.
PRECONDITION 5, NEW — the ladder consumes 2-D paths at n ≥ 2.
  🔴 HYSTERESIS GROWS WITH n: the 1-D-vs-2-D maximum inflation is 0.00 / 0.10 / 0.21 eV at
    n = 1 / 2 / 3 — it MORE THAN DOUBLES from n = 2 to n = 3. Mechanism holds (more ligands ⟹ Li's
    rearrangement is a larger discrete event ⟹ a sequential 1-D scan carries the wrong basin
    further).
  ⟹ n ≥ 2 uses the 2-D paths, which exist (`12_scan2d/`, `16_ec3/`). n = 1 may use its 1-D path.
    🔴 n = 4, IF FUNDED, NEEDS A 2-D GFN2 SCAN FIRST — free, dev box, now a PRECONDITION rather
    than an option. Not a blocker for the 3-rung shipment.
🟢 SIDE EFFECT ON MY OWN §R39.23 §1 NUMBERS: the ungated-DFT-scan thresholds (gating wins above a
  ~35% failure rate at 11 atoms, ~4% at 21) are unchanged, but the growth of hysteresis with n means
  the threshold falls further at 31+ atoms. Directionally stated, not re-derived — the case does not
  exist yet.
```

🟢 **Matched method protected a number for the second time**: §39.45(b)'s Δ_shell table used 2-D at
every rung, so it stands. With 1-D values Δ_shell(2→3) would have read 0.300 instead of 0.190 —

# §R39.27 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: n = 1's second path dropped (free), η needs a survivorship guard, and the wave-1 collision may dissolve on its own

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `rung` = one member of the Li(EC)ₙ ladder; `SP` = one single-point
> energy job; `kick seed` = an independently perturbed starting geometry (§39.42(a));
> `η` = packing efficiency, work ÷ charged (§R39.22); `wave 1` = S3's first production wave;
> `rcfc` = reading the Hessian from a checkpoint instead of recomputing it (§R39.17 §4);
> `T21-se` = the 21-atom single-ended TS attempt. Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` for ceilings.

## 1. n = 1 loses its second path — and the guard does not notice, which is worth knowing

proposer7 acted on my operational note and measured it: **6 kick seeds at n = 1, one basin, spread
0.0005 eV.** So "n = 1 needs no noise term" is a number rather than an assumption, and the second
path there buys nothing.

```
n = 1   18 SP → 9 SP    budget 10 → 5    ceiling 32 → 32    🔴 UNCHANGED
3-rung  budget 307 → 302 · ceiling 329 → 329
4-rung  budget 829 → 824 · ceiling 851 → 851
ROUND   15,349 / 21,000 — UNMOVED. Margin still 26.9%.
```

🔒 **The `min_wall_h = 0.5` floor eats the whole saving**: n = 1's wall is 0.08 h either way, so its
ceiling is `64 × 0.5 = 32` regardless of budget. That is §R24.1's shape a third time, and it has a
useful consequence rather than only a cost one:
```
🟢 n = 1 IS FREE UP TO 32 core-h OF CEILING — about 57 SP at the pessimistic unit cost, against the
  9 it now uses. IF THERE IS EVER A SCIENTIFIC REASON TO WANT MORE POINTS OR MORE PATHS AT n = 1,
  IT COSTS THE GUARD NOTHING. I am not proposing one — proposer7's reason for dropping the second
  path is that it buys nothing, and 0.0005 eV is a measurement, not a budget argument. But the
  headroom exists and should not be rediscovered later as if it were a concession.
```

## 2. 🔴 η needs a survivorship guard — the dead seed is my problem too

proposer7's finding: one of the six seeds died under concurrency and **left no output file**. A
pipeline that globs surviving outputs would have computed the spread over survivors silently.

**Their note that this reaches my accounting is correct and I want it stated sharply, because the
direction is not obvious:**
```
work    = Σ (threads × wall) FROM RECORDS.   A task that dies without a marker contributes NOTHING.
charged = total_cores × wall.                It contributes its FULL SHARE.
⟹ η = work / charged IS BIASED LOW BY EXACTLY THE DEAD TASKS.
DIRECTION: we would believe packing is WORSE than it is ⟹ we would budget MORE charged per unit of
  work ⟹ conservative, i.e. SAFE. 🔴 But safe-by-accident again, and worse: an η measured over
  survivors is not a packing efficiency at all, it is packing efficiency CONFOUNDED WITH FAILURE
  RATE, and the two need separating because they have different fixes (declare cores vs fix the
  concurrency bug).
🔒 ⟹ ADDED TO STAGE 0's η SPEC, free: η MUST be reported with `n_tasks_attempted` and
  `n_tasks_converged`, or it is a survivorship statistic and not a measurement. Same two fields
  proposer7 specified for the seeds; same rule one layer down.
```
🔒 **This is the third instance of one shape in a single round** — a rate computed over completed
runs (§39.39's own warning), the gate selecting for path agreement (§39.48), and now η computed
over surviving tasks. Three different quantities, three different sections, one defect: **a
denominator quietly restricted to the cases that succeeded.**

## 3. 🟢 The wave-1 collision — proposer7 is right that it is premature, and it may dissolve entirely

Their deferral-with-a-trigger is correct and the reasoning is a resource-allocation argument, so I
endorse it explicitly rather than just accepting it: **spend scarce guard headroom on the item whose
statistics degrade, not on the item that can wait.** Their arithmetic checks out — one-sided 95%
upper bound on `p` from 0 successes is `1 − 0.05^(1/n)`: **n = 3 ⟹ 0.632, n = 2 ⟹ 0.776.** At n = 2
the futility rule is very nearly blind, and §39.43(d) already pre-registered it as a catastrophe
detector rather than an estimator, so dropping to 2 takes the one property it still has.

**And I can add something they could not: the collision is contingent on a saving already queued.**
```
AS PRICED TODAY
  wave 1 @ 3 attempts alone          20,739 / 21,000   🔴 MARGIN 261 = 1.2%. It carries NOTHING
                                                          else — not even a route smoke.
  wave 1 @ 3 + MTD pilot             24,747            REFUSED
  wave 1 @ 2 + MTD pilot             17,834            fits
IF THE rcfc SAVING LANDS (queued for the next route smoke, §R39.17 §4 / §39.46)
  T21-se's Hessian recomputation moves out of the IRC jobs ⟹ their caps drop ~50%
  ⟹ T21-se ceiling ≈ 6,913 → ≈ 4,993        [ESTIMATE ON AN ESTIMATE — the Hessian fraction is a
                                              stacked LITERATURE 30-50%, never measured here]
  wave 1 @ 3 attempts               ≈ 14,979
  wave 1 @ 3 + MTD pilot            ≈ 18,987 / 21,000   🟢 FITS, margin 9.6%
⟹ 🟢 THE COLLISION MAY NEVER NEED THE TRIGGER TO FIRE. It exists only in the branch where BOTH
  stage 0 releases the pilot AND the rcfc saving has not landed.
🔴 NOT BANKED. Two stacked estimates and a code change that has not shipped. I am flagging a
  branch that may close itself, not removing the collision — and the 1.2% margin on the
  three-attempt-alone case stands either way and is the number that should worry someone.
```

## 4. proposer7's fourth control — accepted, and it is the one my own round demonstrates best

> *"An author's own spec is not a spec until it has been run against a case it could fail."*

🔒 Adopted as the fourth alongside §R39.25 §5's three. **The evidence is not only theirs.** G-SCAN-2
was falsified by the first path they tested it on; their Δ_shell violated a rule they had written
two paragraphs earlier; my 5-point bracket was an optimistically-biased sampling design that
survived until someone asked what it evaluated; my exponent inference divided by an anchor whose
provenance I had flagged twice. **Four specs, four authors' own rules, none caught by care and all
four caught by execution or by the other person.** The three controls in §R39.25 §5 are all
"put the label in the cell"; this fourth one is different in kind — it is a demand that the spec be
*run*, and it is the only one of the four that would have caught all four failures.

**Reported to**: team-lead (n = 1 reprice, the η survivorship field, and the contingent dissolution
of the wave-1 collision) and proposer7 (the free headroom at n = 1 and the η direction).

# §R39.28 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: the re-plan trigger gets a derivation, and applying proposer7's cross-Hamiltonian rule catches a defect in my own ladder

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `stack` = my per-SP unit-cost estimate (the `li_ec_cation` opt+freq
> anchor ÷ 20–40 optimisation cycles × the level3 route multipliers); `rung` = one member of the
> Li(EC)ₙ ladder; `CAP` = §R26.1's per-link ceiling, `cores × max_wall_h` = 64 × 48 = 3,072 core-h;
> `cliff` = the discontinuous doubling of a task's ceiling when its budget crosses CAP and `links`
> goes 1 → 2; `SP barrier` = a barrier computed from DFT single points along a GFN2 path.
> Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` for ceilings.

## 1. 🟢 proposer7's re-plan trigger — accepted, and 3× turns out to have a derivation

Their clause: *if the first rung's measured per-SP cost differs from the stack by more than ~3×,
the remaining rungs are re-planned before they are submitted, not after.* **Accepted. And the
number is better than a round figure — here is where the real discontinuities sit.**

```
IF THE MEASURED PER-SP COST IS f × MY STACK, the budgets scale by f and the ceilings follow —
until a task's budget crosses CAP = 3,072, at which point `links` goes 1 → 2 and its ceiling
DOUBLES INSTANTLY (§R26.1's stair-step, the defect I wrote and then walked into twice).
  n = 4 rung (budget 522)   CLIFF AT f = 3,072 / 522 = 5.9×
  n = 3 rung (budget 227)   CLIFF AT f = 3,072 / 227 = 13.5×
  n = 1, n = 2              no cliff in any plausible range (n = 1 is `min_wall`-clamped anyway)
ROUND-LEVEL TOLERANCE (3-rung ladder inside the bundled round, 15,349 / 21,000):
  f = 3    ladder ceiling 329 → 923      round 15,943   🟢 fits
  f = 10   ladder ceiling 329 → 3,002    round 18,022   🟢 fits
  f = 13   ladder ceiling 329 → 3,893    round 18,913   🟢 fits, margin 10%
  f = 13.6 n = 3 crosses CAP ⟹ 6,144     round 22,148   🔴 REFUSED — a 0.6× step in f flips it
```

```
🟢 ⟹ THE TRIGGER BELONGS AT f = 3, AND ITS REASON IS: IT IS HALF THE DISTANCE TO THE NEAREST CLIFF
  (5.9× at the n = 4 rung), which is the first point at which a re-plan stops being an edit to a
  budget field and becomes a TASK SPLIT. 🔒 A trigger placed by margin-to-the-nearest-
  discontinuity is arguable; one placed by feel is not, and this project has spent several rounds
  on the difference.
🔴 AND THE COST OF NOT HAVING IT, which is what makes it worth pre-registering rather than
  remembering: at f = 5 with no trigger, the n = 3 and n = 4 tasks are budgeted at 227 and 522
  against a true need of ~1,135 and ~2,610. They do not fail loudly — THEY CAP OUT AND RETURN
  NOTHING. ⟹ ~749 core-h of GUARANTEED-NULL SPEND, plus a round of latency, against a trigger
  that costs zero and is checkable the moment the first rung lands.
```

## 2. 🔴 Applying proposer7's new rule to my own item catches a defect in the SP barrier

Their rule, from G-SCAN v3: **no gate, criterion or derived value ever subtracts energies from two
different Hamiltonians** — the reverse scan is GFN2, the certified reactant is a DFT object, and
comparing their energies produces a number that every log calls successful. Same class as the C-8.1
grid seam.

**I applied it across §R39 and everything is clean except one thing, which is mine:**
```
Δ_shell                GFN2 barrier − GFN2 barrier.                          🟢 intra-GFN2. CLEAN.
SP ladder energies     DFT SP − DFT SP, on GFN2 GEOMETRIES.                  🟢 intra-DFT. CLEAN.
SP-vs-full calibration DFT-on-GFN2-geometry − DFT-on-DFT-geometry.           🟢 CLEAN — same
                       Hamiltonian, different geometries, and the geometry difference IS WHAT THE
                       CALIBRATION EXISTS TO MEASURE. Not the same defect.
🔴 THE SP BARRIER ITSELF   As I specified it, `barrier = E(top of GFN2 path) − E(reactant)`, and I
   never said WHICH reactant energy. If it takes the DFT-OPTIMISED certified reactant, then the
   barrier's two ends are geometry-inconsistent: THE REACTANT IS RELAXED AND THE TOP IS NOT.
   ⟹ THE SP BARRIER COMES OUT SYSTEMATICALLY TOO HIGH.
```

```
🟢 FIX, free, and it is the exact parallel of proposer7's v3 clause ("the certified reactant
  contributes the STRUCTURE and never an ENERGY"):
     BOTH ENDS OF AN SP BARRIER MUST COME FROM THE SAME PATH.
     Use the GFN2 path's own FIRST FRAME at DFT SP as the reactant reference. The certified
     reactant contributes the structure the path starts from, and no energy.
  Cost: ZERO — the 7-point spec already computes both endpoints, so the first frame's SP exists.
🔴 AND THE DIRECTION IS WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BEING "CONSERVATIVE". An unrelaxed top against a
  relaxed reactant biases the barrier HIGH ⟹ the rate LOW ⟹ NOT §0-h's optimistic direction, so it
  would not have tripped my usual alarm. But the ladder's PURPOSE is a DIFFERENCE across n, and the
  relaxation error GROWS WITH n — a 41-atom cluster has far more to relax than an 11-atom one.
  ⟹ A BIAS THAT IS SAFE IN EVERY INDIVIDUAL RUNG IS NOT SAFE IN THE QUANTITY THE LADDER EXISTS TO
  PRODUCE. That is the same shape as proposer7's own matched-method finding, one level down, and I
  would not have found it without their rule to run my own item against.
```

## 3. No cost impact from G-SCAN v3, confirmed

The gate still runs at GFN2, still costs one extra scan, and the refine pass is now decoupled into
its own §39.42(b) job. **The 168-of-ceiling cheap-probe total and the 15,349 / 21,000 round are
both unaffected.** §R39.26's precondition 2 now points at v3 rather than v2.
🔒 And I endorse their decision to stop avoiding the constant, on cost grounds as well as
methodological ones: **a hidden constant inside a proxy costs more than a visible one**, because the
proxy has to be re-derived every time someone doubts it and the constant does not. v1 measured the
wrong quantity and v2 was anti-correlated with the pathology; 0.05 eV, stated as half the project's
declared 0.1 eV sensitivity, is the first version anyone can argue with — and the separation on the
three measured cases (4× under / 10× over / 9× over) is not close at any of them.

## 4. 🔒 The round's control list, final form

proposer7's tally: two errors of theirs caught by measurement, two of mine caught by them, two of
theirs caught by coder11 reading before implementing, two lucky escapes. **None caught by the
author's own care.** Their conclusion — end the list with the two mechanisms that have a
demonstrated hit rate — is right, and §2 above is a fifth data point for it: **I found a defect in
my own item only by running someone else's rule against it.**

```
PASSIVE (catch a misread, cost ~0, necessary but never sufficient)
  1  unit-in-the-cell        raw-KNL vs reference · DEV BOX vs KNL with the κ bracket ·
                             work vs charged
  2  declare cores on every Item                    (ADR-110 — 16× on the guard, no physics)
  3  assert present, not defaulted                  (the under-reporting direction has no test)
  4  no cross-Hamiltonian subtraction                (proposer7, §39.49 — and it caught §2 above)
ACTIVE (demonstrated hit rate, and the only two that cost anything)
  5  run the spec against a case it could fail
  6  have it read by whoever has to implement it
🔒 Entries 1-4 are labels. Entries 5-6 are the only ones with a hit. That ordering should not be
  read as priority — 1-4 are free and 5-6 are not — but a plan that ships 1-4 and skips 5-6 has
  shipped the entries with a zero hit rate this round.
```

**Reported to**: proposer7 (the derived trigger, and the SP-barrier defect their rule caught) and
team-lead (the trigger as a pre-registered budget condition for coder11).
