# §R39.29 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: the `rcfc` smoke priced into this round, and 🔴 proposer7's floor-anchor flag exposes the largest unquantified item left in §R39

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `rcfc` = reading the Hessian from a checkpoint instead of
> recomputing it (`irc=(rcfc,…)` vs `irc=(calcfc,…)`); `route smoke` = a cheap job whose only
> purpose is to verify a route/deck works before anything relies on it; `[MEASURED, FLOOR]` = a
> measurement known to be a lower bound because an identified bias points upward (§39.33(e));
> `CREST` = the conformer-search stage; `maxpoints` = Gaussian's IRC step limit;
> `success-conditioned denominator` = proposer7's §39.51 name for a ratio that quietly loses the
> cases that failed. Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` for ceilings.

## 1. 🟢 The `rcfc` smoke rides this round — priced, and it is trivial

proposer7 is right that this is not a new decision: §39.43(c) already ruled rcfc rides *"the next
submission's route smoke"*, and this submission is the next one. **Priced so it can actually be put
in the Item list rather than remembered as an intention:**

```
DESIGN (cheapest that verifies the thing): the R-A single-ended attempt already runs
  ts_opt + freq, so a TS Hessian .chk EXISTS in that job. Add a SECOND, SHORT IRC job that reads
  it with `rcfc` and runs 3 points, and compare its first 3 IRC points against the `calcfc` IRC's
  first 3. 🔒 No extra Hessian is computed — that is the whole point of the design.
COST      3 IRC steps at 11 atoms ≈ 260 core-h × (3 / ~30 points)
          ⟹ 10 / 26 / 60 core-h  [ESTIMATE].  Budget = 60 (cap) · wall 0.94 h · ceiling 60.
ROUND     15,349 + 60 = 15,409 / 21,000  ⟹ 🟢 margin 26.6% (was 26.9%). Not a decision.
```
🟢 **And it dissolves the collision rather than banking a contingency**, exactly as proposer7 says:
with rcfc landed *before* wave 1, three attempts plus the MTD pilot is ~18,987 (9.6%). Their ruling
now has an explicit premise and a fallback I endorse — **if rcfc has not landed by then, take two
attempts plus the pilot rather than a three-attempt round with no room in it.** A round that cannot
carry the verification its own results depend on is worse than a weak futility rule.

## 2. 🔴🔴 THE FLOOR-ANCHOR FLAG — proposer7 is right, and I can say exactly where I am exposed

Their flag: *"the TS-attempt costs in that total rest on P1's 527.822, which §39.33(e) established
is `[MEASURED, FLOOR]` with its dominant identified bias pointing UP. A 1.2% margin against a
floor-anchored estimate is not a margin."* **Correct. Here is the exposure item by item, because
"everything is a floor" is not actionable and this is not uniform.**

```
T11-se (11 at, single-ended)   BUILT FROM STAGES, NOT FROM P1's TOTAL:
    ts_opt+freq  from P1's `ts_qst2` 267.822 × 0.5-1.5
    2×IRC        from P1's 125.707 + 134.293 = 260.000 × 0.6-1.5
    scan         GFN2, independent
  ⟹ 🟢 NOT EXPOSED TO THE CREST OMISSION — no CREST stage enters a single-ended attempt
    (§39.39(d) is scan → opt=ts → freq → IRC) and none enters my derivation.
T11-qst2 (11 at, double-ended)  BUILT FROM P1's TOTAL 527.822 × 1.0-1.5
  ⟹ 🔴 EXPOSED. P1's breakdown lists ts_qst2 / irc_forward / irc_reverse AND NOTHING ELSE —
    THERE IS NO CREST LINE IN IT, although `P1.sh` carries a `sei_stage crest` call. Either CREST
    did not run, or it ran and is missing from the breakdown. I do not know which and I am not
    guessing. If a QST2 attempt properly includes a conformer search, 527.822 is a floor for it.
🔴🔴 THE ONE THAT MATTERS FAR MORE — IRC TRUNCATION, and it reaches EVERY row I wrote:
    §R38.10 names IRC truncation as one of the two identified upward biases on the 302.4 anchor,
    and the SUPERSEDED table records that P1's FIRST round produced `n_frames = 1` per direction —
    an artefact (R33.5/ADR-066). THIS round's IRC cost 125.7 and 134.3 core-h, which is ~2 h each
    at 64 cores and looks substantial. 🔴 BUT I DO NOT KNOW THE FRAME COUNT, AND I DO NOT KNOW
    WHETHER IT TERMINATED ON CONVERGENCE OR ON `maxpoints`. I used 260.000 as a central value.
```

### What happens if the IRC anchor is a floor by a factor `t`

```
                       as priced      t = 2         t = 5
T11-se  2×IRC row        325           650         1,625
T11-se  TOTAL            662           987         1,962
T21-se  2×IRC row      3,120         6,240        15,600
T21-se  TOTAL          6,371         9,491        18,851
T21-se  CEILING        6,913        ~12,000      ~21,500  🔴 EXCEEDS THE GUARD ON ITS OWN
⟹ AT t = 5 A SINGLE PRODUCTION-SIZED TS ATTEMPT IS UNSUBMITTABLE. The ≤3-attempts-per-round
  ceiling (§R39.15 §5) becomes ≤1, and §R39.21's n = 3 verdict — already "not submittable" —

🔒 I am NOT claiming t > 1. I am claiming t IS UNMEASURED, that it multiplies the single largest

### 🟢 It is closable for free, and it is now the highest-value unread field in the project

READ FROM P1's EXISTING IRC OUTPUT (already in the tree, no compute):
  · number of IRC points per direction
  · termination reason — convergence vs `maxpoints` vs wall
TWO FIELDS. They decide whether every production-class number in §R39 is central or a floor.
🔴 THIS SUPERSEDES MY OWN "nothing outstanding on engineer7's side" FROM §R39.25. It was true of
  the questions I had asked. It was not true of the questions I should have asked — I took
  260.000 as central because it was `[MEASURED]` and did not check whether it was `[MEASURED,
  FLOOR]`, which is a distinction this document's own flush block spends a paragraph on.

## 3. 🟢 `success-conditioned denominator` — adopted, and the structural fix supersedes my two-field patch

proposer7's name and one-question test: **"if one case fails, what happens to my denominator?"**
Stays ⟹ fine. Shrinks ⟹ the ratio is conditioned on success and must say so in its own name.
It fired **four** times this round: U-56's rate over completed runs, the gate's spread over paths
that agreed, **my η over surviving tasks**, and their seed spread over seeds that produced a file.

```
🔒 THEIR STRUCTURAL FIX IS BETTER THAN MY TWO-FIELD CONVENTION AND SUPERSEDES IT. coder11 found it
  already implemented: `payload/P3.sh:63-73` writes the attempt list and creates every attempt
  directory BEFORE dispatch; `:134-141` iterates THAT LIST at collection and emits `rc: -1` where a
  result is missing rather than skipping it.
  ⟹ `n_attempted` is PRE-REGISTERED rather than observed, and cannot shrink after the fact.
  ⟹ MY TWO FIELDS ONLY WORK IF `n_attempted` IS ITSELF COUNTED FROM SOMETHING THAT SURVIVES
    FAILURE. Globbing outputs misses a dead task; globbing directories misses one that died before
    its directory existed. I specified the fields and not their provenance, which is the same
    defect one level down.
⟹ η's accounting adopts the P3 pattern: `n_tasks_attempted` comes from the pre-dispatch manifest,
  never from a glob. Free — the pattern is already in the tree and merely needs reusing.
```

## 4. Two items closed

```
🟢 n = 1 EXTRA HEADROOM — DECLINED by proposer7 and recorded as declined, so it is not re-offered
  later as a concession. 6 seeds, one basin, 0.0005 eV: more points buy resolution on a quantity
  already below any resolution the ladder can use. 🔒 Their sentence is the one to keep: FREE IS

🟢 THE 3× RE-PLAN TRIGGER — already placed with its derivation in §R39.28 §1 (3× is half the
  distance to the nearest §R26.1 cliff, 5.9× at the n = 4 rung). Their independent restatement of

# §R39.30 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: the relaxation term is half-free this round, and an n = 3 certification is priced so the refusal is a number

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `bias(n)` = the SP-vs-full-attempt barrier difference at ligand
> count n; `relaxation term` = the energy the SP convention does not take because its geometry is
> unoptimised; `E31` = a hypothetical endpoint certification at n = 3 (31 atoms); `CAP` = §R26.1's
> per-link ceiling 3,072 core-h. Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` for ceilings.

## 1. 🟢 Confirming proposer7's "partly free" — and it is exactly half, at the end that can be measured

With the §R39.28 §2 fix (both ends of an SP barrier from the same path), `bias(n)` decomposes:

```
bias(n) = [ E(top, SP)        − E(TS, optimised)      ]   ⟵ TS-END RELAXATION
        − [ E(first frame,SP) − E(reactant, certified) ]   ⟵ REACTANT-END RELAXATION
🟢 REACTANT END — FREE AND MEASURABLE IN THIS ROUND at n = 1 AND n = 2. Both energies are already
  bought: the SP first frame by the ladder, the certified reactant by R-A's in-flight endpoint
  (n = 1) and by E21 (n = 2, inside cut U56-2). ⟹ 0 core-h, 2 points, and it is the component
  whose GROWTH WITH n we can actually observe before wave 1.
🔴 TS END — NOT AVAILABLE. It needs a real TS optimisation, i.e. the full attempt: n = 1 has one in
  this round, n = 2 waits for T21-se in wave 1, and n = 3/4 never get one (§R39.21 §2).
⟹ THE LADDER GETS HALF ITS RELAXATION TERM AT TWO RUNGS THIS ROUND, FOR NOTHING. That is more
  early calibration than §R39.21 §3b allowed for, and it does not change §3b's conclusion — one
  full calibration point until wave 1 — because half a term at two rungs is not a bias.
```

proposer7 declined to buy certifications at n = 3/4 on judgement. **The number supports them and is

# §R39.31 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: 🔴🔴 the IRC truncation is CONFIRMED — and it is a GATE failure before it is a cost failure. The cost fix is ~6% of an attempt, not 2–5×.

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `IRC` = intrinsic reaction coordinate; `maxpoints=30` = Gaussian's
> explicit step limit in the shipped route `irc=(calcfc,forward/reverse,maxpoints=30)`;
> `t` = the factor by which a converged IRC's point count exceeds 30; `C-2` = the coder constraint
> requiring a two-directional IRC verdict; `U-56a` = the binary feasibility gate that unblocks S3;
> `indeterminate` = C-2's honest third verdict, which supplies a denominator for U-56b but does NOT
> close U-56a (§39.39(f)); `terminal opt` = a plain geometry optimisation started from the last IRC
> point. Units: raw-KNL core-h.

## 1. Confirmed from the raw logs (lead, source read — not inference)

```
irc_forward.log   "Total number of points: 30"  — EXACTLY maxpoints. Energy 0.00000 → −0.00526 Ha,
                  monotonically falling, STILL FALLING STEEPLY AT POINT 30. No plateau.
irc_reverse.log   same, −0.00542 → 0.00000, same shape, no plateau.
route             irc=(calcfc,forward/reverse,maxpoints=30), level2, stage wall 7071/7554 s
                  = 125.7 / 134.3 core-h — EXACTLY the numbers I quoted.
🔒 "Normal termination" is a LINK exit status. The IRC did not stop because it reached a stationary
   point; it stopped because it ran out of allotted steps. Had G16 converged early it would have
   stopped before 30.
```

## 2. 🔴🔴 REFRAMING — and this is the part that matters more than the cost

**`260.000 core-h` is not a floor. It is an EXACT measurement of a 30-point IRC.** What is a floor
is a *converged* IRC, which is a different job. That distinction changes what is broken:

```
🔴 A 30-POINT TRUNCATED IRC CANNOT SATISFY U-56's OWN CONDITIONS, BY CONSTRUCTION.
  §39.39(d)'s verification: "the IRC's reverse endpoint must match the INDEPENDENTLY certified
  reactant (different job, different route) within the RMSD tolerance."
  An IRC that stops with the energy still falling steeply HAS NO ENDPOINT TO COMPARE. The honest
  verdict is C-2's `indeterminate` — and §39.39(f) is explicit that `indeterminate` supplies a
  denominator for U-56b but DOES NOT CLOSE U-56a.
⟹ 🔴 IF U56-2's ATTEMPTS INHERIT `maxpoints=30`, EVERY ONE OF THEM RETURNS `indeterminate`, U-56a
  STAYS OPEN, AND THE ROUND BUYS COST DATA AND NO GATE.
🔒 THAT IS THE FAILURE CLASS THAT KILLED P1 — a run that terminates normally, produces numbers, and
  cannot count in either direction. It is currently sitting in the shipped route as an explicit
  config value, and it would have been discovered after the compute was spent.
```

🔴 **And the lead is right that my "insulated" wording needs correcting.** §R39.29 said T11-se is not
exposed **to the CREST omission**, which is true, and separately flagged IRC truncation as reaching
"every row I wrote", which is also true — but the two sentences sat close enough together to read as
"T11-se is safe". **It is not. The truncation is a property of the ROUTE, not of P1's execution, so
any new single-ended IRC using the same `maxpoints=30` reproduces it exactly.** Stated
unambiguously here because the favourable-direction misread is the one this document's own flush
block predicts.

## 3. 🟢 The cost fix — and it is ~6% of an attempt, not the 2–5× I projected

A converged IRC is the expensive answer. It is **not the only one**, and the cheap one is standard
practice: **an IRC does not have to run to convergence to establish connection — it has to reach the
BASIN of the certified endpoint, after which a plain optimisation confirms identity.**

```
per-IRC-point cost   260.000 / 60 points = 4.33 core-h/point at 11 atoms, level2  [MEASURED]
t (points needed)    UNKNOWN. The forward direction descended 0.143 eV in 30 points and is still
                     falling; R-A's GFN2 ΔE_rxn is −0.317 eV, so ~half the DESCENT remains and MORE
                     than half the POINTS do (IRC steps shorten near a minimum). [ESTIMATE] t = 2-5.

OPTION A — CONVERGED IRC (raise maxpoints)                11 atoms       21 atoms
  IRC row at t = 2 / 3 / 5                            650/975/1,625   6,240/9,360/15,600
  T11-se / T21-se TOTAL                               987-1,962       9,491-18,851
  🔴 at t = 5 the 21-atom attempt's ceiling is ~21,500 — UNSUBMITTABLE ALONE.

OPTION B — 30-POINT IRC + TERMINAL OPT PER DIRECTION       ⟵ RECOMMENDED
  IRC 30 points (unchanged)                    325            3,120
  + 2 terminal opts (endpoint-class, 7.5-41)   15-82          144-788   (× S₂₁ = 9.6)
  IRC STAGE TOTAL                              340-407        3,264-3,908
  T11-se / T21-se TOTAL                        ~677-744       ~6,098-6,742
🟢 ⟹ T21-se STAYS AT ~6,371 BASE. THE CURRENT NUMBER SURVIVES. Option B costs ~6% of an attempt;
  Option A costs 50-200%. The ≤3-production-attempts-per-round ceiling, the Δ_shell economics and
  §R39.21's n = 3 verdict ALL SURVIVE UNCHANGED under Option B and NONE of them survive Option A
  at t = 5.
CEILING   the terminal opt rides INSIDE the IRC job (sequential, the two-stage endpoint pattern of
  R38.12 §3). Add ~10% to the IRC job's cap ⟹ T21-se ceiling 6,913 → ~7,100. Round: immaterial.
```

```
🔴 OPTION B'S WEAKNESS, STATED BECAUSE IT IS A REAL ONE AND THE CHOICE IS NOT MINE: a terminal opt
  can relax to a DIFFERENT minimum than the IRC would have reached, and near a bifurcation it
  probably would. It is a weaker claim than a converged IRC. 🟢 But it is FALSIFIABLE in the useful
  direction — if the opt lands anywhere other than the certified reactant, that IS the finding, and
  §39.39(d) already treats a non-matching reverse endpoint as informative rather than as noise.
🔒 WHETHER OPTION B SATISFIES C-2 IS A SCIENCE RULING AND IT IS proposer7's. I have priced both and
  I am recommending B on cost, with its weakness attached — not judging whether it is admissible.
⚠ AND A THIRD OPTION EXISTS THAT I AM NOT PRICING AS PRIMARY: raise `maxpoints` ONLY for the R-A
  attempt (the U-56a gate case, 11 atoms, cheapest) and use Option B everywhere else. That buys one
  fully-converged IRC as a calibration of Option B's own error, for ~1,300 core-h at 11 atoms.
  🟢 Same shape as the SP ladder's calibration, and it is the cheapest way to make B defensible.
```

## 4. What this changes, immediately

```
🔴 CODER11, GATE-BLOCKING, NOT COSMETIC: `maxpoints=30` must not be inherited by U56-2's IRC jobs
  as-is. Either raise it (Option A) or add the terminal opt (Option B). Shipping it unchanged
  produces a round of `indeterminate` verdicts and leaves U-56a open. This outranks every other

🔴 §R39.2's IRC ROW IS RELABELLED: `156 / 325 / 546` is EXACT for a 30-point IRC and a FLOOR for a
  converged one. Both statements go in the cell. Under Option B the row becomes 340 / 407 / ~600

🟢 UNCHANGED UNDER OPTION B: cut U56-2 (1,281 / 3,514 / 5,257), T21-se 6,371, Δ_shell = one T21-se,
  ≤3 production attempts per round, the n = 3 submission limit, the bundled round 15,409 / 21,000.
🔴 UNDER OPTION A AT t = 5, NONE OF THOSE SURVIVE. The choice between A and B is therefore not a

## 5. 🔒 The self-account, because this one was mine to catch and I did not

I quoted `125.707 + 134.293 = 260.000` from the review log in §R39.2 and used it as a central value
through eleven subsections. **The route string containing `maxpoints=30` was one field away, in the

   A COST FIGURE IS A MEASUREMENT OF WHATEVER THE ROUTE ACTUALLY DID. Reading the number without

# §R39.32 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: 🔴 the amended C-2 collides with my Option B, and that collision decides whether S3 production is affordable at all

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `C-2` / `condition 7` = the coder constraint and §39.32(g) condition
> requiring a two-directional IRC verdict, amended by proposer7's §39.53 so that termination by
> `maxpoints` ⟹ `indeterminate`; `Option A` / `Option B` = §R39.31's converged-IRC and
> 30-points-plus-terminal-opt designs; `|ν_imag|` = the magnitude of the transition state's single
> imaginary frequency, measured by the `freq` step that runs immediately before the IRC;
> `t` = the factor by which a completed IRC's point count exceeds 30; `K` = the constant in
> proposer7's proposed `maxpoints ∝ 1/|ν_imag|` sizing rule. Units: raw-KNL core-h.

## 1. 🔴🔴 THE COLLISION — and our messages crossed, so proposer7 has not yet seen Option B

```

                   "every future TS attempt must budget for a COMPLETED IRC"
my §R39.31:        OPTION B = keep 30 points + a TERMINAL OPT per direction, ~6% of an attempt
🔴 UNDER THE AMENDED CONDITION 7 AS WRITTEN, OPTION B STILL TERMINATES BY `maxpoints` AND THEREFORE
  STILL RETURNS `indeterminate`. The terminal opt is not an IRC step and the rule does not mention
  it. ⟹ Option B is dead unless condition 7 gains a clause for it.
🔒 THIS IS NOT A DISAGREEMENT — IT IS A CROSSING. proposer7 wrote the amendment before my Option B
  arrived. THEY MUST RULE WITH OPTION B IN FRONT OF THEM, because the two are not independent:
  one is a chemistry condition and the other is the only affordable way to satisfy its intent.
```

**Why this is the single most consequential open decision in §R39, stated as arithmetic:**

| | Option B (if condition 7 admits it) | Option A (completed IRC) at t = 2 |
|---|---|---|
| T11-se | ~677–744 | 987 |
| T21-se | ~6,371 | 9,491 |
| T21-se ceiling | ~7,100 | **15,360** (IRC 3,120/direction > CAP 3,072 ⟹ links 2 ⟹ 6,144 each) |
| production attempts per round | **≤ 3** | 🔴 **≤ 1** (2 × 15,360 = 30,720 ≫ 21,000) |
| S3 wave 1 | 3 attempts, one round | 🔴 1 attempt, one round |
| separating p = 0.2 from p = 0.5 | 5–10 rounds (§R39.15 §6) | 🔴 **15–20 rounds** |

🔴 **At Option A the futility rule's `n` falls to 1 per round and the S3 schedule stops being a

## 2. 🟢 proposer7's `1/|ν_imag|` predictor is the way out, and it is better than either option

Their observation: P1's TS mode is **−48.4 cm⁻¹**, very soft, so the IRC's initial steps are tiny
and each point covers little energy. Points-to-completion scale inversely with `|ν_imag|`, **and
`|ν_imag|` is measured by the `freq` step that runs immediately before the IRC.**

```
🔴 FIRST CONSEQUENCE, AND IT UNDERMINES MY OWN ANCHOR IN A WAY I HAVE TO STATE: −48.4 cm⁻¹ IS
  UNUSUALLY SOFT. A C–O cleavage TS is typically 200-800 cm⁻¹. ⟹ MY ONLY IRC ANCHOR COMES FROM
  WHAT IS PLAUSIBLY THE SOFTEST-MODE CASE IN THE PROJECT, and I have been propagating its point
  count to every other reaction.
  · as a POINT COUNT it is unrepresentatively HIGH  (a 300 cm⁻¹ TS needs ~6× fewer points)
  · as a TOTAL COST it is unrepresentatively LOW    (it was truncated at 30)
  🔒 TWO ERRORS OF OPPOSITE SIGN AND I CANNOT DETERMINE THE NET. Stated as an open uncertainty
  rather than resolved by picking whichever direction is convenient.
⚠ AND A CHEMISTRY FLAG I AM RAISING ONLY BECAUSE IT HAS A COST FACE: if the mode is soft BECAUSE
  IT IS THE WRONG MODE, then the IRC's expense is a SYMPTOM OF A WRONG SADDLE, not a cost to
  budget for. Ω is the instrument for that and it is uncalibrated (U-57). proposer7's call, not
  mine — but "budget more for the IRC" and "this saddle is wrong" are not the same response.
```

### 🟢 The design that follows, and it is the cheapest gate left in §R39

```
🔒 SIZE `maxpoints` PER REACTION FROM THE MEASURED |ν_imag|, NOT FROM A CONSTANT — proposer7's
   proposal, and for pricing it does something better than reduce the cost: IT CONVERTS `t` FROM AN
   UNKNOWN FLAT MULTIPLIER ON THE WHOLE S3 POOL INTO A PER-REACTION BUDGET WITH A MEASURED INPUT.
   A flat t = 2 across the pool is catastrophic (§1). A per-reaction budget is not, because most
   production TSs are stiffer than R-A's.
🔒 AND THE GUARD IS SATISFIED WITHOUT A DYNAMIC CEILING, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT SHIPPABLE:
   plan-time BUDGET = the worst plausible |ν_imag| (⟹ the ceiling the guard checks)
   run-time SPEND   = whatever the measured |ν_imag| actually needs
   That is exactly how every cap in this document already behaves. No new machinery.
🟢 NEW GATE, and it is the fifth instance of the round's own pattern — a free measurement one stage
  earlier deciding whether to fund the expensive stage:
     THE `freq` STEP MEASURES |ν_imag| BEFORE THE IRC IS FUNDED. IF |ν_imag| IS BELOW THE THRESHOLD
     AT WHICH A COMPLETED IRC FITS THE PER-DIRECTION CAP, DO NOT SPEND THE IRC — RECORD
     `indeterminate, mode too soft to complete within budget` AND STOP.
  COST AVOIDED PER FIRING   the entire IRC stage: ~325 core-h at 11 atoms, ~3,120 at 21.
  COST TO IMPLEMENT         a comparison against a number the freq step already prints. FREE.
  🔴 THRESHOLD: derived from the BUDGET, not from chemistry. At 21 atoms a 3,072 per-direction cap
     buys ~74 points at 4.33 × S₂₁ core-h/point. The |ν_imag| that needs ≤74 points is unknown
     until `K` is calibrated — SAME CALIBRATION proposer7 already requires, on the first two
     completed IRCs. ⟹ ONE calibration serves both the sizing rule and the gate.
```

# §R39.33 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: B+ priced. It costs the third production attempt per round — unless the `rcfc` saving lands first.

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `B+` = proposer7's §39.55 upgrade of Option B — 30-point IRC plus

> agreement establishing the connection and disagreement returning `indeterminate`;
> `Option A` = a converged IRC (raise `maxpoints`); `terminal opt` = a plain geometry optimisation
> started from an IRC point; `rcfc` = reading the TS Hessian from a checkpoint instead of
> recomputing it in each IRC direction. Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` for ceilings.

## 1. B+ priced — +15% per attempt at both sizes

```
terminal opt, endpoint-class   7.5 – 41 core-h at 11 atoms  [ESTIMATE, R38.13]  × S₂₁ 9.6 at 21
B+ = 4 opts per attempt (2 per direction), against Option B's 2.

at 11 atoms and +15% at 21. proposer7's "~12%" was close and the difference is rounding, not
disagreement. Against Option A's +50–200%, this is the cheap answer by an order of magnitude.

Their §39.55 §5 lists "≤3 production attempts" among what B+ protects. **It does not, at today's
prices.** The ceiling, not the spend, is what decides it:

                          IRC × 2, each carrying one direction + 2 terminal opts:

🔴 AND THAT LANDS ON proposer7's OWN FUTILITY RULE, in the exact way they refused for the MTD pilot:
   0 of 3 leaves p's 95% upper bound at 0.632; 0 of 2 leaves 0.776. They declined to drop to n = 2
   for the pilot's sake and B+ takes the same attempt for its own sake.

### 🟢 The resolution, and it makes an item already in this round load-bearing

```
WITH THE `rcfc` SAVING LANDED, the Hessian recomputation leaves both IRC directions:
  IRC base per direction 1,560 → ~780 · + opts 465/2 ⟹ ~1,012 ⟹ cap 1,152 each ⟹ 2,304
  T21-se CEILING = 0.5 + 3,072 + 2,304 = 5,377
  3 × 5,377 = 16,131 / 21,000   🟢 ≤ 3 SURVIVES, margin 23%.
🔒 ⟹ B+ AND ≤3 PRODUCTION ATTEMPTS ARE COMPATIBLE IF AND ONLY IF `rcfc` LANDS FIRST. That is a HARD

  to U-56 — but "B+ agreed with a converged IRC on two reactions with different coordinates"
  (R-A alkyl C–O, R-B carbonyl C–O) is a materially stronger statement than one reaction, and it
  is the SELECTIVITY pair, i.e. the case most likely to bifurcate.
⟹ OFFERED, NOT RECOMMENDED — the science of whether a second calibration point is worth 1,280 of
  ceiling is proposer7's. What I can say is that it is AFFORDABLE, which is not obvious from the
  ruling's framing, and that R-B is the reaction where a bifurcation is most likely to show up.
```

# §R39.35 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: 🔴 SELF-CORRECTION — my anchor-free IRC row omitted the `calcfc` Hessian. The `rcfc` precondition is REINSTATED; proposer7's ruling stands.

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `calcfc` = compute the Hessian at the start of the run (what the
> shipped IRC route does, **once per direction**); `rcfc` = read it from a checkpoint instead;
> `path gradients` = the per-point SCF+gradient evaluations along the IRC; `B+` = §39.55's
> two-terminal-opts-per-direction design; `Ω gate` = §39.56's rule that an IRC is not funded when
> the imaginary mode's projection onto the intended break coordinate is below the floor.
> Units: raw-KNL core-h, `charged` for ceilings.

## 1. 🔴 The error, and it is the same class I have been cataloguing

§R39.34 re-derived the IRC row from `li_ec_cation`'s per-cycle cost × a literature point count.
**That derivation counts PATH GRADIENTS ONLY. It silently omits the `calcfc` Hessian that the
shipped route computes once per direction.**

```
🔴 ⟹ §R39.34's "IRC pair, 21 atoms = 115 / 960 / 6,624" IS THE `rcfc` NUMBER. I published it as
  the general number and then used it to withdraw the `rcfc` precondition — which is circular:
  I removed the dependency by quietly assuming the thing it depended on.
🔒 THE CLASS IS THE ONE I NAMED TWO SECTIONS AGO AND THEN COMMITTED: "a cost figure is a
  measurement of whatever the route actually did." I re-derived a component and did not check
  which job my new derivation describes. Third instance this round, first one that is mine twice.
```

**Corrected. The Hessian is a separate, large term (§R39.15 §4: 40–130 core-h at 11 atoms,
280–1,716 at 21) and whether it appears is exactly what `rcfc` decides:**

| IRC pair (both directions), base | 11 atoms | 21 atoms |
|---|---|---|
| **without `rcfc`** (2 × Hessian + 2 × path) | **270** | **2,360** |
| **with `rcfc`** (2 × path only) | 100 | 960 |
| saving from `rcfc` | 170 | **1,400** |

🟢 **The `rcfc` saving of ~1,400 core-h per 21-atom attempt independently reproduces §R39.17 §4's
~1,630 estimate, which was derived a completely different way (a Hessian-fraction argument on the
tight-from-guess total).** Two independent routes to the same number — the mechanism proposer7 and
I have been calling the only one that tells you a finding is real.

## 2. 🟢 ⟹ proposer7's ruling #1 STANDS. My §R39.34 withdrawal is RETRACTED.

```
T21-se, base            without rcfc 6,542   ·   with rcfc 5,142
T21-se, CEILING
  without rcfc   IRC/direction base 1,180 + opts 465 = 1,645 ⟹ cap 2,048 each ⟹ 4,096
                 + ts_opt+freq 3,072 + scan 0.5 = 7,169
                 3 × 7,169 = 21,507  >  21,000   🔴 ≤ 2 ATTEMPTS
  with rcfc      IRC/direction 480 + 465 = 945 ⟹ cap 1,536 each ⟹ 3,072
                 + 3,072 + 0.5 = 6,145
                 3 × 6,145 = 18,435 / 21,000     🟢 ≤ 3 ATTEMPTS, margin 12%
```
🔒 **`rcfc` IS a precondition for ≤3 production attempts per round, and therefore for the futility
rule's operating characteristic.** proposer7's framing is right and mine was wrong twice — first
by pricing without it, then by "withdrawing" a dependency I had removed by assumption.
⟹ **the 60 core-h route smoke, already in this round, is load-bearing for the calendar.** If it
fails it costs the third attempt every round, which doubles the rounds needed to separate
`p = 0.2` from `p = 0.5`.

## 3. 🟢 proposer7's fourth-stage split — priced, and it is better than a saving

Their argument, which is mine one stage later and which I did not apply: *the 3-job split exists so
a failed TS optimisation never pays for the IRC; a truncated or indeterminate IRC should likewise
never pay for the terminal opts.*

```
CEILING: NEUTRAL. IRC jobs tighten from a 1,536 cap (which had to carry the opts) to 1,024, and the
  opts get their own 1,024 ⟹ 2,048 + 1,024 = 3,072, IDENTICAL to the combined design.
  🔒 So the quantisation neither helps nor hurts — proposer7 was right not to assume it did.
EXPECTED SAVING: P(IRC caps out or returns indeterminate) × 465 core-h/attempt at 21 atoms.
  At 25% that is ~116 core-h/attempt, ~350 per production round. Real but second-order.
🟢 THE ACTUAL REASON TO TAKE IT IS CORRECTNESS, NOT COST: under the amended condition 7, AN IRC
  THAT CAPS OUT IS `indeterminate` — SO ITS TERMINAL OPTS ARE WORTHLESS BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT MERELY
  WASTED. Paying for them is paying for a computation whose input is already known to be invalid.
⟹ ADOPT. FINAL CHAIN, four stages and three free gates:
     scan → ts_opt+freq → [Ω GATE] → IRC → [COMPLETION GATE] → terminal opts (B+)
  Each gate is a comparison against a number the previous stage already emits. Cost of all three: 0.
```

## 4. 🔴 A finding that falls out of the cap arithmetic: my IRC cap and `maxpoints` are the same constraint

```
An IRC stopped by `maxpoints=30` is truncated ⟹ `indeterminate` (amended condition 7).
An IRC stopped by ITS WALL CAP is ALSO truncated ⟹ ALSO `indeterminate`.
🔴 ⟹ SETTING THE IRC's WALL CAP BELOW WHAT COMPLETION NEEDS IS EXACTLY EQUIVALENT TO SETTING
  `maxpoints` TOO LOW. Two names, one constraint, and only one of them was being discussed.
⟹ THE CAP MUST BE SIZED TO COMPLETE, OR THE ATTEMPT IS PRE-DOOMED — a cap set for budget tidiness
  silently converts a fundable attempt into a guaranteed `indeterminate`.
🟢 AND THAT IS THE SECOND, BETTER REASON `rcfc` MATTERS: it halves the per-direction cost, so a
  cap that is GENEROUS enough to complete still fits inside ≤3 attempts. Without it the choice is
  generous caps at ≤2 attempts, or ≤3 attempts with caps that will truncate some of them.
🔴 RESIDUAL, STATED NOT HIDDEN: at the pessimistic point count (3,312/direction) even the generous
  cap truncates. Any cap is a bet on an unmeasured count — but a cap-out returns
  `budget_exhausted` WITH THE COUNT REACHED, which is the missing datum. It fails loudly and it
  fails informatively, which is the best available property for a bet.
```

## 5. R-B calibration — taken, conditional, and not committed yet

```
🟢 TAKEN by proposer7, and their reason is better than mine: R-A and R-B SHARE A REACTANT and
  differ only in which bond breaks ⟹ IF A BIFURCATION EXISTS IN THIS SYSTEM IT IS WHERE THE TWO
  CHANNELS DIVERGE ⟹ R-B is not a second easy data point, it is THE CASE B+ IS MOST LIKELY TO
  FAIL ON. That is control #5 (run the spec against a case it could fail) applied to a ruling
  rather than to a spec.
⚠ CONDITIONAL ON Ω — if R-B's saddle returns Ω below the floor its IRC is not funded and there is
  no calibration to buy. 🔒 I AM NOT TREATING THE +1,280 CEILING AS COMMITTED until Ω returns, and
  the round's margin is quoted both ways: 17,201 without it, 18,481 with.
🔴 AND THE CORRECTION TO MY OWN EXPOSURE FRAMING, WHICH proposer7 IS RIGHT ABOUT: the R-B
  calibration reduces the PROBABILITY of the ~2,300 core-h bet, NOT ITS SIZE — both calibrations
  and all three non-gate attempts ride the same submission, so nothing can be sequenced between
  them. "We added a second calibration" reads like risk reduction; it is probability reduction.
```

## 6. Naming, because three uses is the threshold

proposer7 is right that a pattern used three times without a name gets re-derived a fourth time by
someone who did not read the sections. Both earned it this round:
```
HIERARCHICAL-WITH-OVERLAP   buy the expensive method ONCE where it is affordable, run the cheap one
  on the SAME case, let the overlap calibrate.  Uses: the SP ladder (n = 1, 2), B+ (R-A and now
  R-B), the `maxpoints` sizing rule.
SELF-REFERENTIAL-INSTEAD-OF-IMPORTED   define a tolerance from a quantity the run itself measures,
  never from a constant carried in.  Uses: G-SCAN v3, B+'s two-start-point agreement, `maxpoints`
  from |ν_imag| (mechanism kept, calibration withdrawn with its anchor).
🔒 A THIRD IS NOW ALSO AT THREE AND IS MINE TO NAME, since all three instances were cost items:
  GATE-BEFORE-YOU-PAY — a free comparison against a number the PREVIOUS stage already emits,
  placed immediately before the expensive stage. Uses: the reverse-scan gate before the DFT
  attempt, the Ω gate before the IRC, the completion gate before the terminal opts. Cost of all
  three: zero. Combined avoided spend: ~660 + ~1,891 + ~465 per 21-atom attempt.
```

**Reported to**: proposer7 (the retraction, the corrected table, the fourth-stage adoption) and
team-lead (`rcfc` is a precondition again — my withdrawal one message ago was wrong).

# §R39.36 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: FINAL. 🔴 A live crossed-ruling error on `rcfc`, the two-sided `ts_opt+freq` bracket, and what engineer8 inherits.

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `engineer8` = my successor; `two-sided` = an uncertainty whose
> direction is unknown, as opposed to one known to bias low or high; `role` = a distinct thing a
> single computation is being relied on to supply; `ill-conditioned Hessian` = one with many
> near-zero eigenvalues, which slows quasi-Newton convergence. Units: raw-KNL core-h.

## 1. 🔴🔴 READ THIS FIRST — A LIVE ERROR IS IN FLIGHT BETWEEN TWO DOCUMENTS

```
§39.57(a)  proposer7 RULED `rcfc` a precondition for S3's schedule.        ← CORRECT
§R39.34    I withdrew that dependency.                                     ← WRONG (my error:
           the anchor-free IRC row omitted the `calcfc` Hessian, so it was silently the `rcfc`
           number, and I removed the dependency by assuming the thing it depended on)
§R39.35    I RETRACTED the withdrawal. `rcfc` IS a precondition.           ← CORRECT, CURRENT
§39.58(b)  proposer7 marked their own §39.57(a) SUPERSEDED on the strength
           of my §R39.34 — BEFORE §R39.35 reached them.                    ← 🔴 RESTS ON MY ERROR
```
🔴 **`02_METHOD_SPEC.md` §39.58(b) currently carries a superseded-block on a ruling that was right.
It must be un-superseded.** The live position is §R39.35: without `rcfc`, T21-se's ceiling is 7,169
and `3 × 7,169 = 21,507 > 21,000` ⟹ **≤2 production attempts**; with `rcfc`, 6,145 ⟹ **≤3**.
🔒 **The 60 core-h `rcfc` route smoke in this round is load-bearing for the calendar.** If coder11's
queue was re-prioritised downward on my §R39.34, restore it.

⚠ **And the shape is worth naming for whoever reads this next**: proposer7's §39.57(a) was *sound,
load-bearing and wrong at once*, because the ceiling under it had been computed from a lithium hop
— their own words, arriving at their own ruling. Mine was the mirror: sound arithmetic on a
component whose job I had not checked. **Two people, two correct chains of reasoning, one wrong
number underneath each.**

## 2. `ts_opt+freq` — carried two-sided, and that is a harder input, not a softer one

proposer7 is right that my "plausibly low" was one-sided reasoning. Their counter-mechanism is real
and P1's own numbers support it: a spectator saddle sits in a **flat** region (mode −48.4 cm⁻¹ with
neighbouring real modes at 36.7 and 96.7), an ill-conditioned Hessian slows quasi-Newton
convergence, and **converging onto a shallow hop may cost MORE cycles, not fewer.**

```
WAS   267.822 × 1.25 × [0.5 – 1.5]   ⟹ 147 / 335 / 563   (11 atoms)
NOW   267.822 × 1.25 × [0.33 – 3.0]  ⟹ 110 / 335 / 1,005 — TWO-SIDED, magnitude unbounded
  [ESTIMATE. The bracket is widened to reflect two live mechanisms of opposite sign; it is NOT a
   measurement of either. Base is unchanged because neither mechanism is favoured.]
```

| T21-se (with `rcfc`) | opt | base | pess |
|---|---|---|---|
| previously | 1,444 | 5,142 | 15,752 |
| **two-sided** | 1,185 | **5,142** | **21,586** 🔴 |

```
🔴 THE PESSIMISTIC TAIL NOW EXCEEDS THE ROUND GUARD ON ITS OWN. The BASE does not move, and the
  CEILING does not move (caps are caps) — so ≤3 production attempts survives the SUBMISSION test
  unchanged. What falls is the PROBABILITY THAT ALL THREE COMPLETE, and I cannot quantify it:
  `ts_opt+freq`'s base (3,216 at 21 atoms) already brushes its own 3,072 cap in design A.
🔒 ⟹ THE HONEST STATEMENT FOR WAVE-1 SIZING: ≤3 is a submission fact, not a completion forecast.
  Anyone planning three completed barriers per round is planning against a number that has never
  been measured on a correct saddle.
```

## 3. 🟢 R-A carries five roles — and the hedge is already funded

proposer7's count: the U-56a gate · the `ts_opt+freq` anchor · the IRC point count · the
terminal-opt anchor · the `1/|ν_imag|` calibration (six with B+'s). **If R-A returns Ω below the
floor or fails to converge, five things are lost in one job.**

```
🟢 THE HEDGE COSTS NOTHING AND IS ALREADY IN THE ROUND. R-B is 11 atoms, funded, and under
  §39.57(b) it also receives a converged IRC. ⟹ ROLES 2-5 TRANSFER INTACT to R-B. R-A and R-B
  stop being only the selectivity pair and become a REDUNDANT ANCHORING PAIR at zero marginal cost.
🔴 ROLE 1 DOES NOT TRANSFER AUTOMATICALLY — U-56a needs a success under all eight conditions, so
  R-B carries the gate only if its own Ω, IRC and B+ all pass. If R-A fails, "can R-B carry the
  gate" is the FIRST question, not an improvisation. Still zero extra spend; it is an ordering.
🟢 AND THE FREE MEASUREMENT proposer7 ASKS FOR IS ONE I SHOULD HAVE ASKED FOR: report roles 2-5's
  anchor values PER REACTION, NEVER POOLED. If R-A and R-B disagree by more than ~2× on point count
  or cycle count, that disagreement IS A MEASUREMENT OF REACTION-TO-REACTION SPREAD — 🔴 the

# §R39.37 — engineer7, 2026-08-20: postscript — budget-made nulls close a FEEDBACK LOOP on S3's own sizing rule

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `U-56b` = the per-attempt TS success fraction and cost distribution,
> measured during S3 wave 1; `p` = that fraction; `1/p` = the multiplier S3's sizing rule applies to
> get from barriers-needed to attempts-to-fund; `indeterminate` = C-2's third verdict;
> `budget-class indeterminate` = one produced by a cap rather than by chemistry.
> Units: raw-KNL core-h.

proposer7's §39.59 §3 states the corollary of my §R39.35 §4 — if caps manufacture `indeterminate`s,
U-56b is partly measuring our own budget policy. **Correct, and there is a cost-side consequence
one step further out that is mine to name, because the sizing rule is a budget artefact.**

```
🔴 THE LOOP:
   caps set too tight  ⟹ more budget-class `indeterminate`s
                       ⟹ measured p falls
                       ⟹ 1/p rises  (S3 sizes attempts as barriers-needed × 1/p)
                       ⟹ S3 looks MORE expensive
                       ⟹ pressure to tighten caps  ⟹ back to the top.
🔒 EVERY STEP LOOKS LIKE A CHEMISTRY FINDING AND NONE OF THEM IS. The loop is closed entirely
  through numbers this project would report as measurements of the reaction class.
```

**The error direction is the one we have NOT been guarding**: every other bias we chased this round
pointed at an **overrun**. This one points at **concluding the project is unaffordable when it may
not be** — a scope-killing direction. §39.43(d) already limits what the futility rule may claim;
this is the same hazard reaching the sizing rule, where nothing limits it.

```
🟢 FIX — proposer7's field, and it is already free: every `indeterminate` carries its CAUSE, and
   the two classes tally separately.
     CHEMICAL   Ω below floor · B+ disagreement · IRC connects the wrong pair      = A RESULT
     BUDGET     maxpoints · wall cap · cumulative budget · maxcycles               = A PURCHASE
   U-56b is computed over attempts ALLOWED TO COMPLETE, with the budget-truncated count reported
   ALONGSIDE and never folded in.
🟢 ADDING THE COST-SIDE HALF, which is mine: **`1/p` MAY ONLY BE COMPUTED FROM THE CHEMICAL CLASS.**
   A sizing multiplier derived from a denominator that includes budget-class nulls is a multiplier
   we set ourselves, and it would arrive labelled as a property of the chemistry.
🟢 AND THE FREE DIAGNOSTIC proposer7 NAMES IS A COST INSTRUMENT AS MUCH AS A SCIENCE ONE:
     a large BUDGET class  ⟹ THE CAPS ARE WRONG — an engineering finding, and an actionable one,
                             because caps are the one input we fully control
     a large CHEMICAL class ⟹ the pipeline is wrong — a science finding
   Today they are indistinguishable in a single count, and the two demand opposite responses:
   SPEND MORE PER ATTEMPT versus STOP AND FIX THE METHOD.
```

🔒 **And the symmetric guard, since proposer7 named theirs.** Their failure mode is asking *"how
would we know if this went wrong?"* without an affordable instrument attached — indistinguishable
from refusing to decide. **Mine is the mirror: producing a price without stating what it is a price
OF.** Every error of mine this round was that shape — 0.247 core-h was a price for threads nobody
used; 260.000 was a price for a lithium hop; my anchor-free IRC row was a price for a job without
its Hessian. ⟹ **the guard on my side is: a cost figure must arrive with the job it measures named
in the same cell.** That is `unit-in-the-cell` in its final and most general form, and it is the one
control this round taught me three separate times.

**engineer7 out. Successor: engineer8. Start at §R39.36.**

> per IRC direction (4 total per attempt) from two points on the truncated path; `terminal opt` =

> (11→21 atoms) used elsewhere in §R39, ≈9.6 — DFT-specific, NOT reused here (no cross-Hamiltonian
> borrowing). Units: raw-KNL core-h, 1-thread-equivalent for GFN2 rows, `work` unless noted.

```

  T21-se   931 core-h    (× S₂₁ 9.6)

GFN2-level (proxy: §R39.20's corrected "GFN2 geometry opt, one quench frame" rate — the only
GFN2-opt cost this project has; a terminal opt from an IRC point is a DIFFERENT job than a quench-
frame relax, so this is an ESTIMATE OF AN ESTIMATE, flagged as such, not a measurement of a
terminal opt specifically):
  per-opt rate, 21 atoms   0.0002 / 0.0007 / 0.0033 core-h (opt/base/pess) [ESTIMATE, §R39.20 §7]
  size scaling 11→21       ×3.7 (measured exponent 2.01 on atom-count ratio 1.909 — NOT S₂₁, that
                            is a DFT-basis-set factor and does not apply to xtb)
  T21-se (4 opts)          0.0028 / 0.028 / 0.13 core-h   — widened ×10 on pess for the proxy gap
  T11-se (4 opts)          0.0008 / 0.008 / 0.04 core-h
```

## 2. Delta, base case

```
T21-se:  931 − 0.028  ≈  931 core-h saved      (B+ opts drop to ~0.003% of the DFT figure)
T11-se:   97 − 0.008  ≈   97 core-h saved
As a share of T21-se's own base attempt cost (5,142, §R39.36 two-sided table): ~18%.
🟢 coder11's flag is right in direction and in size: GFN2-level B+ is not "cheaper", it is
  NEGLIGIBLE against every other term in the attempt. This is what recovers proposer7's original
  "~12%" intuition — that number implicitly assumed a cheap completion check, and DFT terminal
  opts were the thing that broke it (§R39.33 found +15%, not +12%, BECAUSE they were priced at DFT).

## 3. 🔴 What does NOT move automatically, and is the actual risk to the wave-1 arithmetic

```
🔴 THE CEILING (guard-relevant number) is a SEPARATE decision from the WORK just re-priced. Today
  the two opts per direction are folded into the SAME 1,536 core-h/direction cap as the IRC itself
  (§R39.34 §4: base 480 IRC + 465 opts = 945, 60% margin under 1,536). Switching the opts to GFN2
  does not shrink that cap by itself — someone has to re-derive it, or T21-se's ceiling silently
  keeps ~930 core-h/direction of dead headroom it no longer needs.
🔴 ADR-110 RISK, NAMED SO IT DOESN'T RECUR A THIRD TIME (33× on xtb NVT anchor, 290× on GFN2
  quench-opt anchor, both from uncounted threads/cores): if the 4 GFN2 terminal opts are submitted
  as FOUR SEPARATE tasks at the default whole-node convention, the `min_wall_h = 0.5` floor charges
  `64 cores × 0.5 h = 32 core-h` CEILING EACH — 128 core-h of ceiling for ~0.03 core-h of real work,
  a ~4,000× inflation that would be invisible in the spend total and visible only in the guard math.
  🟢 FIX, cost 0: bundle the 4 opts into ONE job (same "bundle small tasks" rule as the queue-wait
  finding, §0 overlay) and declare `cores_per_task` explicitly at 1-4 (ADR-110's rule, not "use

The chemical adequacy of GFN2 for confirming two IRC-truncated paths land in the same minimum

# §R39.39 — engineer8, 2026-08-20: the optional GFN2 pre-filter on B+ — priced, not built

> **Abbreviations, first use**: `pre-filter` = proposer7's optional stage — run the B+ terminal-opt
> pair at GFN2 first; disagreement ⟹ skip DFT, return `indeterminate` for ~0 cost; agreement ⟹
> still pay full DFT B+ (GFN2 agreement is untrustworthy per proposer7 — documented basin-merging
> for Li-coordinated complexes); `p_disagree` = the fraction of attempts where the GFN2 pair lands
> in different basins, UNMEASURED. Ruling context: DFT is the settled level for B+ itself
> (proposer7, this round) — this section is about the OPTIONAL filter placed in front of it, offered
> "not recommended" and explicitly conditioned on clearing "a wide margin."

## 1. What it costs to add — near-zero, and the ceiling doesn't move at all

```
ADDED WORK      2 GFN2 opts/direction × 2 directions, same rate as §R39.38 §1: ~0.03 core-h/attempt
                at 21 atoms base (~0.008 at 11). [ESTIMATE, same proxy caveat as §R39.38 — no
                measured terminal-opt-at-GFN2 figure exists, this is a quench-frame-opt proxy.]
ADDED CEILING   🔴 ZERO. The cap must still budget for the DFT-opt worst case, because the AGREEMENT
                branch always pays DFT regardless of the filter. A pre-filter that never removes the
                worst-case path cannot move a cap sized to the worst-case path. ⟹ this does not
                touch the ≤3-vs-≤2 production-attempt arithmetic in ANY direction — it is a pure
                EXPECTED-SPEND lever, not a SUBMISSION-FEASIBILITY one. Different question from
                everything else in this project's ceiling fights.
```

## 2. What it could save — real, but unquotable today

```
SAVES            p_disagree × 931 core-h (T21-se, 4 DFT opts) PER FIRING, and only on the branch
                  that returns `indeterminate` EITHER WAY (§39.32(g) condition 7's C-2.2: B+
                  disagreement ⟹ indeterminate). 🔒 So the filter changes NO accepted result — it
                  only changes what an indeterminate costs to arrive at. Worth stating plainly since
                  it is easy to mis-read as "more attempts succeed."
p_disagree        UNMEASURED. Illustrative only, NOT a forecast:
                  p = 0.1  ⟹  ~93 core-h/attempt   ·   p = 0.3  ⟹  ~279   ·   p = 0.5  ⟹  ~466
🔴 No expected saving can be quoted without p_disagree, and nothing in this project has measured a
  B+ agreement/disagreement rate yet — R-A/R-B are the first attempts that will produce one.
```

## 3. 🟢 The margin test proposer7 asked for, resolved by NOT building the gate yet

```
The build cost is not core-h (§1 — negligible either way). The real cost is coder11's time, a new
pipeline stage, and a genuinely new failure mode (a GFN2 opt that itself doesn't converge — the
`engine`-class error proposer7 named, §39.69). None of that is worth paying for BEFORE p_disagree
is known, and none of it is needed to FIND p_disagree.
🟢 HIERARCHICAL-WITH-OVERLAP, same pattern as the SP ladder and B+'s own R-A calibration (three uses
  already this round): run the GFN2 pair ALONGSIDE R-A and R-B's real DFT B+, which are already
  funded and already running the DFT opts either way. Record agree/disagree as DATA, gate nothing.
  Marginal cost: the same ~0.03/0.008 core-h from §1, already inside the funded round.
⟹ p_disagree is measured for ~0 additional core-h and ~0 schedule risk, and the gate/no-gate
  decision (and whether it "clears a wide margin") becomes a real arithmetic question next round
  instead of a guess this round. If p_disagree turns out to be, say, <5%, the gate is not worth
  building regardless of how cheap it is — coder11's time and a new failure mode aren't free even
  when core-h is.
```

**Recommendation**: instrument (free, already-funded runs), do not gate. Below Ω emitter in
priority — Ω is load-bearing for U-56a itself (§R39.34 §5, ~5,673 core-h/round of avoided-null
spend); this is a possible future optimization on an already-indeterminate branch. Sequence
accordingly.

**Reported to**: team-lead, proposer7 (the margin question, resolved), coder11 (sent — optional,
non-blocking, below Ω emission, sizing left to coder11 since engineer8 has no visibility into the
B+ code to judge "small diff" from outside).

B+'s terminal opts are **not wired yet** (only the decision half, `bplus_agreement`, and start-point
selection, `bplus_sample_points`, exist — zero production callers). That inverts my "piggyback on

# §R39.40 — engineer8, 2026-08-20: traced — `05_STATE.md`'s round table doesn't reconcile because one cell has the wrong item's number in it

> Non-blocking (lead already cleared submission). Traced per lead's request after confirming today's
> code changes need no re-pricing.

## 1. The gap

`05_STATE.md` §1's round table lists `cut U56-2 (3× 11-atom TS attempts + endpoint certs) ceiling
~6,145`. Summing its own seven listed components (6,145 + 5,328 + 3,128 + 329 + 33 + 1 + 60) gives
**15,024**, not the stated **~17,200**. A ~2,176 core-h gap between a table and its own stated sum.

## 2. Root cause — a mislabeled cell, not a pricing error

**`6,145` is T21-se's ceiling** (a single 21-atom Δ_shell production attempt, WITH `rcfc` — §R39.34
§4, §R39.36 §1), **not `cut U56-2`'s** (the 3×11-atom gate batch this round actually submits).
`cut U56-2`'s own ceiling, per `03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md`'s own most recent full round-composition line
(§R39.33, this document's line 230): **6,530 base + 1,280 (R-A Option-A calibration IRC increment,
§R39.33 §3) = 7,810.** Same document, same section, states the bundled round directly: **"BUNDLED
ROUND 17,201 / 21,000, margin 18.1%"** — which is where `05_STATE.md`'s own `~17,200` total comes
from. **The total is right and independently traceable. One row's number was copy-pasted from a
different item.** Exactly the "read the route, not just the number" failure this project's log
names repeatedly (ADR-110, the 33× xtb anchor, P1's void IRC anchor, ADR-112) — this time in a
summary table rather than in a cost derivation.

## 3. What does NOT follow from this

`§R39.34`'s IRC anchor-free reprice lowered `cut U56-2`'s BASE (spend estimate) from 3,514 to
2,965 — that is a different number from the CEILING (7,810) reconciled above, and per this
project's own standing distinction (caps don't move on their own, §R39.38 §3), the ceiling is
unaffected by a base reprice. The 17,200 total is a ceiling sum; it does not need to move when a
spend estimate does.

## 4. Suggested fix, not made here

`05_STATE.md` is the lead's ledger, not mine to edit. Suggested: replace its `cut U56-2 ...
ceiling ~6,145` cell with **~7,810** (6,530 + the R-A calibration increment), so the table
reconciles to its own stated ~17,200 without a reader needing to cross into `03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md`
to find why it doesn't add up today.

# §R39.41 — engineer8, 2026-08-20: 🔴🔴 S₂₁'s cube law is CONTESTED by real data — every T21-se/E21 figure in this document inherits it, including two of mine

> Relayed from proposer7's §39.72 (real P5 data). Non-blocking for the round already submitted
> (§3), but load-bearing for every T21-se number quoted anywhere in §R39, including §R39.38 §1.

## 1. The measurement that contests it

```
S₂₁ = 7.0/9.6/13.2, EVERY use of it in this document (§R24.1's cube rule × cycle growth, plugged
  in at line 11121 as [ASSUMPTION]) is an ATOM-COUNT power law: bigger molecule ⟹ costs more, by
  N^x, independent of WHAT changed about the molecule.
MEASURED, proposer7, real P5 data:
  ec → li_ec_cation        (+1 Li, 10→11 atoms)           ×2.8
  ec → ec_radical_anion    (+1 electron, 10→10 atoms)     ×2.3
  ec → li_ec_radical       (+1 Li AND +1 electron, 10→11) ×15.2   — independent factors predict
                                                              ×2.8×2.3=6.4; the extra ×2.4 is a
                                                              REAL INTERACTION, not atom count.
⟹ R-C's actual reactant (Li⁺(EC)₂ + electron: cation AND open-shell AND 21 atoms) is exactly the
  combination that breaks a power law built on size alone. li_ec2_cation (closed-shell, no radical)
  ALONE already cost 429.55 core-h and did not converge in 49 cycles.
```

## 2. What this does to my own numbers

```
§R39.38 §1's DFT T21-se B+-opt figure (931 core-h = 97 × S₂₁ 9.6) inherits the cube law directly —
  RETRACTED AS A POINT VALUE. Same for every other T21-se/21-atom figure in this document that
  multiplies an 11-atom number by S₂₁ (§R39.15, §R39.17, §R39.34-.36's T21-se ceilings 6,145/7,169,
  the "3×6,145=18,435 ⟹ ≤3 attempts fit" arithmetic, §R39.20's 2-D GFN2 scan ×S₂₁ figures). None of
  these were mine originally, but I used the same convention without re-checking it, which is the
  exact "flagging provenance is not the same as checking arithmetic" failure §R39.20 §1 already
  named once this round for a different anchor.
🔴 THERE IS NOT YET A REPLACEMENT NUMBER. proposer7's four data points are all 10-11 atom species;
  none is R-C's actual 21-atom cation-radical reactant. Substituting ×15.2 for S₂₁ would be the
  SAME mistake in the other direction — extrapolating a measured factor to a system it was not
  measured on. The honest state is: **T21-se's true cost is unknown, and unknown in a direction
  cube-law systematically underestimated, not merely uncertain in magnitude.**
```

## 3. 🟢 What is NOT affected — the round already in flight

```
🟢 The submitted round (cut U56-2 = 3× T11-se + endpoint certs, ~7,810 ceiling) uses NO S₂₁ anywhere
  — it is priced entirely at 11 atoms. P1b, P5, sp_ladder, stage 0, P-U2′, rcfc smoke: none scale by
  S₂₁ either. 🔒 Nothing in flight needs re-pricing or re-submission over this finding.
🔴 WHAT IS AFFECTED: wave-1 planning. Every "≤3 production attempts fit the guard" statement in
  §R39.34-.37 was computed from a T21-se ceiling built on the now-contested cube law. That
  arithmetic cannot be trusted for a go/no-go on wave 1 until a real 21-atom, cation+open-shell
  attempt (R-C, or R-A/R-B if either turns out to carry the same interaction) produces a measured
  cost. This is the SAME shape as the IRC anchor problem (§R39.34/.35/ADR-112) one level up the
  size ladder: a convenient scaling relation stood in for a measurement, and it broke exactly where
  the chemistry — not the atom count — made it break.
```

## 4. Secondary finding, routed but noted for the budget consequence

```
🔴 u_measured is a ~5× WIDE DISTRIBUTION across seeds of the SAME species at the SAME level (ec
  ×4.4, ec_radical_anion ×5.4, ch3o_radical ×2.1) — wider than r itself (1.0-1.25). The current
  `N₁ = min(600, remaining/(u_measured × r_composite))` sizing formula treats u_measured as a point.
  🔒 BUDGET CONSEQUENCE, mine to flag even though the formula fix is proposer7/coder's: a sizing
  formula built on a point estimate from a 5×-wide distribution will be wrong by up to 5× in
  EITHER direction depending on which tail the point estimate landed on — this is not a tuning
  question, it changes whether a batch sized by N₁ fits its own guard reservation at all. Worth a
  margin buffer or a distribution-aware N₁ before this formula prices anything else.
🔴 Integrity caveats routed to critic10 (proposer7, not mine to resolve): the `level` label on this
  batch is stale (pre-ADR-108, functional AND solvent both disagree with what actually ran) and
  `rc:1` fires on all 20 rows including the 17 that converged — `rc` is not a usable health signal
  on this batch. Neither invalidates §1-§3 above (those come from `opt_cycles`/wall, not from the
  mislabeled fields), but nothing else from this batch should be quoted until critic10 clears it.
```

> Answers coder11's design question (relayed by lead): where should the EpsInf=1.0-vs-18.5
> invariance double-run live — (a) inside `endpoint_prep.sh`/production, collapsible by a config
> switch, or (b) a one-off probe, removed after it answers the question.

## 1. The two contexts are different sizes of the same question

```
ENDPOINT (endpoint_prep_reactant, one job)   extra cost = one more freq/Hessian calc
  ≈ 40-130 core-h  [ESTIMATE, existing anchor §R39.15 §4/§R39.35 — 11-atom Hessian range, NOT
  re-measured for this specific route]. Against a 384 core-h budget cap with only 41.6 spent so
  far: TRIVIALLY AFFORDABLE, doubled or not. No reason to withhold this from every future endpoint
  cert either — the worst case if never collapsed is ~130 core-h/item, forever, on a low-volume item.

P5 (20 species)   extra cost = 20 × one more freq/Hessian calc
  ≈ 800-2,600 core-h  [ESTIMATE, same 11-atom anchor × 20 — WIDE, because P5's species range in
  size (per plan.py: "P1은 40-80원자, P1b는 5-25원자 구간") and the anchor itself is not remeasured
  at any of their actual sizes]. That is 25-85% of P5's ORIGINAL 3,128 core-h budget, ON TOP OF the
  freq re-run this batch already needs post-EpsInf-fix. 🔴 THIS is the number that makes "leave it
  doubled forever" a real cost, not a rounding error — the endpoint case never was.
```

## 2. (a) and (b) cost the SAME core-h — the choice is round-trip structure, not price

```
Both shapes pay for exactly one doubled measurement, once, to learn whether EpsInf matters. The
core-h is identical either way. The difference is calendar/schedule:
(b), a separate one-off probe, is its own submission — its own queue wait. At THIS site queue wait
  INVERTS with size (§0 overlay: 1 node 531s, 4 nodes 111s, 16 nodes 62s — small jobs wait
  LONGEST). A standalone probe for P5's 20-species question would be exactly the small-job shape
  that pays the worst queue-wait tax here, for a measurement (a) gets for free by riding inside a
  batch that's already being submitted.
(a), bundled + config-switch, avoids that extra round trip — but ONLY earns back its cost-safety if
  the switch behaves like this project's existing release gates (u56_2.released, sp_ladder.released,
  05_STATE.md §1): DEFAULT ON (doubled/informative), COLLAPSES ONLY ON EXPLICIT HUMAN ACTION, never
  silently. An auto-collapsing switch (fires once invariance looks confirmed, no human step) is
  exactly the shape that turns a one-time 800-2,600 core-h measurement into either a permanently
  doubled tax (if it never fires) or a silently under-verified single-run (if it fires on a false
  invariance read) — this project's log has both failure directions on record already (ADR-036's
  null-fallback; the six-plus "quiet failure" catalog, §0-p.6/§10).
```

## 3. Recommendation

```
🟢 (a) for BOTH contexts, with the switch built to the release-gate SHAPE, not a fresh design:
  default = double-run, config key flips it to single-EpsInf, flip requires the same explicit
  lead/user action the release flags already require. This gets (a)'s cheap round-trip without
  reintroducing an auto-collapse risk.
🔴 ONE STRUCTURAL NOTE, cost-relevant, not just design taste: run the two EpsInf values as
  SEPARATE PARALLEL TASKS (two array elements / two chained-but-independent jobs), not as one job
  computing both serially. Core-h is the same either way, but endpoint_prep_reactant's 6h wall cap
  is tight against a SERIAL double freq, and P5's array convention (§R22.9: one execution = one
  array task) already has the right shape for this — just add task count, don't add per-task wall.
```

**Reported to**: team-lead, coder11.

# §R39.42 — engineer8, 2026-08-20: P1's 9,216 core-h reservation, traced to source — real, large, and NOT fixable by deleting P1

> Non-blocking, real cluster results already in. Traced per lead's flag (`guard.reservations`
> showing 9,216 for a permanently-excluded item that cost ~0 in practice, 37 s / 0.0103 core-h).

## 1. Root cause, exact, from `plan.py`

```
P1_TOTAL_CORE_HOURS = 6,800   (plan.py:121)
Item("P1", ..., core_hours_budget=6,800, nodes=1, cores_per_task=None (whole node, 64 cores),
     min_wall_h=48.0, ...)                                                    (plan.py:561-568)

size_job(6800, 64, 1, max_wall_h=48, min_wall_h=48):
  ideal_wall = 6800/64 = 106.25h  ⟹ clamped to max_wall_h  ⟹  wall = 48
  links = ceil(6800 / (64×48) − ε) = ceil(2.213) = 3
  reserved = 64 × 48 × 3 = 9,216                                              ⟵ MATCHES lead's number exactly
```

This is a **static, plan-time reservation** computed from the Item's declared worst-case budget and
wall — it has no visibility into what happens at runtime, so it cannot know C-8 will refuse the job
in 37 seconds. The 9,216 is the guard defending against P1 running its full designed chain, which is
structurally impossible today (§2), not a measurement of anything P1 could plausibly spend.

## 2. Why the refusal is structural, not merely observed-so-far

```
C-8 (guards.py:10): "a TS search REFUSES TO START unless both endpoints are converged minima with
  n_imag == 0."
`endpoint_prep_product` — the Item that would have certified P1's PRODUCT endpoint — was explicitly
  REMOVED from the plan when the user ruled P1 permanently out (plan.py:592-599, "C-8-2 취소 기록":
  "product-end certification existed to satisfy P1's C-8 precondition; with P1 permanently excluded,
  the grounds for it are gone").
⟹ P1 CANNOT EVER SATISFY C-8 under the current plan — not "hasn't so far," but "the input that would
  let it pass was deliberately deleted." The 37 s / 0.0103 core-h this round is not luck; it's what
  a structurally-unsatisfiable precondition looks like when measured.
```

## 3. 🔴 Why "just delete the Item" is the wrong fix — a real dependency, not vestige

```
Item("P1b", ..., depends_on=["P1"], ...)                                     (plan.py:639)
missing_dep = [d for d in item.depends_on if d not in runnable_keys]         (plan.py:1225)
```
`runnable_keys` is populated from Items **present in the plan**, checked at plan-build time — not
from P1's runtime success. **If P1 is deleted outright, P1b fails its `missing_dep` check and drops
out of the round entirely.** P1b is this round's SINGLE LARGEST item (5,328 core-h) and its own
stated purpose is the biggest unpriced unknown in the whole project (`r`, the level-cost multiplier,
1.19–9.49× spread — plan.py:641-646). Deleting P1 to save 9,216 core-h of dead ceiling would silently
cost the round its most important item. Exactly the "quietly wrong, not loudly failing" shape this
project's log is full of, and it would have been ME introducing it if I'd recommended deletion.

## 4. 🟢 What actually recovers the ceiling without touching P1b

```
P1's Item stays IN THE PLAN (satisfies P1b's dependency) but its core_hours_budget/min_wall_h no
longer need to assume a full 3-link, 48h/link TS-search chain — that chain can never execute.
ILLUSTRATIVE RESIZE, NOT A COMMITTED NUMBER (coder's call, flagged not built):
  core_hours_budget  6,800 → ~50-100   (10-50× the measured 0.0103, generous margin for a re-check
                                        or a slower C-8 evaluation than this round's)
  min_wall_h         48.0  → ~1-2 h
  ⟹ reserved falls from 9,216 to roughly 64-136 core-h — RECOVERS ~9,080-9,150 core-h of ceiling,
    ≈ 43% OF THE ENTIRE 21,000 GUARD. The largest single lever priced this session, well above the
    Ω emitter's 5,673/round or B+'s GFN2 delta.
🟢 THIS IS NOT A RISKIER BET ON C-8. A shrunk wall/budget makes the FAILURE MODE BETTER, not worse:
  if C-8 ever fails to fire (bug, config drift), the OLD reservation lets P1 burn up to 9,216 core-h
  before hitting its wall cap; the NEW one catches the same failure inside ~1-2h instead. Shrinking
  the reservation is a strict improvement in both directions — cheaper when C-8 fires (which it
  structurally must), safer when it somehow doesn't.
```

## 5. What this is and is not

```
🔴 NOT a code change I am making. Item budgets and guard defaults are coder territory; this crosses
  from pricing into implementation. Flagged with the exact numbers so it is a small, well-specified
  diff rather than a rediscovery.
🔴 NOT free of a decision. Reducing a defensive reservation on the item tied to the user's own
  "permanently out" ruling touches something a ruling was made about — worth a nod from lead/user
  before coder touches it, even though the change only ever makes the guard tighter around a
  structurally-dead path, never looser.
🟢 EVERY OTHER round this session is unaffected — P1's reservation has been 9,216 in every round
  table quoted in this document without anyone pricing it as its own line, because it was inherited
  silently from the Item's original (pre-exclusion) design budget.
```

### 3a. 🔴 The real finding: the doubling is priced 29× above its own physics

Only the `freq` stage reads `EpsInf` (proposer7 §39.73; confirmed here — the keyword appears nowhere
outside the tight/freq stage's log). **That stage costs 2.27 core-h.** The arm costs 65.87 because
it is shipped as an independent sibling job that re-runs `rough` + `tight` from scratch.

```

cost of the only stage that can depend on EpsInf     2.27 core-h
ratio                                                  29.0×
```

On this item the waste is 63 core-h and does not matter. On P5 it is the entire cost of the doubling:

```
P5 EpsInf doubling, design (A) — as-shipped shape, each EpsInf value = full opt+freq re-run
  basis: P5's own measured floor, 1,003.40 core-h for 20 finished tasks (opt-only)
  2nd arm  ~1,000–2,000 core-h   [ESTIMATE, widened for t21/t22 and for the freq that never ran]
  ⟹ §R39.43's 800–2,600 band was RIGHT FOR THIS DESIGN. No revision needed if (A) is kept.

P5 EpsInf doubling, design (B) — freq-only from the stored converged geometries
  basis: one MEASURED Hessian, 2.27 core-h at 11 atoms / doublet / this level
  optimistic (all species ~11-atom class, 20 × 2.3)                  ~46 core-h
  base     (mean ~3× the anchor over P5's 3–21 atom mix)            ~140 core-h
  pessimistic (5 of 20 in the cation+open-shell 21-atom class,
               each 20–40× the anchor)                              ~600 core-h
  [ESTIMATE] — 13× spread, and it stays wide on purpose. I have exactly ONE measured Hessian
  and ZERO measurements above 11 atoms. I am deliberately NOT applying an atom-count power law
  as if it were knowledge: that is the S₂₁ cube-law mistake (§R39.41), and the bracket is loose
  in the direction the cube law under-predicted.
```

**(B) is 3–20× cheaper than (A).** `05_STATE.md` §1a already states the optimized geometries survive
in the tree and "a re-run only needs to redo the freq half," so (B) is consistent with the plan of
record — but whether the bracket is scientifically valid at a FIXED geometry is proposer's call, not
mine. My contribution is the price gap, not the ruling. Two facts for whoever rules it: G16's own log
says `IEInf=0` (equilibrium solvation), which is the basis of proposer7's pre-registered prediction
that `EpsInf` is read and not used; and a fixed-geometry bracket isolates the `EpsInf` effect from a
geometry difference, which the shipped design does not.

Evidence that (A) is not merely wasteful but NOISY: the two arms' `rough` stages — same molecule,
same level, same cap — cost **36.2 vs 51.62 core-h, a 1.42× spread**, and exit on geometries that
differ by up to ~0.1 Å on hydrogen. This is proposer7's §39.72(2) "`u_measured` is a distribution"
finding recurring at the ITEM level rather than across P5 seeds. Under (A) the bracket comparison
would carry that spread inside it.
🔴 **Caveat, stated so nobody reads it the other way**: the two arms are NOT a clean A/B on `EpsInf`
even for the opt stage — the full arm also ran a different start-selection path (`start=packaged`,
`start_selection.json`, absent from the base arm). The geometry difference must not be attributed to
`EpsInf`.

### 3b. Not my call, but load-bearing: the arm produced a C-8 certificate

`terminal_status.json`: `status: converged`, `"n_imag == 0 at the tight/freq stage, C-8.2/C-8.3
certificate"`. `f1_observables.json`: `normal_termination: true`, `opt_converged: true`,
`n_imag_at_convergence: 0`, ⟨S²⟩ 0.7533→0.75 at both stages. Nine `Frequencies --` blocks = 27 modes
= 3N−6 at N=11, a complete Hessian. Reported as fact for pricing purposes (the EpsInf fix works and
endpoint certification is no longer a schedule risk); the chemistry read belongs to proposer.
🔴 The bracket itself is **half done** — only the `EpsInf=18.5` endpoint exists; invariance cannot be
decided from one arm. **Cost to complete: 2.27 core-h freq-only from the stored `endpoint_tight.chk`
(10.5 MB, on disk), or 65.9 core-h as another full sibling job.** Cheapest open decision on the board.

## 4. P6 — κ landed, and the thread-scaling result is bigger news than κ itself

`[MEASURED]`, new-window execution, 3/3 valid: ADR-048's gate (`declared == requested ==
nprocshared == cores_observed`) passed on every task, all rc=0. Anchor is a single point (`sp`) on
the 11-atom Li(EC) reduced radical at wB97XD/gen + PCM — **the same system class as the endpoint and
U56 chains**, which is what makes it usable rather than decorative.

```
κ = 287 s (cluster, 16 threads) / 177.3 s (dev box, 16 threads, Ryzen 7800X3D) = 1.619
```

⟹ **every dev-box-derived cost or wall figure in this document must be multiplied by 1.62 for
cluster execution.** `[MEASURED — this system, this job type]`. The report's own label forbids
generalizing to other codes; I treat it as valid for the G16 DFT chain (endpoint / U56 / P5 /
T11-se) and NOT for xtb/GFN2 items, which have their own separate anchor.

Thread scaling, same anchor, same round:

```
threads   wall_s   core-h per job   speedup vs 1 thread   parallel efficiency
--------  -------  --------------   -------------------   -------------------
      1     2514            0.698                 1.00×                  100%
     16      287            1.276                 8.76×                   55%
     64      176            3.128                14.28×                   22%
```

S(16→64) = 287/176 = **1.631** against 4× ideal ⟹ packing gain 4/S = **2.45×** (§R22.3).

🔴 **Planning consequence, and it is the largest recoverable inefficiency currently in the plan:
whole-node 64-thread G16 costs 2.45× the core-h of 16-thread packing, and 4.5× that of serial, for
identical work. Every DFT Item in this plan runs whole-node.** Applied to the item measured above:

```
endpoint arm, 58.03 core-h of G16 work    charged core-h   wall      fits 6 h cap?
  64 threads (as shipped)                          58.03   1.03 h    yes
  16 threads                                      ~23.7    ~1.7 h    yes (3.5× inside)
   1 thread                                       ~12.9    ~9.1 h    NO — exceeds the cap
```

⟹ **16 threads is the throughput-optimal setting for the DFT chain and it fits the existing wall
caps.** This is the right trade at this site specifically: the throughput probe measured 200
concurrent jobs accepted with 54–61 s queue wait at 1/4/16 nodes, so wall-clock is the cheap axis
here and core-h is the scarce one. Rough effect if applied across the DFT items: ~2.4× on core-h at
~1.7× wall. Not free — each Item's wall cap needs re-checking against its own longest stage first.

🟡 **One misreading to head off, because the numbers invite it.** The endpoint arm's 78–83% figures
in §3 are THREAD OCCUPANCY (G16 CPU-h ÷ elapsed × cores), not parallel efficiency. Occupancy is an
upper bound on efficiency, never a measure of it: G16 can keep 64 threads 80% busy and still return
only a 1.63× speedup over 16. The 22% in the table above is the real scaling number and the 78% does
not contradict it. **Cheapest possible validation before acting on the 2.45×: re-run ONE already-
measured stage at 16 threads and compare wall — ~24 core-h, ~1.7 h, no new science.** The anchor is
an `sp`; `opt` and `freq` have different parallel profiles and I have not measured theirs.

## 5. P1 — resize verified on hardware; one recorded number is wrong by 64×

Reserved 64.0 core-h / 1.0 h wall after coder11's resize. Measured this round: refused by C-8 in
37 s at 64 cores = **0.658 core-h charged**, wall 0.0103 h, rc=6. Fourth consecutive refusal across
the two rounds (4 runs, 2.68 core-h total). The guard reconciles exactly: `core_hours_reserved:
11,297.39` = 20,065.39 − 9,151.61 (P1 resize) + 384.00 (the new `epsinf_full` sibling).

🔴 **`05_STATE.md` §1a records the refusal as "measured: 0.0103 core-h, 37s" and the resize margin as
"~6,200×". `0.0103` is the WALL-HOURS number, mislabeled as core-h.** Charged cost is 0.658 core-h
(whole-node, 64 cores). The true margin is 64 / 0.658 = **97×**, not 6,200×. The resize decision is
unchanged and still correct — 97× is a generous margin — but STATE says outright that "the margin is
itself the safety property," so the record should carry 97×. Same defect shape this project keeps
finding: a number correctly computed, wrong label on the cell.

## 6. Two ceiling recoveries available now, both backed by this round's measurements

```
(a) P6 sizing. Reserved 1,944 core-h (24 h wall cap × 1/16/64 threads), spent 6.25. 313× over.
    P6's slowest task ran 42 min. Resize to a 2 h wall cap: reserves 2 + 32 + 128 = 162 core-h.
    RECOVERS ~1,782 core-h of ceiling.  [MEASURED basis: 0.711 / 1.498 / 4.036 core-h actual]
    Same fix shape as P1's resize, lower stakes, and now backed by real data rather than a guess.

(b) Endpoint certifications inside U56-2's ~7,810 ceiling. Priced at 384 core-h each; measured
    65.87. U56-2 needs 3 ⟹ 198 core-h, not 1,152. RECOVERS ~950 core-h of that ceiling.
    🔴 Do NOT tighten to the measured cost. n=1, and the one other endpoint attempt this project
    has ever made crashed. Keeping ~2× headroom over the measurement (≈130 core-h/endpoint) still
    recovers ~760 core-h and leaves the failure margin intact.
```

Also flagged, not a recovery: `probe_qw_n64` has a job directory but no execution record — the
64-node queue-wait arm reports `still_queued` and never returned. **The largest queue wait this
project has actually measured is 16 nodes at 56 s.** Any schedule that assumes a 64-node allocation
arrives promptly is unmeasured.

## 7. Infrastructure defect, routed to lead for coder

`endpoint_prep_reactant_epsinf_full` appears in `plan`, appears in `guard.reservations` (384 core-h),
and has a complete job tree containing this project's first C-8 endpoint certificate — but emits **no
entry in `pilots[]`**. The round's single most valuable artefact is invisible in the report rollup
and recoverable only by reading the job directory by hand. Same class as the "measured but unread"
defects catalogued through §39.69 and §39.74, this time on the reporting side rather than the
producing side.
