# §R39.57 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: re-certification accepted at full cost; the branch survives, relocated from "freq-only vs full" to "warm start vs cold start"

proposer8's §39.94 rules that the endpoint certificate does NOT transfer to acetone, for a reason
that is not about EpsInf at all: **a certificate is a certificate of a model, and the production
model changed** — an all-zero parameter row is replaced by a populated one, and the §39.90(b)
inertness result was measured on the zeros. Accepted without reservation. It is ordinary hygiene, it
does not reopen the cancelled experiment, and my "freq-only re-certification at ~4–5 core-h" is
**withdrawn**: a stage that never re-optimises never confirms the geometry is stationary on the new
surface, so it cannot certify that model. proposer8 is right and the reasoning is not close.

🔒 I also accept the H2 correction and it was mine to get wrong: I invoked proposer8's own
structural-null argument (§39.85(e), "choose the probe most likely to BE the counterexample") to
justify the **minimum-coupling molecule on the board**, which inverts it. A null on a neutral
nonpolar closed-shell diatomic cannot separate "never read" from "read, but this solute barely
polarises the continuum". The smoke survives on a different and better basis — its decisive readout
is the log, not the frequencies, and *"a term is either computed or it isn't"* is molecule-independent.

## 1. The branch is not dead — it moved, and the new one does not touch the certificate's meaning

What proposer8 rejected was **freq-only**: no re-optimisation, so the geometry is never confirmed
stationary on the acetone surface. Correct. But the stored geometry has a second, entirely different
use that is not a certificate claim at all:

```
REJECTED (correctly)   freq-only on the stored geometry
                       -> the geometry is an OUTPUT never re-derived on the new surface.
                          Cannot certify the production model.

PROPOSED INSTEAD       full opt=(tight,calcfc,maxcycles=200) + freq on the acetone surface,
                       WARM-STARTED from the certified geometry via geom=check.
                       -> the optimiser converges on the PRODUCTION surface, n_imag is computed
                          there, deck_verification names acetone. A complete certificate.
                          The stored geometry is an INPUT GUESS, and a starting guess is not
                          part of what a certificate certifies — C-8 verifies convergence
                          independently of where the optimiser started.
```
The `rough` stage exists to walk from a packaged idealised guess into the basin. Started from an
already-certified geometry on a near-identical surface, that stage has no work to do. **Not running a
stage whose purpose is already satisfied is not a corner cut.**

### Priced, all from the endpoint's own measured stage internals

```
                                                    core-h    basis
tight opt (233.1 s G16: 4 SCFs at 19/14/10/5
  cycles + 1 CalcFC Hessian + ~4 Berny steps)         4.14     [MEASURED]
freq (127.6 s)                                        2.27     [MEASURED]
stage setup + smoke + wrapper                         1.66     [MEASURED]
-------------------------------------------------------------
WARM START, base                                     ~8.1 core-h
WARM START, pessimistic (3x the Berny steps if the
  surface moved more than expected)                 ~14
COLD START fallback (full rough+tight, if the warm
  start leaves the basin or hits maxcycles)          42-66     [MEASURED, incl. 1.43x spread]
```
**~8 vs ~66 is an 8× saving on an item that gates `u56_2.released`.** Worst case if the warm start
fails is ~14 + 66 = ~80 against a guaranteed 66 — so the bet is ~8 to save ~58, against ~14 to lose.

### 🟢 And the sequencing removes even that risk, because the smoke runs first

```
smoke returns fully inert (Atomic radii, Cavity type, term list all identical)
    -> the surface is unchanged; warm start is near-certain to converge in few steps.  ~8 core-h
smoke shows a changed cavity or new terms
    -> the surface moved; go straight to cold start, don't gamble.                    ~42-66
```
The branch is therefore decided by a measurement already scheduled, at no added cost — the same
structure as before, relocated to a question where it does not touch what a certificate means.

🟡 **proposer8's ruling to check, not mine**: whether a warm-started tight optimisation is a complete
C-8 certificate. My claim is only that it re-derives the geometry on the production surface, which is
the property the freq-only version lacked. If the ruling is that a certificate must also re-derive
the *path* to the geometry, the answer is ~66 and I withdraw this too.

# §R39.58 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: proposer8's force criterion VERIFIED against the artefact — the mechanism is real, but the criterion as stated would false-refuse every certificate it exists to grant

§39.95 rules that a freq-only re-certification satisfies C-8 iff, read from that one job:
`n_imag == 0`, max force ≤ the optimisation level's convergence threshold, RMS force ≤ the same.
**I checked all three against the real log before pricing off them.** The mechanism is real. The
threshold comparison is not — and it fails in the expensive direction.

## 1. 🟢 The mechanism is CONFIRMED — a freq step does print its own forces

`endpoint_tight.log`, after `Link1: Proceeding to internal job step number 2` (line 3199):
```
4243:  Center     Atomic                   Forces (Hartrees/Bohr)
4258:  Cartesian Forces:  Max     0.000032681 RMS     0.000016752
```
proposer8's construction works. A freq-only job carries both C-8 halves.

## 2. 🔴🔴 But the criterion as stated compares two DIFFERENT quantities, and would refuse the certified geometry itself

G16 prints forces in two places and they are not the same number:
```
Cartesian Forces (what a freq job prints)      Max 0.000032681   RMS 0.000016752
Convergence table (what carries the threshold) Max 0.000000      Threshold 0.000015   YES
                                               RMS 0.000000      Threshold 0.000010   YES
```
The convergence table reports forces in the **optimiser's internal/redundant coordinate space**,
with translations, rotations and redundant combinations projected out. `Cartesian Forces` is the raw
gradient. They differ by construction.

⟹ **Reading `Cartesian Forces: Max` (3.27e-5) and comparing it to the tight threshold (1.5e-5)
REFUSES the certificate — on the exact geometry G16 itself certified as converged at tight**, by a
factor of 2.2 on max and 1.7 on RMS. Every warm re-certification would be false-refused and sent to
the ~42–66 core-h cold path. **Cost of the defect: ~58 core-h per certificate, and a refusal that
looks like a real finding.**

## 3. 🟢 The fix is a same-quantity comparison, and its floor is already MEASURED

The original optimisation prints the same quantity at the same geometry. From the same log:
```
final optimisation cycle (line 2688)   Cartesian Forces: Max 0.000032685 RMS 0.000016753
freq step, same geometry (line 4258)   Cartesian Forces: Max 0.000032681 RMS 0.000016752
agreement                              4e-9 Hartree/Bohr absolute, 1.2e-4 relative
```
**Proposed criterion, replacing the threshold comparison:**
> the re-certification freq job's `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS` must reproduce **the original
> optimisation's FINAL `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS`** — not the convergence-table threshold.

Why this is better rather than merely different:
```
- like-for-like: the same quantity, computed the same way, at the same geometry
- it has a MEASURED floor (4e-9 absolute) from data already on disk, so the criterion is
  calibrated rather than asserted
- it measures the question directly. "Did the surface move at this geometry" is exactly what a
  gradient comparison answers; a threshold comparison answers "is this geometry converged in a
  coordinate system the freq job never reports"
- it is far MORE sensitive: a surface shift shows in the 5th significant figure of the gradient
  long before it moves a threshold verdict
```
🟡 **The inference it supports, stated precisely so proposer8 can rule on it rather than infer it**:
reproducing the original Cartesian forces demonstrates the **gradient field is unchanged at that
geometry**, hence the geometry is as stationary on acetone as it was certified to be on generic.
Combined with `n_imag == 0` measured on acetone, both C-8 conditions are then established on the
production surface — one measured directly, the other by demonstrated gradient invariance rather
than by assumption. That is the inheritance proposer8 required be measured, and it is measured.

## 4. 🟢 proposer8's threshold warning CONFIRMED with real numbers — it is not hypothetical

```
endpoint, opt=(tight)   Max Force threshold 0.000015   RMS 0.000010
P5 rows, plain opt      Max Force threshold 0.000450   RMS 0.000300      <- 30x looser
P5 ec_radical_anion_s0, converged row:  Max Force 0.000195  -> PASSES default (0.00045)
                                                            -> FAILS tight (0.000015) by 13x
```
Applying tight criteria to a default-converged geometry would fail every P5 row for a reason with
nothing to do with acetone, exactly as warned. **And the §3 fix removes the hazard entirely**, since
a per-row same-quantity comparison never touches a threshold and therefore cannot mismatch one.

## 5. Pricing, updated

```
endpoint re-certification, freq-only, self-verifying     ~4-5 core-h   [MEASURED basis]
   (Hessian 2.27 + same-basis guess=read ~0.04 + setup 0.61 + smoke 0.20 + wrapper 0.85)
fallback if the force comparison fails: full rough+tight  ~42-66
does NOT wait on the smoke — the job decides its own branch
GATES u56_2.released -> schedule EARLY
```
The warm-started-full-reoptimisation option from §R39.57 is **withdrawn as unnecessary**: proposer8's
self-verifying freq-only is cheaper (~4–5 vs ~8) and strictly better founded, because it measures
condition (i) rather than re-deriving it from a warm start that could itself have inherited the old
basin. My branch was the right instinct applied one level too coarsely.

🟢 **P5's C-9 audit: per-row validity flag confirmed free.** Each recovery job prints its own
`Cartesian Forces`; comparing them to that row's own final optimisation forces costs one grep. Rows
that reproduce ⟹ audit valid; rows that do not ⟹ audit `indeterminate`, recorded as such, cost
measurement untouched. No change to the ~92–152 core-h estimate.

## 6. Live sheet

                                                   prerequisite for the re-certification
endpoint re-cert under acetone      ~4-5 (or ~42-66 if its own forces refuse); GATES release
16-thread packing validation        ~24
P5 freq-only recovery, 17 rows      ~92-152        conditional on the acetone deck reaching P5
-------------------------------------------------------------------

# §R39.59 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: warm start accepted and repriced; the force-units defect is moot for the endpoint but LIVE for P5's audit — measured on four rows

## 1. Endpoint re-certification, final: warm-started `opt=(tight,calcfc) freq` on acetone

proposer8's §39.96 approves it as a complete C-8 certificate, on grounds stronger than cost: the cold
start is the option with a **documented failure mode in this project today** (§39.89's
`li_ec_radical_s0_L2` cold-started from a packaged planar seed and converged to 180.00° / 0.0000 Å
coplanar, its own pre-registered falsifier), and the warm start **preserves basin identity**, which is
what U56-2 actually needs — the same chemical species on the new surface, not an independent search
that could silently change what the reaction is.

```
                                                       core-h   basis
warm start, converging in ~1 Berny step                 ~6.8    [MEASURED stage internals]
  (CalcFC Hessian ~2.3 + ~19 SCF cycles ~0.6 + freq 2.27 + overhead 1.66)
warm start, taking the same ~4 steps as the original     ~8.1    [MEASURED]
warm start, pessimistic (3x the steps)                  ~14
COLD START fallback (only if the basin check fails)     42-66    [MEASURED, incl. 1.43x spread]
```
🟢 **Self-verifying, and the smoke is not a prerequisite.** If the surface moved materially the
optimiser takes more steps and costs more, or the basin check refuses and says so. proposer8's
condition 2 — *converging in one step is a valid outcome, not a defect* — is what makes the price
range meaningful rather than a hedge: **the cheap end of the range is the informative outcome, not
the lucky one.**

My §R39.57 warm start is therefore reinstated and my §R39.58 endorsement of freq-only is withdrawn.
Three revisions of this number today (~4–5 → ~66 → ~8 → ~4–5 → ~8). Recording that plainly rather
than presenting the final figure as if it had been stable: **the item cost ~8 core-h and the pricing
of it cost more analyst time than the compute will.** Worth it only because two of the revisions were
real findings (the model-changed ruling, and the force-units defect below), not bookkeeping.

## 2. 🔴🔴 The force-units defect is MOOT for the endpoint but LIVE for P5 — and it flips a real row

The endpoint warm start reads convergence from **G16's own convergence table**, which is the correct
instrument and carries its own thresholds. §R39.58's defect does not touch it.

**But P5's per-row C-9 audit is freq-only by construction** — the recovery runs Hessians on stored
geometries and cannot re-optimise them. So a force check there must read `Cartesian Forces` from the
freq job, and §R39.58's mismatch bites. Measured on four rows:

```
species                  Cartesian Max   convergence-table Max   default threshold   ratio
ec_radical_anion_s0_L2     0.000195412        0.000195              0.000450          1.00
hco3_anion_s0_L2           0.000510141        0.000398              0.000450          1.28  🔴
h2o_s0_L2                  0.000008772        0.000014              0.000450          0.63
li_ec_cation_s0_L2         0.000052608        0.000024              0.000450          2.19
```

🔴 **`hco3_anion_s0_L2` would be FALSE-REFUSED**: its Cartesian max force (5.10e-4) exceeds the
default threshold (4.5e-4) by 1.13×, while G16's own table says `Maximum Force 0.000398 Threshold
0.000450 YES`. Its C-9 audit would be recorded `indeterminate` for a units reason. **One of four
sampled rows — potentially ~25% of the 17.**

🔴 **And the mismatch cannot be corrected with a factor.** The Cartesian-to-internal ratio measured
across these four rows spans **0.63 to 2.19 — a 3.5× spread, non-monotone, and it goes BOTH
directions** (Cartesian smaller than internal for h2o, more than double for li_ec_cation). There is
no fudge factor that rescues a threshold comparison; the two quantities are not related by a scale.

### 🟢 The fix, unchanged from §R39.58 and now with four supporting measurements

> the recovery freq job's `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS` must reproduce **that row's OWN final
> optimisation `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS`** — never a threshold.

Per-row, same quantity, same geometry, immune to the 0.63–2.19 spread by construction, and calibrated
by a measured floor (4e-9 Hartree/Bohr absolute at the endpoint, where both numbers exist in one
log). Costs one grep per row. **Prevents ~25% of the audit from being lost to a units mismatch.**

🟡 proposer8's ruling to make: this changes what condition (i) *means* for the audit — from "is this
geometry converged" (a threshold claim) to "is the gradient field unchanged at this geometry" (an
invariance claim). For the C-9 purpose I believe the invariance claim is the right one, since the
question is whether the stored geometry is still stationary on the surface now in use. But that is a
methodology call and I am supplying the measurement, not the ruling.

## 3. Live sheet
```
smoke, three decks               ~0.3 core-h   code-path + anchor questions only
endpoint re-cert, warm start     ~7-8 (6.8-14); cold fallback 42-66 only if the basin check
                                 refuses. Self-verifying, no smoke prerequisite. GATES release.
16-thread packing validation     ~24           needs a payload change
P5 freq-only recovery, 17 rows   ~92-152       conditional on the acetone deck reaching P5
-------------------------------------------------------------------
whole remaining programme        ~125-245 core-h   = ~1% of guard
ceilings: P6 -1,782 (landed), U56-2 11-atom certs -384 (gated), 21-atom untouched
```

**a rule cited by name is not a rule applied — a rule compressed to its conclusion inverts easily.**
When citing a prior ruling to license a choice, cite the CRITERION, not the verdict. My H2 error was
exactly this: I quoted "one probe is enough" (the conclusion) to justify the probe the selection
criterion (the working part) excludes.

# §R39.60 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: the three-rung ladder priced — run rungs 1 and 2 as ONE job, because the scarce currency is round-trips, not core-h

proposer8's §39.97 replaces the withdrawal with a three-rung escalation. Accepted; the withdrawal was
mine and it was too broad, exactly as they say — it left a ~4–5 core-h attempt jumping straight to
~42–66 with nothing between. Pricing the ladder, and proposing one change that is about schedule
rather than money.

## 1. The ladder priced as stated (each rung a separate submission)

```
rung 1  freq-only, self-verifying                     ~4.5 core-h   cumulative  ~4.5
rung 2  warm-started opt=(tight,calcfc) freq          ~8            cumulative ~12.5
rung 3  cold rough+tight, after a human looks         ~42-66        cumulative ~55-79
```
Escalating from rung 1 to rung 2 discards rung 1's Hessian (~2.3 core-h). Break-even against going
straight to rung 2: the ladder is cheaper iff **P(rung 1 succeeds) > 56%**.

🔴 **And that probability is unknown, with proposer8's own caveat arguing it may be low.** The 4e-9
floor was measured between two runs on the *same* solvent model. Across `generic` → `acetone`, if the
cavity discretisation changes at all, the Cartesian residual changes with it — proposer8's point that
part of the 3.27e-5 is cavity-tessellation noise rather than chemistry cuts directly against rung 1's
success rate.

🟢 **But I am not going to optimise this, and saying so is the recommendation.** The whole decision
spans 4.5 to 12.5 core-h — a spread narrower than the 1.43× run-to-run wall variation already
measured on this system, and 0.06% of the guard. Choosing between them on expected cost would be the
same analyst-time-exceeds-compute-cost trap already flagged in §R39.59. **The ladder's structure is
right; its cost is not a decision variable.**

## 2. 🟢 The change worth making is about round-trips, not core-h

**This item gates `u56_2.released`.** An escalation from rung 1 to rung 2 across two submissions costs
a full submit/collect cycle on a release gate. A round is worth vastly more than 6 core-h — that has
been the governing fact all day.

```
RUN RUNGS 1 AND 2 AS ONE JOB, two Link1 steps:
  step 1   freq only, on the stored geometry              rung 1's measurement
  step 2   opt=(tight,calcfc) freq, warm-started          rung 2's measurement
  cost     2.31 + 6.41 + 1.66 overhead (paid once)  =  ~10.4 core-h
  READ THEM IN LADDER ORDER: step 1's verdict first; step 2 consulted only if step 1 is
  inconclusive.
```
**This preserves proposer8's ladder semantics exactly** — the escalation is in the *reading order*,
not in the submission. It is the same **compute-and-record versus consult** separation this project
has already used three times (C-10.1 for cost probes, Ω, and B+ under §39.77): both rungs are always
computed and always recorded; which one is *consulted* depends on the branch.

```
cost of the change      +5.9 core-h over the lucky path (~4.5 -> ~10.4)
what it buys            removes one possible round of latency from a release gate
                        AND makes rung 2 a recorded datum even when rung 1 succeeds, so the
                        gradient-invariance claim and the re-derived minimum are both on file
```
🟢 Second-order benefit worth naming: when rung 1 *succeeds*, step 2 becomes a free confirmation that
the warm start lands on the same geometry — i.e. §39.96's basin check gets its data anyway, on the
case where nobody would otherwise have bought it. That is proposer8's own always-computed-always-
recorded argument, applied to the rung that would otherwise be skipped.

🔴 **Rung 3 must NOT be pre-run.** proposer8's wording — "considered only after someone looks" — is
right, and the cost supports it: rung 3 is ~42–66 core-h against a case whose whole meaning is that
*the structure moved to another species*, which is a finding to surface, not a job to retry.

## 3. Accepted with no cost implication

```
- displacement criteria are properties of the optimiser's last STEP, not of the point. A
  freq-only job takes no step, so they are irrelevant to stationarity and must not block a
  certificate. Reading rule, costs nothing.
- no numeric band for "reproduce". The measured floor is 4e-9; a middle threshold would be an
  invented constant. Rung 2 exists precisely so the ambiguous case is resolved by measurement
  rather than adjudicated by a made-up number. Costs nothing, and it is the right shape.
- per-row C-9 flag for P5: unchanged, one grep per row, same-quantity comparison.
```

## 4. Live sheet, final for the day
```
smoke, three decks                   ~0.3 core-h    code-path + anchor questions only
endpoint re-cert, rungs 1+2 one job  ~10.4          self-verifying; GATES u56_2.released
   rung 3, only after a human looks  ~42-66         not scheduled, not pre-run
16-thread packing validation         ~24            needs a payload change
P5 freq-only recovery, 17 rows       ~92-152        conditional on the acetone deck reaching P5
------------------------------------------------------------------------
whole remaining programme            ~127-247 core-h   = ~1% of guard
ceilings: P6 -1,782 (landed), U56-2 11-atom certs -384 (gated), 21-atom untouched
```

🔒 The day's transferable rules, both proposer8's, one extended by me:
```
- a rule cited by name is not a rule applied: a rule compressed to its CONCLUSION inverts
  easily. Cite the criterion, not the verdict.
- a mechanism being true does not make a criterion built on it well-formed. The mechanism
  licenses that the datum exists; only reading the file identifies WHICH datum it is.
- metadata describes a calculation; only the structure describes a molecule. Verify a
  qualification against the artefact, not only a disqualification.
- name the scaling variable and verify it moves as expected -- extended to sets: verify the
  set is UNIFORM in it.
```

# §R39.61 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: round reservation reconfirmed at 9,131.39; and `--rerun endpoint_prep_reactant` is the WRONG mechanism for the acetone re-certification

## 1. ✅ Reservation chain reconfirmed
```
11,297.39   returned round reservation (results/sei_probe_report.cpu.json)
 -1,782.00   P6 wall 24 -> 2 h                                        [MEASURED basis]
= 9,515.39
   -384.00   endpoint_prep_reactant_epsinf_full removed (bracket cancelled)
= 9,131.39   confirmed against coder12's figure
```

## 2. 🔴🔴 `--rerun endpoint_prep_reactant` executes rung 3, not the re-certification

The re-certification's price is **~10.4 core-h** (rungs 1+2 in one job, §R39.60), not the 65 core-h
single-arm figure carried forward from the cancelled design (A). But the mechanism matters more than
the number:

```
`--rerun endpoint_prep_reactant`  ->  runs endpoint_prep.sh  ->  rough + tight from the
                                      PACKAGED GUESS  ->  that is rung 3, skipping rungs 1 and 2
```
Two independent objections, and the second is the serious one:
```
COST      ~42-66 core-h instead of ~10.4
HAZARD    cold-starting from a packaged guess is the DOCUMENTED failure mode (C-9 / ADR-066),
          demonstrated in this project TODAY: §39.89's li_ec_radical_s0_L2 cold-started from a
          packaged planar seed and converged to 180.00 deg with heavy atoms coplanar to
          0.0000 A -- its own pre-registered falsifier. And the warm start PRESERVES BASIN
          IDENTITY, which is what U56-2 needs: the same chemical species on the new surface,
          not an independent search that may return a different minimum and silently change
          what the reaction is.
```
**`--rerun` remains the correct TRIGGER** — the existing marker predates spec digests, so it reads
`unknown` and skips, and only `--rerun` submits it. **What must change is the payload behind it.**

🔴 **§R39.47's Trap 1 recurring on a new item**: after the acetone rebuild the `pkg_fingerprint`
differs, so `sei_stage` rejects the stored stage markers and the rough stage re-runs regardless of
intent. **The ladder must be a payload with no rough stage in it at all — not a flag on
`endpoint_prep.sh`.** Identical 15× silent blow-up, identical fix, second occurrence.

## 3. Sizing: `endpoint_prep_reactant` KEEPS 384 / 6 h — deliberately the opposite of the product item

```
endpoint_prep_reactant   keep 384 / 6 h.  Rungs 1+2 need ~0.2 h wall, but rung 3's fallback is a
                         full cold rough+tight and needs the 6 h. Reserve for the WORST rung.
                         Ceiling is not scarce (9,131 of 21,000).
endpoint_prep_product    6 -> 3 h correct as applied. First-time cold certification, measured
                         wall 1.029 h, so 3 h is 2.9x headroom against a 1.43x measured spread.
endpoint_prep_rc_reactant  UNCHANGED at 1,536 / 24 h. No measurement exists for the 21-atom class.
```

## 4. §R39.47 re-based
```
DEAD    design (C) pair, 7.9-9.3 core-h                  already retired in §R39.56
DEAD    "both arms at the same thread count" (trap 2b)   no two arms; rungs 1+2 sharing one job
                                                         makes thread-count identity automatic
LIVE    trap 1: no rough stage in the payload            MORE relevant now, see §2
LIVE    trap 2a: declare cores_per_task explicitly       unchanged
LIVE    the 1e-9 SCF floor and the 4e-9 Cartesian-force  now LOAD-BEARING: they calibrate
        agreement, both measured from data on disk       rung 1's pass criterion
LIVE    kappa = 1.619, thread scaling, packing gain      unaffected
```

## 5. Residual on the physics-env guard, flagged not fixed

coder12 built it as a **key-set** comparison (which keys were present) rather than "all keys
required" — better than what I asked for: it covers detection failing (key disappears ⟹ `unknown`,
never `stale`) AND keeps working on clusters with no module system.

🟡 Residual: if detection returns a **different non-empty string** — a site module rename,
`gaussian/g16.c01.linda` → `gaussian/g16.c01` — the key set is unchanged and the value changed ⟹
`stale` ⟹ every item resubmits at once. That is a legitimate "different binary" signal and no string
comparison can separate it from a cosmetic rename, so **no fix requested.** The mitigation if it ever
bites is the blast-radius cap deferred in §R39.52 §2, and *"a site module rename caused one mass
resubmit"* is precisely the trigger to build it then. Recorded so the cause is known on the day
rather than diagnosed from scratch.

# §R39.62 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: 🔴🔴 TWO OF PROPOSER7'S THREE COST FACTORS ARE MEASURED ON CONVICTED GEOMETRIES — reproduced exactly from the stage costs, and the interaction term is the one with no replacement

proposer8's §39.98 convicts `ec_radical_anion_s0_L2` (0.82 eV above its own C1 seed) and
`li_ec_radical_s0_L2` (180.00°, heavy atoms coplanar to 0.0000 Å). I went to check which of my
numbers sit on those rows. **The answer is worse than the two rows.**

## 1. proposer7's §39.72 factors reproduced EXACTLY from the stage markers — then convicted

```
species (all level2)          stage core-h   point group   ratio vs ec_s0   proposer7's factor
ec_s0_L2                          8.84          C2V           1.00          (denominator)
li_ec_cation_s0_L2               24.94          C2V           2.82          "+1 Li+  x2.8"   ✓
ec_radical_anion_s0_L2           20.46          C2V           2.31          "+1 open x2.3"   ✓
li_ec_radical_s0_L2             134.06          C2V          15.16          "BOTH    x15.2"  ✓
```
All three reproduce proposer7's published factors to the quoted precision, from the stage markers
alone. **That confirms which rows the factors were built on — and every one of them is C2V.**

```
ec_s0_L2 (denominator)     C2V but CLEARED — 0.0060 eV above its own C1 seed (ec_s1_L2). Fine.
li_ec_cation_s0_L2         C2V, SINGLE SEED, never audited.        -> x2.8  UNVERIFIED
ec_radical_anion_s0_L2     C2V, CONVICTED by 0.82 eV (§39.98).     -> x2.3  ON A TRAPPED STRUCTURE
li_ec_radical_s0_L2        C2V, CONVICTED at 180.00 deg (§39.89).  -> x15.2 ON A TRAPPED STRUCTURE
```

🔴🔴 **Two of the three factors are measured on structures now convicted as symmetry-trapped, and
the third is unaudited. The ×15.2 interaction term is the one that retired the S₂₁ cube law
(§R39.41) and currently has NO replacement** — so the quantity standing in for a retracted cost
model is itself now suspect.

## 2. How wrong, and in which direction — bracketed, both ends biased

`ec_radical_anion` is the one convicted row with a converged C1 counterpart already on disk:
```
ec_radical_anion_s0_L2  (C2V, TRAPPED)     20.46 core-h   -> factor 2.31
ec_radical_anion_s1_L2  (C1,  CORRECT)    110.33 core-h   -> factor 12.48
```
**The open-shell factor is 2.3 or 12.5 depending on which structure you measure — 5.4×.** And this is
exactly proposer7's §39.72(2) "×5.4 seed spread" for this species. **It was never variance. It is one
seed being trapped and the other not.**

🔴 **Both endpoints are biased and neither is the answer:**
```
2.31  measured on a trapped structure -> too LOW (the optimiser converged into a symmetry
      constraint instead of searching the real surface)
12.48 measured on the correct structure but from a seed that also started further from the
      minimum -> contaminated UPWARD by conformer distance, which §39.72(2) established is
      what opt cost actually tracks
```
**True factor bracketed [2.3, 12.5], 5.4× wide, and the bracket is not a confidence interval — both
ends are known-biased point estimates.** No number in that range is currently defensible.

## 3. 🔴 The planning consequence I have to withdraw

§R39.45 and prior sections carried proposer7's advice, which I endorsed, to **extend ADR-087's
no-pooling rule to seeds-within-a-species** — treating the ×5.4 spread as a distribution to be
propagated into `N₁ = min(600, remaining/(u_measured × r_composite))`.

**That is wrong and I am withdrawing my endorsement.** The spread is not a property of the cost of
computing a species; it is the cost difference between converging to the right structure and
converging into a trap. **Propagating it as uncertainty models an artefact of a missing `nosymm`
keyword as if it were physics** — and it would inflate every sizing estimate that consumes it.

**Correct handling**: exclude convicted seeds first, THEN look at whether a spread remains. Once
`nosymm` is fixed on P5's decks, the residual spread is the real conformer-quality effect and is the
thing worth pooling rules about.

## 4. Where the remaining free audit actually applies — 4 rows, not 17

proposer8 is right that the energy/point-group tiers did most of the audit for free. Enumerating the
17 converged rows by what is left to learn:

```
genuinely symmetric molecules (symmetry is real chemistry, a priori not traps)
    c2h4 D2H, co2 D*H x2, h2o C2V, pf6_anion OH                          5 rows, no audit needed
already C1 (nothing to be trapped in)
    ch3o_radical_s1, ec_radical_anion_s1, ec_s1                          3 rows
already convicted or cleared for free by a second seed
    ec_radical_anion_s0 (convicted), li_ec_radical_s0 (convicted),
    ec_s0_L2 (cleared 0.006 eV), ch3o_radical_s0 (cleared 0.006 eV),
    ec_s0_L1 (covered by its L2 counterpart)                             5 rows
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AUDIT-RELEVANT RESIDUE: symmetric, single-seed, unaudited
    emc_s0_L2           CS   NBasis 404   Hessian ~28.1 core-h
    emc_s0_L1           CS   NBasis 340   Hessian ~17.9
    li_ec_cation_s0_L2  C2V  NBasis 321   Hessian ~11.3   <- 🔴 see below
    hco3_anion_s0_L2    CS   NBasis 174   Hessian  ~1.1
                                          -------
                                          ~58.4 core-h of the ~118 recovery
```
🟢 **The audit is still free** — all four are in the recovery anyway for the `u_cheap` denominator.
Its **scope** shrank from 17 rows to 4, exactly as proposer8 said; the cost did not change.

🔴 **`li_ec_cation_s0_L2` is the one to look at first**, and not because of its price. It is C2V,
single-seed, a **Li complex** (the U-55 floppy-PES class), and it is the closest structural analogue
to `li_ec_radical_s0_L2`, which proposer8 convicted at 180.00°. Strong prior that it is trapped too —
**and it is the sole basis for the ×2.8 Li⁺ factor.** If it falls, all three of proposer7's factors
are on trapped or unaudited ground.

## 5. Accepted from §39.99, with the framing corrected

🟢 **The duplicate Hessian is a measurement, not overhead — accepted, and it improves my own number's
standing.** I priced escalation as "discards rung 1's Hessian (~2.3 core-h)". Wrong framing: letting
step 2's `calcfc` recompute it makes the two Hessians an **independent repeat of the same quantity in
the same job**, whose deviation is the in-job reproducibility floor for this species at this basis.
That is the same control proposer8 made me price at +11 core-h as a third `Link1` step on the (now
cancelled) level2 control — **here it arrives free, because the ladder already computes both.**
⟹ **~10.4 core-h stands, and none of it is waste.** `readfc` refused for what it costs in
information, not on risk grounds — same job, same checkpoint, no `chk_handoff` copy, so the failure
mode that forced the handoff fix cannot occur.

🟢 **Rung 3's prescription changes but its PRICE does not**, and the reason is worth recording: the
endpoint chain's deck **already carries `nosymm`** (`#p nosymm wB97XD/gen ...`, verified in
`endpoint_tight.gjf`). **Only P5's 22 decks lack it.** So §39.98(d)'s C1-perturbed prescription costs
the endpoint nothing extra — the perturbation is free and the keyword is already there. **~42–66
core-h stands for rung 3.**

# §R39.63 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: NO OBJECTION to the cold path for Round A — my C-9 warning is refuted by a controlled comparison already on disk, which I had read and not opened

coder12 asked for my objection on record before lead decides between running
`--rerun endpoint_prep_reactant` cold today (~42–66 core-h) and building the ladder payload first
(~10.4 core-h, ~2 h of coder time on G16 paths this package has never exercised).

**No objection. Ship cold today.** The reasoning below is against my own §R39.61 position.

## 1. 🔴 My C-9 objection is REFUTED — and by data I had already read

§R39.61 argued that a cold start re-exposes the endpoint to the symmetry-trap failure mode
demonstrated today on `li_ec_radical_s0_L2` (180.00°, heavy atoms coplanar to 0.0000 Å). coder12
replied that `endpoint_prep.sh` carries defenses P5's decks lack. **They are right, and the proof is
a controlled comparison sitting in this round's own artefacts:**

```
SAME SPECIES, [Li(EC)]0 reduced radical, SAME planar-seed pathology, TWO payloads:

P5 deck             #p wB97XD/gen ... opt freq       no nosymm, no C-9 kick
                    -> converged 180.00 deg, heavy atoms coplanar 0.0000 A. TRAPPED (§39.89)

endpoint_prep.sh    #p nosymm ... opt=(loose)  AND  #p nosymm ... opt=(tight,calcfc) freq
                    perturbation_provenance.json:  applied: true
                      before: max_out_of_plane 0.000000 A, is_coplanar TRUE   <- the identical
                                                                                 pathology
                      kick 0.25 A, seed 1, max displacement 0.23583 A
                      after:  max_out_of_plane 0.205795 A, is_coplanar FALSE
                    -> converged 129.41 deg, against an experimental reference of ~138(2) deg.
                       ESCAPED.
```
**The endpoint's packaged seed had exactly the same defect — perfectly coplanar heavy atoms — and the
payload detected it, kicked it out of plane, and converged to a chemically sensible structure.** The
cold path's C-9 exposure is not merely "weaker"; it is measured, on this species, this round, and it
held.

🔒 **Third time today, same error shape, and it is the rule proposer8 gave me.** I cited
`perturbation_provenance.json` as *present* in §R39.45's file listing and never opened it. **Metadata
describes a calculation; only the artefact describes what happened.** I broke that rule within hours
of adopting it, on the exact question it governs.

🟡 One accuracy correction to coder12's list, in their favour on three of four: `nosymm` (both
stages), the C-9 out-of-plane kick, and the F1 symmetric fingerprint all **fired** this round. The
dual-start defense did **not** engage — `start_selection.json` shows `n_starts: 1, selected:
packaged`. So it is three demonstrated defenses plus one that was available and idle.

## 2. The cost argument is coder12's too, and consistency requires me to say so

~50 extra core-h is 0.24% of the guard. **I have argued all day that at this scale cost is not a
decision variable** (§R39.60 declined to optimise a 4.5-vs-12.5 core-h ladder for exactly this
reason). It would be incoherent to now spend a round's latency to save 50 core-h.

And the schedule argument runs the other way from where I had it: the ladder needs `%oldchk` and
`--Link1--`, **neither of which this package has ever emitted** — I flagged that myself in §R39.49.
**A new payload failing on first use costs a round, which is the currency I have called scarce all
day.** Round A on a proven payload is the lower-variance choice.

## 3. What the cold path genuinely loses, and why none of it blocks

```
LOST  rung 1's gradient-invariance measurement (is grad-E unchanged at the stored geometry
      across generic -> acetone). Mitigated: the smoke's PCM-block diff answers the anchor
      question anyway, and the cold path's converged geometry compared against the stored one
      is a DIRECT structural answer rather than a gradient proxy -- arguably better.
LOST  the duplicate-Hessian in-job reproducibility floor (§39.99). It was a bonus, not a
      requirement.
LOST  ~5.9 core-h of information-per-core-h efficiency. Immaterial.
```

## 4. 🔴 One free condition, and it is a reading rule not a build

**The cold path's failure mode is CONFOUNDED and that must be stated before the run, not after.**
If the cold re-certification's converged geometry disagrees with the stored 18.5 geometry by covalent
graph, there are two causes and this design cannot separate them:
```
(a) the surface moved (generic -> acetone)          <- the finding we would want
(b) a second cold start landed in a different basin <- an artefact of cold-starting twice
```
A warm start would have excluded (b) by construction. So:

> **If the graph check fails, do NOT conclude the surface moved.** Record it as `indeterminate,
> cause: cold-start basin confound`, and resolve it with a warm start from `endpoint_tight.chk`
> (~10.4 core-h, the ladder, which is being built for Round B anyway).

Costs nothing, preserves the finding if it happens, and prevents a payload artefact being published
as a solvent-model result. Precedent is direct: §39.42(a) measured 5/6 kick seeds landing in one GFN2
basin at 21 atoms, and §39.41 has a 0.59 eV two-basin case — cold starts landing in different basins
is a measured behaviour of this project, not a hypothetical.

🟢 Probability is low: the 18.5 arm's cold start already produced a clean graph and a sensible angle
at 11 atoms with the kick applied. **Worst case if it fires: ~42–66 spent, then ~10.4 for the ladder
= ~76 against ~10.4.** Still under 0.4% of the guard.

## 5. Recorded position

```
Round A            run `--rerun endpoint_prep_reactant` COLD, today.   ~42-66 core-h
                   NO OBJECTION from compute-cost or from C-9 exposure.
                   ONE condition: the confound reading rule in §4, free.
Round B            build `endpoint_recert.sh` (the ladder) as planned -- product and rc
                   endpoints need it regardless, and it becomes the disambiguator if §4 fires.
```

**Reported to**: coder12 and team-lead.

# §R39.64 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: 🔴🔴 MY `p = 2.2` SCALING EXPONENT IS INVALID — its two calibration points differ in symmetry as well as basis. Plus the factor re-measurement priced.

proposer8's §39.100 says symmetric rows are cheap by roughly the point-group order. I went to check
which of my anchors carry symmetry. **The one that matters most does, and it invalidates a
calibration I have been quoting all afternoon.**

## 1. The defect

```
P6 anchor (my NBasis-321 calibration point)   deck has NO `nosymm`
                                              log: Full point group C2V
                                              Framework group C2V[C2(COLi),SGV(C2O2),X(H4)]
                                              171.7 s / 25 SCF cycles = 6.87 s/cycle
endpoint (my NBasis-173 point)                deck HAS `nosymm`, C-9 kick applied
                                              log: Full point group C1
                                              ~1.75 s/cycle (BACKED OUT, not measured directly)
```
I computed `p = ln(6.87/1.75) / ln(321/173) = 2.21` and attributed the entire ratio to basis size.
**One point exploits C2V symmetry and the other cannot. A third variable moved and I did not check
it** — the scaling-variable rule, pointed at my own anchor, for the fourth time today.

## 2. How bad — the exponent is not uncertain, it is UNCONSTRAINED by my data

```
if C2V buys |G| =    P6 nosymm-equivalent   ratio vs endpoint   implied p
             1            6.87 s/cycle            3.93            2.21   <- what I quoted
             2           13.74                    7.85            3.33
             4           27.48                   15.70            4.45
             8           54.96                   31.41            5.58
```
proposer8's own measurements (`ec` 4.38×, `ch3o_radical` 2.07×, n = 2, contaminated by seed distance)
put the saving somewhere in 2–5×, so **`|G| = 1` — the only value under which my exponent is correct —
is the one value the available evidence argues against.**

🔴 **A two-point calibration with two moving variables determines nothing.** The honest statement is
not "p is 2.2 ± something"; it is **"p is unconstrained by the data I have."**

Second softness, stated because it compounds: the endpoint's 1.75 s/cycle was **derived**, not
measured — I subtracted an assumed Hessian cost (~127 s) from step 1's 233.1 s covering 48 SCF cycles
plus a `CalcFC` Hessian plus ~4 gradients. Both sides of the calibration are soft.

## 3. What this damages, and what it does NOT

```
🔴 DAMAGED — everything built on the exponent
   the P5 per-species Hessian table (§R39.48)
   the P5 frequency-only recovery estimate:
        17 converged rows at p=2.2 ->  92 core-h
                            p=3.0 -> 152
                            p=4.46 -> 396      <- 4.3x the number I have been quoting
   the ec_radical_anion / hco3_anion / level2-control Hessian estimates (all now retired anyway)
   ⟹ these are biased LOW, in the dangerous direction: we would size assuming cheaper
     Hessians than the fixed nosymm decks will deliver.

🟢 NOT DAMAGED — direct measurements with no scaling step
   the endpoint's 2.27 core-h Hessian and 65.87 core-h job (measured, nosymm, no extrapolation)
   the 17/5 P5 convergence split (a count, not a cost)
   kappa = 1.619 -- SAME job both sides (P6 anchor, cluster vs dev box), symmetry CANCELS
   the 2.45x 16-vs-64-thread packing gain -- same job both sides, symmetry CANCELS
   proposer7's x2.8 / x2.3 / x15.2 -- C2V / C2V, symmetry CANCELS (proposer8's point, confirmed;
     they remain broken by the TRAP, which is a different and better-defined defect)
```
🟢 The table's **ordering** survives — NBasis ranking is robust to the exponent. "Four species carry
most of the cost" stands; the absolute core-h do not.

## 4. 🟢 The fix is ~15 core-h and it rides the round already being submitted

```
probe A   the P6 anchor deck, UNCHANGED, plus `nosymm`.  sp, 11 atoms, NBasis 321, 64 threads.
          measured symmetric cost 3.05 core-h -> expect ~6-15 with symmetry off
probe B   the same sp at NBasis 173 (the endpoint's level3 basis), also `nosymm`, same species,
          same thread count.                                        ~0.6-3 core-h
TOTAL     ~15 core-h  [MEASURED basis, upper end]
```
This is a **two-point, single-variable** calibration: same species, same job type, same thread count,
same symmetry setting, only the basis differs. It replaces an exponent that currently determines
nothing.

🟢 **And probe A doubles as the direct |G| measurement proposer8's §39.100 hypothesis needs** — the
same deck with and without `nosymm` on a real system, with no seed-distance contamination, because
the geometry is identical. Their n = 2 ratios are contaminated by seed distance and cannot separate
the two effects; this one can, and it costs ~12 core-h more than a number nobody currently trusts.

**Payoff**: ~15 core-h to make a table valid that currently prices an item at anywhere from 92 to
396 core-h. **The uncertainty it removes is 4.3× on the largest remaining item in the programme.**

## 5. The factor re-measurement proposer8 asked me to price

Spec (§39.100(5)): cost(species) ÷ cost(ec), both on correct structures, comparable starting
displacements, `nosymm`, four species, displacement reported.

```
species             status                                         opt-only core-h @64 threads

ec_radical_anion    MEASURED C1 seed already on disk (s1)               110.33   [MEASURED]
li_ec_cation        no C1 seed -> symmetric 24.94 x (4.0-5.4)        100 - 135   [ESTIMATE]
li_ec_radical       no C1 seed -> symmetric 134.06 x (4.0-5.4)       536 - 724   [ESTIMATE]

🔴 **`li_ec_radical` alone is 65–72% of the bill.** It is also the species carrying ×15.2, the

# §R39.65 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: `P5_freq_recovery` item-shaped sizing for coder12 — and DO NOT use a freq/opt ratio

## 1. 🔴 First, the shape question: a freq/opt ratio is the wrong instrument

coder12 asks what freq/opt ratio to apply per size class. **None. The ratio does not exist as a
stable quantity, and using one would repeat the atom-count error in a third disguise.**

```
opt cost  =  (number of Berny cycles) x (cost per cycle)     -- cycles vary 4x+ with seed quality
freq cost =  ONE Hessian + CPHF over 3N perturbations        -- independent of how many cycles
                                                                the optimisation happened to take
```
`li_ec_radical_s0_L2` cost 134.06 core-h of optimisation because it took many cycles. Its Hessian is
one Hessian. `h2o_s0_L2` cost 1.53 core-h of optimisation. Their opt costs differ 88×; their Hessian
costs differ by roughly (321/74)^p × (33/9), which is a different number entirely. **A freq/opt ratio
would propagate seed quality into a quantity that does not depend on it.**

Correct basis: **NBasis for the integral/derivative work, 3N for the CPHF work**, anchored on the one
directly measured Hessian (2.27 core-h, NBasis 173, 3N = 33, `nosymm`, C1, 64 threads).

🟡 And to be explicit about coder12's "7 core-h freq of 65 total": that 7.02 is the **tight STAGE**
(tight optimisation + freq). The freq alone was **2.27** core-h from G16's own `Elapsed time` on the
`Link1` step. The 7.02 figure is the right one for a stage budget and the wrong one for a Hessian
anchor.

## 2. `P5_freq_recovery` — per-row `task_budgets`, sized as a CEILING not an estimate

Budget = `Hessian(p = 4.46) × 1.5 + 1.66` overhead, floored at 6.4 core-h (0.1 h × 64 cores).
**Deliberately sized at the pessimistic exponent** — §R39.64 leaves `p` unconstrained between 2.2 and
~4.5, and a reservation must be safely above the truth, not centred on it. The `p = 2.2` column is
shown only so the spread is visible.

```

🔴 **`emc_s0_L2` is 32% of the item on its own.** If the item ever needs cutting, that is the row —
and it is one of only four rows carrying residual C-9 audit value (§R39.62), so cutting it costs
audit scope, not just cost.

🟡 The `nosymm` requirement coder12 names is already priced in: the stored geometries are symmetric
(C2V/CS for most rows), so a `nosymm` Hessian on them costs the point-group factor more than the
original symmetric run did. That is exactly what the `p = 4.46` branch represents, and it is why I am
sizing there rather than at `p = 2.6`.

## 3. `cores_per_task`: declare **64**, and the reason is comparability, not trap 2a

coder12 is right to ask, and I need to correct a possible misreading of my own trap 2a. **Trap 2a
asked for the value to be DECLARED, not for it to be SMALL.** The hazard was a site default silently
changing the sizing; the fix is an explicit number.

**Declare `cores_per_task = 64`, matching P5 round 1.** Not 16, and here is the trade:
```
16 threads   saves ~60% of the item's core-h (the measured 2.45x packing gain)
             BUT u_opt was measured at 64 threads in round 1. u_cheap = u_opt + u_freq would then
             be assembled from TWO thread configurations -- a total no single configuration would
             ever produce. That is §39.61(c)'s assembled-provenance problem, and u_cheap is the
             ITEM'S ENTIRE DELIVERABLE (§39.78: it is what B1's sizing rule consumes).
64 threads   costs ~240 core-h more than 16 would
             BUT both halves share one cost basis and u_cheap means what it says
```
**Answer to coder12's question: yes, declaring 16 WOULD break comparability, and the deliverable is
the comparability.** Pay the 240 core-h.

🟢 **The clean path exists and it is one round out**: run the ~24 core-h 16-thread validation
(§R39.64), and if it confirms the 2.45×, run *future* P5 rounds entirely at 16 threads — both halves,
one basis, comparable within themselves. **Never mix the halves; switch a whole round at a time.**

## 4. Answering the ladder-consumer question: fold them, build rung 1 only

```
rung 1 mechanism  freq from a stored geometry
                  CONSUMER: P5_freq_recovery -- 17 rows, needed regardless. BUILD IT.
rung 2 mechanism  warm-started opt+freq from a stored checkpoint
                  CONSUMER: only the disambiguator if Round A's covalent-graph check fails
                  (§R39.63's reading rule). MAY NEVER FIRE. DO NOT BUILD YET.
endpoint_prep_product / rc_reactant
                  never certified under any solvent -> they need the FULL cold path, not the
                  ladder. They are not consumers of either mechanism.
```
⟹ **Yes: only P5 needs rung 1. Fold the two into one `freq_from_stored_geometry` mechanism and stop
there.** Same call as "rung 3 must not be pre-run", one level up: build the mechanism that has a
consumer today, and let the one whose trigger may never fire wait for its trigger.

🟡 Boundary: whether the ladder as a *method* survives is proposer8's ruling, not mine. My answer is
only that **rung 2's mechanism has no consumer this round**, so its build cost is speculative. If
Round A's graph check fires, it becomes urgent and is ~2 h of work then.

# §R39.66 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: the reuse and the 16-thread saving are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — and re-running everything is cheaper AND removes proposer8's own caveat

proposer8's §39.102 rules: reuse the two measured C1 rows, replicate P5's `s1` protocol (0.1 Å kick,
level2, default grid) for the two missing species, and — separately — require **all four factor
species at the same thread count**, since these runs produce geometries and energies, not just
timings.

**Those two requirements collide, and following the second one all the way out inverts the first.**

## 1. The collision

The two reusable rows were measured at **64 threads**. So:
```
(A) reuse the two + run two new, ALL AT 64 THREADS      set uniform at 64  ✓
(B) run all four at 16 THREADS                          set uniform at 16  ✓
                                                        but discards the two measured rows
```
Both satisfy uniformity. proposer8 preferred (A) on the reasonable ground that re-running a 110
core-h measurement for hygiene buys nothing. **But the 2.45× packing gain applies to the WHOLE set,
including `li_ec_radical`, which is 65–72% of the bill — so (B) is cheaper despite the re-runs.**

## 2. Priced, using the three measured `s1`/`s0` ratios as the scaling basis

```
measured s1/s0 ratios (kick, no nosymm):  ec 4.38, ec_radical_anion 5.39, ch3o_radical 2.07
                                          range 2.07 - 5.39   [MEASURED, n=3]

(A) reuse two + two new, all at 64 threads
    li_ec_cation    24.94 x (2.07-5.39)  =    52 -   134 core-h
    li_ec_radical  134.06 x (2.07-5.39)  =   277 -   723
    NEW SPEND                                329 -   857 core-h

(B) all four at 16 threads, production 0.25 A amplitude
    all four at 64-thread equivalent          478 - 1,006
    / 2.45 packing gain                       195 -   411
    + the 16-thread validation                       24
    TOTAL                                     219 -   435 core-h

    (B) is cheaper by                         110 -   423 core-h
```
**(B) wins at both ends of the range, including the cost of the validation that makes it legal.**

## 3. 🟢 And (B) removes a caveat proposer8 said could only be removed by measuring twice

§39.102's stated weakness: the factors would be measured at a 0.1 Å kick on the old deck, and
transfer to the 0.25 Å production protocol is an assumption — **weakest for the floppy Li complexes,
which are exactly the species carrying ×2.8 and ×15.2.** proposer8 noted removing it "means measuring
at both amplitudes."

**Under (B) nothing is reused, so there is no old protocol to match.** Run all four at the
**production** 0.25 Å amplitude and the transfer assumption never arises — one amplitude, the one
that matters. The caveat is not mitigated, it is **absent**.

⟹ **(B) is cheaper, satisfies uniformity, AND is scientifically cleaner than (A).** That is unusual
enough to be worth stating plainly rather than presenting as a cost preference.

## 4. Recommendation, decision-ready

```
1. run the 16-thread packing validation FIRST          ~24 core-h  (already lead-approved)
2. if it confirms ~2.45x  -> option (B): all four species, 16 threads, 0.25 A production
                            amplitude, uniform set.               ~195-411 core-h
3. if it does NOT confirm -> option (A): reuse the two measured rows, replicate the s1
                            protocol at 64 threads for the two missing species, and carry
                            proposer8's amplitude caveat as written. ~329-857 core-h
```
The validation is a genuine branch point, not a formality: it decides a ~110–423 core-h difference
AND whether a stated caveat exists. **Its leverage has now been counted twice today** (§R39.64 for
this item, §R39.65 for the P5 recovery's future rounds) — it is the highest-value 24 core-h on the
board by a wide margin.

🔴 **Under (B), the discarded rows are not wasted.** `ec_s1_L2` (38.74) and `ec_radical_anion_s1_L2`
(110.33) remain the ONLY measurements of these species at 64 threads and become the cross-check for
the packing gain at production scale — a second, free confirmation of the 2.45× on real workloads
rather than on a single `sp` anchor. Record them as retained, not superseded.

## 5. Probe A's scope boundary — accepted and recorded here so it cannot be misquoted later

proposer8 separates the symmetry saving into (a) reduced symmetry-unique integral/SCF work and
(b) fewer optimiser degrees of freedom. Probe A is an `sp`: **no optimiser, so it measures (a) only.**

```
🟢 (a) alone is EXACTLY the right scope for the P5 recovery — freq-only at a fixed geometry, so
   (b) is identically zero there. Probe A fully determines the correction to the 92-396 range.
🔴 (a) alone is a LOWER BOUND for optimisation costs — the factors, wave-1 sizing — where (b) is
   live. proposer8's 4.38x / 2.07x measured (a)+(b) together WITH seed-distance contamination;
   probe A measures (a) cleanly; NEITHER gives (b).
🔴 NOBODY may quote probe A's number as "the symmetry correction for an optimisation" -- and the
   person most likely to do it is me, three sections from now, having forgotten which one it was.
```

## 6. Attribution correction carried from §39.102

My §R39.63 and §R39.64 both attributed the P5 trap to the missing `nosymm` keyword. **proposer8's
seed-file evidence shows the true root cause is `amplitude_ang: 0.0` — no kick.** Every P5 `s1` row
escaped *without* `nosymm`, because G16 detects the point group of the INPUT geometry and a perturbed
seed is detected as C1, leaving no group to enforce. Both mitigations stay; **the attribution in my
sections was wrong and this is the correction.**

🟢 One consequence in my favour that I should not overclaim: this does **not** change §R39.64's
conclusion that my `p = 2.2` exponent is invalid. The P6 anchor was an *unperturbed idealised guess*
detected as C2V and run without `nosymm` — it had neither mitigation, so it enjoyed the symmetry
saving whatever the root cause is named.

**Reported to**: proposer8 and team-lead.

proposer8's §39.104 accepts (B) and correctly demolishes my claim that the two retained 64-thread

arithmetic for the same shape. **It is there, in the number I used to win the argument.**

# §R39.68 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: probe AC accepted; the calibration becomes ONE job of five steps; and a seventh instance — this one a self-contradiction inside my own document

## 1. 🔴 Probe B moved three variables — accepted, and the fix pays twice

proposer8's §39.106 is right. My "one variable at a time" set was three-quarters one variable at a
time:
```
probe 0    C2V, default grid, NBasis 321      MEASURED 3.05 core-h   <- the only baseline
probe A    probe 0 + nosymm                    one variable   OK
probe C    probe 0 + UltraFine                 one variable   OK
probe B    NBasis 173, nosymm, UltraFine       THREE variables from probe 0   ✗
```
Probe B is one variable from a point that **does not exist**. As designed, the basis exponent would
emerge only by first assuming symmetry and grid are separable and dividing them out — **the exact
assumption this project has already falsified.** ×2.8 × ×2.3 predicted ×6.4; the measurement was
×15.2, a ~2.4× interaction, and that is why the cube law was retracted. **Our largest cost surprise
to date is a failure of factors to multiply**, and I was about to build the replacement calibration
on the assumption that they do.

```
probe AC   NBasis 321, nosymm, UltraFine
   (1) gives probe B a real baseline: B - AC differs by BASIS ALONE, so the exponent is a
       measurement rather than a residue after two divisions
   (2) tests separability for free: predicted AC = probe0 x (A/probe0) x (C/probe0)
       vs measured AC. Agreement -> factors multiply here and may be used independently later.
       Disagreement -> the interaction is found BEFORE it is embedded in a sizing rule.
```
🟢 proposer8's framing is the one to keep: **the extra probe is the only one of the five that can
fail.** The other four return numbers; AC returns a verdict.

## 2. The calibration should be ONE job of five `Link1` steps

```
step 1  probe 0    C2V, default grid, NBasis 321          3.05  RE-RUN, see below
step 2  probe A    + nosymm                                6-15
step 3  probe C    + UltraFine                             4- 6
step 4  probe AC   + nosymm + UltraFine                    8-31
step 5  probe B    NBasis 173, nosymm, UltraFine           1- 8
---------------------------------------------------------------
                                             TOTAL       ~22-63 core-h, ONE submission
```
🟡 Wider than proposer8's ~17–39 because I carry |G| = 2–8 and grid = 1.3–2.0 rather than their
narrower central values. Not a disagreement — a wider prior on two factors nobody has measured yet.

**Re-run probe 0 inside the job rather than reusing the P6 anchor's 3.05.** It costs 3.05 core-h and
buys same-node, same-build, same-thread comparability across all five points — the identical argument
proposer8 used for the one-job rungs and for the same-thread-count constraint on the factor species.
A baseline measured in a different job and a different build is the seventh moving variable.

🔴 **One deck constraint or the calibration is corrupted in the cheap direction: NO `guess=read`
between steps.** Each probe must converge its SCF independently. If a later step inherits an earlier
step's density, it is fast for a reason that has nothing to do with the variable being measured, and
every factor after step 1 comes out too small. Same shape as §R39.49's `%chk` collision, one level
down: **shared state between steps that are supposed to be independent.** Give each step its own
`%chk` or none, and do not carry a guess.

## 3. 🔴 Seventh instance, mine — and this one is a self-contradiction inside this document

proposer8 corrects my justification for the `ec`-at-both-thread-counts measurement. I called the
2.45× anchor's C2V a "known contaminant". **§R39.64 §3 of this same document says the opposite, and
it is right:**

> "the 2.45x 16-vs-64-thread packing gain — same job both sides, symmetry CANCELS"

Then §R39.67, three sections later, called C2V "a known contaminant" of that same number. **I
established the correct fact and then quoted the wrong version of it.** Different shape from the
previous six — not a comparison across an unenumerated difference, but proposer8's *"cite the
criterion, not the verdict"* failure applied to my own writing. A conclusion I had derived became a
slogan I reused without re-deriving.

🟢 **The correct justification, which is stronger**: the anchor is an `sp`, and the gain is being
applied to **optimisations** — many SCF cycles, gradient steps, checkpoint I/O, a different parallel
profile entirely. **The workload shape is the first-order limitation; the symmetry is second-order at
most** (the work *distribution* can shift with fewer unique integrals, so not exactly zero, but not
the leading term). The ~50–78 core-h measurement is right; **buy it because the anchor is the wrong
workload, not because it had symmetry on.**

## 4. The pattern, in proposer8's formulation — the most useful thing produced today

> **A number that decides a comparison gets the least scrutiny precisely because it is the output of
> the reasoning rather than an input to it. Inputs get checked; conclusions get used.**

The sixth instance appeared in the number used to win the argument. The seventh appeared in a
conclusion I had correctly derived and then re-quoted. **The only mechanical defence that has worked
today is enumerating what differs BEFORE dividing** — not afterwards, and not when the ratio looks
surprising. All seven looked entirely reasonable at the time.

factor re-measurement, 4 species (B)    ~254-821
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

# §R39.69 — engineer9, 2026-08-21: eighth instance accepted — the calibration probes become `freq`, ~36–146 core-h, and they retire a question that contaminates the packing measurement too

proposer8's §39.107: **probe 0 is an `sp`, and four of the five numbers the calibration exists to
produce are Hessian corrections.** Verified from the deck myself before repricing:
`jobs/P6_t*/anchor.gjf` = `#p wB97XD/gen scrf=(pcm,solvent=generic,read) sp`; `anchor.log` has zero
`Frequencies --` lines and one `SCF Done`. **The workload-shape objection I raised against the 2.45×
anchor two messages ago was sitting inside my own replacement design.** Eighth instance, mine,
accepted without reservation.

## 1. Why it is not a technicality — the two factors have different mechanisms in the two workloads

```
SYMMETRY  in an `sp`   reduces symmetry-unique two-electron integrals.               ONE saving.
          in a `freq`  does that AND collapses the 3N nuclear perturbations to the
                       symmetry-unique subset.                                       TWO savings.
   => an sp-measured symmetry factor is a LOWER BOUND for the Hessian one, so the P5 recovery
      correction it feeds would still be biased LOW -- the same dangerous direction, arrived at
      through the calibration built to fix it.

GRID      wB97XD is range-separated with 100% long-range exact exchange, which never touches the
          integration grid. The grid affects XC quadrature only, and the XC FRACTION of total cost
          differs between an SCF and the CPHF/XC-second-derivative work in a frequency.
   => the grid factor need not transfer either, and its DIRECTION cannot be settled by argument.
```

## 2. Repriced as five `freq` probes, one job

Built from the two anchors that exist, not from a factor chain: the measured Hessian
(2.27 core-h, NBasis 173, nosymm/C1, UltraFine, 64 threads) and the measured cold SCF
(3.05 core-h, NBasis 321, C2V, default grid, 64 threads).

```
probe                            core-h        what it isolates
AC (321 nosymm UltraFine)      14.9 -  61.1    baseline for B; separability verdict
A  (321 nosymm default)        10.5 -  52.6    GRID factor (vs AC)
C  (321 C2V    UltraFine)       3.2 -  12.2    SYMMETRY factor (vs AC)
0  (321 C2V    default)         3.1 -  10.1    re-measured baseline, in-job
B  (173 nosymm UltraFine)       2.6 -   8.5    BASIS exponent (vs AC, one variable)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOTAL, one job, one submission  36.1 - 146.1 core-h   (was ~22-63 as `sp` probes)
```
The spread is wide because the Hessian symmetry saving admits **|G| to |G|²** — symmetry both reduces
each solve and reduces the number of perturbations — and nobody has measured which. **That width is
the reason to run the probes, not a defect in the estimate.**

## 3. 🟢 The bonus proposer8 identified is the part that justifies the increase

A `freq` job must converge its SCF first, and this project already separates those two numbers in
the endpoint log (Hessian/CPHF 2.27, SCF component measured separately). So **each probe returns
three quantities, not one**:
```
the SCF-component factor       (what the sp probes would have measured)
the Hessian-component factor   (what the factors are actually APPLIED to)
their RATIO                    <- nobody holds this, and it decides whether an `sp` anchor may
                                  EVER stand in for a Hessian again -- including for the 2.45x
                                  packing question
```
⟹ one set of five `freq` probes **replaces the five `sp` probes and makes a separate
`sp`-versus-Hessian study unnecessary.** The increase from ~22–63 to ~36–146 buys a question retired,
not more data.

**Justification in one line, and it is proposer8's**: four of the five numbers this calibration
exists to produce are Hessian corrections, and **an `sp` probe cannot produce one.**

## 4. 🔴 What these probes deliberately do NOT answer, and why that is correct

**Hessian thread-scaling is not measured by this set** — all five run at 64 threads. That is a gap,
and it should stay one:
```
the P5 recovery runs at 64 threads by ruling (§R39.65: u_cheap's two halves must share a basis),
so its thread scaling does not affect anything this round.
IF a future round switches P5 to 16 threads, THAT is when to measure it -- running probe AC at both
thread counts, +15-60 core-h.
```
Building it now would be paying for an answer to a question no current item asks. Same call as
"rung 2 has no consumer yet" and "rung 3 must not be pre-run".

## 5. Accepted, unchanged

```
- no `guess=read` between steps. 🟡 proposer8's addendum is right and belongs in the record: the
  BASIS probe necessarily gets a different initial guess because its basis differs. That is
  inherent to the comparison, not a defect -- but it must be stated, or a later reader will
  "fix" it.
- probe 0 re-run in-job rather than reusing the P6 anchor's 3.05.
- my wider priors over proposer8's narrower ones, since nobody has measured either.
```

## 6. On the seventh instance being a different animal

proposer8's diagnosis is worth keeping because it names a limit on this document's usefulness:
**a conclusion correctly derived, then re-quoted in its wrong form. No new reasoning was involved to
go wrong — only recall.** ⟹ **a document is not a defence against this class: the correct statement
was on the page and the wrong one got written anyway.**

The defence that scales: **when a prior conclusion is about to carry weight, re-derive it in one line
rather than recall it. A re-derivation that takes longer than a line was never a slogan to begin
with.** Applied here: "symmetry cancels in the 2.45×" re-derives as *same job, both sides, ratio* —
one line, and it would have caught §R39.67 before it was written.

calibration, five `freq` probes, one job  36-146         was 22-63 as `sp`; retires the
                                                          sp-vs-Hessian question as well
clean packing measurement (`ec`)          50- 78         optimisation thread-scaling
P5_freq_recovery (17 rows)              652 reserved / ~92-424 expected
factor re-measurement, 4 species (B)     254-821

# §R39.74 — engineer10, 2026-08-21: NO Link-number SCF-vs-Hessian classification exists anywhere in this project's record — §39.108(c)(1)'s premise traced and corrected, two real options given to coder13

coder13 (picking up P5_freq_recovery from coder12) asked for the exact G16 Link-number set used to
split `u_freq` into an SCF component and a Hessian/CPHF component, citing §39.108(c)(1): *"engineer9
already does exactly this on the endpoint job ('Hessian/CPHF 2.27 core-h, SCF 0.6'), ... free — both
timings are in the same log."* Traced every citation of that 2.27 figure across §R39.47/§R39.65/
§R39.69 before answering rather than guessing a Link mapping. **The premise does not hold as
literally stated — no Link-number classification exists, and no standalone freq-only job's log has
ever actually been decomposed into SCF vs Hessian.**

## 1. What "2.27 / SCF component" actually are — two different, neither a Link-level split

```
"2.27 core-h Hessian/CPHF"    = §R39.47 §1: G16's OWN "step 2 (freq, Link1)" elapsed time, WHOLE.
   [MEASURED]                   This is a REAL, free split -- but it is G16's automatic internal-
                                 job-step boundary for a COMBINED `opt ... freq` route (opt=step1,
                                 freq=step2), i.e. an OPT-vs-FREQ split, not an SCF-vs-Hessian split
                                 WITHIN the freq step. Step 2's own 1-cycle SCF (it inherits a
                                 converged density in-job, no guess=read needed) is bundled into the
                                 2.27 uncounted, because it is cheap enough not to matter there.

"SCF re-convergence 0.04-0.71" = §R39.47 §1-2: NOT measured from any freq-only job's log (none
   [ESTIMATE]                    existed yet). Backed out by SUBTRACTION: step 1's 233.1 s covered
                                 48 SCF cycles + one CalcFC Hessian + ~4 gradients; subtracting an
                                 assumed Hessian cost and dividing by 48 gives ~1.5-2 s/cycle, then
                                 multiplied by an ASSUMED 1-19 cycle range for how a FRESH job
                                 restarting cold from a checkpoint might behave. A rate estimate
                                 extrapolated across a different stage, not a component measured in
                                 the same job/log the Hessian number came from.

(a THIRD, unrelated number also floats around: the calibration's "cold SCF" anchor, 3.05 core-h,
 is P6's own `sp` smoke job at NBasis=321/C2V/default-grid -- a totally different molecule/basis/
 symmetry/grid than the 173-NBasis endpoint Hessian. §R39.69 already flags this cross-job mismatch
 as a real limitation, which is WHY the 5-probe calibration exists.)
```

**⟹ §39.108(c)(1) conflates a real, free G16-native split (opt-step vs freq-step) with an SCF-vs-
Hessian split inside one freq step that was never actually measured that way.** Not proposer9's
fault specifically — it is a re-quote of my own predecessor's numbers, same "correct fact, wrong
recall" shape as §R39.68 §3 caught in this same document. Flagging back to proposer9 since it's
their spec item's premise, not just coder13's question.

## 2. Two real options for coder13 — building a Link-number classifier from scratch is NOT recommended

Recommend against inventing a Link-number rule: no G16 reference for it exists in this project's
record, nobody has verified which Links belong to which phase for THIS route/version, and a wrong
classification would silently poison a number whose whole purpose is comparability.

```
OPTION A (default, FREE) -- record each row's raw TOTAL u_freq only (already what's being built).
  Rely on the 5-probe calibration (§R39.69, already in flight, 36-146 core-h) for the SCF-fraction
  question -- it is a REAL matched sp-vs-freq subtraction (probe 0 = sp baseline vs probes A/C/AC/B
  = freq, same geometry/basis per probe) at CONTROLLED conditions, which is exactly what a per-row
  split would need and P5's rows individually cannot cheaply provide. Apply the probes' ratio to
  each row's total as an ESTIMATE if a split is ever needed downstream -- never invent one per row.

OPTION B (MEASURED, small extra cost, only if a true PER-ROW split is actually required) -- one
  extra matched `sp` job per row, SAME geometry/basis/symmetry as that row's freq recovery job;
  Hessian_row = freq_total_row - sp_total_row. Real per-row measurement, no Link parsing.
  ROUGH COST: 17 extra small `sp` jobs. Using the P6 sp anchor (3.05 core-h at NBasis 321) scaled by
  each row's own NBasis (74-404, §R39.65's table) with the SAME unconstrained p=2.2-4.46 bracket
  already carried for this recovery: roughly 0.05-3.5 core-h/row depending on size, **~5-40 core-h
  total for all 17** [ESTIMATE, order-of-magnitude only -- ask if you want the row-by-row table
  priced properly before committing to option B].
```

**Recommendation: ship option A now** (zero extra cost, doesn't block anything already in flight);
revisit option B only if the calibration probes' ratio-based estimate turns out to be insufficient
for whatever downstream use needs the per-row split — that is proposer9's call, not a build default.

**Reported to**: coder13 (direct), proposer9 (premise correction — their §39.108(c)(1)), team-lead.
